stories.title: Fernando Alonso delays his 2027 decision as Aston Martin bets a car upgrade will keep him — with Alpine still circling
stories.what_happened: Fernando Alonso confirmed he still has no firm decision or timeline on whether he will race for Aston Martin in 2027, saying he wants to properly evaluate the team's progress before committing. Aston Martin's design chief Adrian Newey said he is 'pretty confident' the relationship will continue, and is pinning hopes on a significantly revamped car — with a major aerodynamic overhaul and weight-saving changes — arriving around the **Hungarian Grand Prix** to make the case Alonso should stay. Speculation has also intensified that Alonso could instead join Alpine, where his old ally Flavio Briatore is now team principal, potentially replacing Franco Colapinto; Briatore says Alonso is 'quite happy' where he is, without ruling anything out. Alonso himself has pushed back hard on some of the noise, calling persistent negativity about Aston Martin 'borderline abuse' earlier this season.
key_points: Alonso, whose Aston Martin contract expires at the end of **2026**, says he'll decide his future **after the summer break**.
Design chief **Adrian Newey** is banking on a revamped car — with an **aerodynamic overhaul and weight-saving push** — debuting around the Hungarian GP to convince him to stay.
Alonso has publicly shut down some Alpine talk, calling negativity around Aston Martin '**borderline abuse**.'
Alpine boss **Flavio Briatore**, Alonso's long-time associate, says Alonso is '**quite happy**' at Aston Martin — but hasn't fully killed the rumour.
At **44**, Alonso has said he wants to end his F1 career on a high, not on a low note.

depth.background: Fernando Alonso is a two-time world champion and, at 44, the oldest driver on the current F1 grid. He joined Aston Martin in 2023 on the promise the team — backed by billionaire owner **Lawrence Stroll** and legendary designer **Adrian Newey** — would become a genuine title contender, but the team has struggled to deliver a competitive car through 2026. Speculation has grown that Alonso could instead reunite with **Flavio Briatore**, his former Renault team boss and mentor, who now runs the Alpine team where Alonso won both his championships nearly two decades ago.

stories.title: Tens of thousands in Indiana enter a second week without power after a deadly storm
stories.what_happened: Beginning **August 11**, a powerful storm system dropped more than **11 inches of rain** on parts of Indiana over three days, causing record flooding and knocking down large numbers of trees and power lines. As of **August 21**, tens of thousands of residents are entering their **second week without electricity**, with some describing day nine as 'survival mode.' The prolonged outages have forced school closures: Gary's district, serving about **4,300 students**, shut down on **August 13**, just weeks into its school year, and remains closed through at least today, while Portage Township Schools — which had to cancel its planned August 12 opening — now doesn't expect to resume classes until **August 25**. Local officials say the delay in restoring power comes from ongoing safety hazards: downed trees across properties and infrastructure damage crews still need to clear and repair before lines can be safely re-energized. Businesses in affected areas have also been unable to reopen.
key_points: A storm dumped more than **11 inches of rain** over three days starting **August 11**, triggering record floods and toppling trees onto power lines.
Some residents are now on their **ninth straight day** without electricity, describing conditions as 'survival mode.'
Gary's school district, serving about **4,300 students**, has been closed since **August 13** and remains shut through at least today.
Portage Township Schools, forced to cancel its Aug 12 start, now aims to reopen on **August 25**.
Officials blame the drawn-out outages on ongoing **downed trees and property damage** crews still have to clear.

depth.background: Indiana sits in the US Midwest, a region increasingly hit by intense, fast-moving storms that dump extreme rainfall in short bursts — a pattern many climate scientists tie to a warmer atmosphere holding more moisture. When a storm's winds and rain bring down large numbers of trees onto power lines across a wide area at once, utility crews can't just flip a switch: they often have to clear debris and rebuild sections of the wire network street by street, which is why outages after severe storms can stretch past a week even in a wealthy country with a modern grid.

stories.title: China rejects Trump's demand to join the 'economic D-Day' campaign against Iran
stories.what_happened: China's foreign ministry publicly rejected Washington's request to join or support the new sanctions campaign. Spokesman Lin Jian said **sanctions and pressure tactics 'are not the solution'** to the underlying dispute, and that 'military force and pressure tactics will only lead to escalation that serves no one's interests.' Beijing instead called for a political and diplomatic resolution between Iran and the US. The rebuff came the same day Iran's foreign ministry warned that any official who orders or carries out the new US sanctions could face prosecution — a largely symbolic but pointed signal of defiance. Bessent had directly named China days earlier as the key holdout whose cooperation the sanctions campaign needs to actually bite.
key_points: China's foreign ministry spokesman **Lin Jian** said sanctions and pressure tactics are 'not the solution' to the Iran standoff.
Beijing called instead for a **'political and diplomatic approach'** and dialogue between Tehran and Washington.
Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** had urged China — Iran's biggest oil customer — to 'get with the program' on sanctions.
Analysts note the **US has little real leverage** over Beijing, which buys the bulk of Iran's sanctioned oil exports.
Iran's own foreign ministry separately warned that officials who **order or enforce the new US levies are liable to prosecution**.

depth.background: On Wednesday, President Trump declared what he called an 'economic D-Day' against Iran — a sweeping sanctions push meant to cut off the country's remaining trade lifelines after the two nations' recent military confrontation. The campaign leans heavily on pressuring third countries, especially **China**, which has continued buying discounted Iranian crude oil despite years of US sanctions, keeping Iran's economy afloat. Treasury Secretary Bessent has been the public face of the push, calling it potentially 'the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world.' China has historically shrugged off US secondary sanctions threats tied to Iran, treating its energy relationship with Tehran as a matter of sovereign trade policy.

thread.changed: China — Iran's largest oil customer — has now publicly refused to join the campaign, calling sanctions 'not the solution,' exposing the biggest gap in Washington's isolation strategy.

stories.title: Hamilton's brand-new Ferrari chassis flops in its debut, deepening his title-bid crisis
stories.what_happened: Hamilton's new chassis made its debut in Friday's Sprint Qualifying at Zandvoort — and struggled. He qualified seventh, more than six-tenths of a second off Russell's pole time, and over half a second slower than teammate Charles Leclerc, who took third. The result came just after Hamilton had publicly urged Ferrari to 'apply pressure' on championship leader Antonelli ahead of the session — instead, it was Hamilton's own car that fell short. Antonelli, meanwhile, struggled too (sliding into the gravel in SQ1) but still out-qualified Hamilton by finishing fifth. Ferrari now heads into Saturday's Sprint race and Sunday's Grand Prix needing to find real pace from the new chassis fast, with the championship gap to Antonelli unchanged at 50 points.
key_points: Ferrari built Hamilton an **all-new chassis** specifically for Zandvoort to reboot his championship push.
In its first outing, Hamilton qualified only **7th** for the Sprint — **six-tenths of a second off pole**.
He finished **over half a second behind** his former teammate Charles Leclerc's sister Ferrari.
Hamilton trails championship leader **Kimi Antonelli by 50 points** with the season more than half over.
Hamilton himself had urged Ferrari to **'apply pressure'** on Antonelli just before this session — the opposite happened.

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton joined Ferrari for the 2025 season chasing the elusive eighth world title that eluded him at Mercedes, but his first two seasons with the Italian team have been marked by inconsistency rather than the dominance many expected. Ferrari had already been publicly warned about 'sloppy' mistakes threatening its title push this season, and the team responded by fast-tracking a completely new chassis for Hamilton specifically for this Zandvoort weekend — a significant mid-season resource commitment meant to close the 50-point gap to Antonelli.

thread.previously: We reported that Ferrari was fast-tracking an all-new chassis for Hamilton specifically for the Dutch Grand Prix, as part of an escalating push to save his title challenge.
thread.changed: The new chassis debuted in Friday's Sprint Qualifying and underwhelmed — Hamilton qualified only 7th, over half a second slower than teammate Leclerc, with the 50-point gap to Antonelli untouched.

stories.title: George Russell snatches a surprise sprint pole at Zandvoort as Antonelli slides into the gravel
stories.what_happened: In a tightly-fought Sprint Qualifying session, **George Russell** set the fastest time — a 1:11.567 — to claim a surprise pole position for Saturday's Sprint race, beating Lando Norris by four-tenths of a second. Charles Leclerc was third and Oscar Piastri fourth, with barely a tenth of a second covering the top four cars. Championship leader Antonelli endured a scrappy session, sliding off into the gravel during SQ1 and ultimately settling for fifth, about two-tenths off his teammate Russell's pace. Max Verstappen, racing at his emotional final home Grand Prix, qualified sixth. Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari — freshly fitted with an all-new chassis specifically built for this race — could only manage seventh, more than six-tenths off Russell and over half a second behind his old teammate Leclerc's sister car.
key_points: **George Russell** topped Sprint Qualifying with a **1:11.567**, **0.41 seconds** clear of Lando Norris.
Championship leader **Kimi Antonelli** could only manage **5th** after sliding off into the gravel during SQ1.
**Lewis Hamilton's** upgraded Ferrari struggled to **7th**, over half a second off the pace.
The top four — Russell, Norris, Leclerc, Piastri — were separated by **less than a tenth of a second**.
It's the **first-ever Formula 1 Sprint** held at Zandvoort, in the circuit's **final scheduled season** on the calendar.

depth.background: Zandvoort's Dutch Grand Prix returned to the F1 calendar in 2021 after a 36-year absence, drawing enormous 'Orange Army' crowds for local hero Max Verstappen, but 2026 marks its last scheduled appearance before the track drops off the calendar. This weekend also introduces the Sprint format to Zandvoort for the first time — a shortened Saturday race worth extra championship points, preceded by a separate Sprint Qualifying session on Friday instead of the usual second practice. Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes' 19-year-old sensation, arrived with a commanding 50-point championship lead over Lewis Hamilton after winning six of the season's first eleven races.

stories.title: Australia drops out-of-form opener Weatherald, recalls Renshaw after historic Darwin upset
stories.what_happened: Australia named their squad and XI for the second Test against Bangladesh, to be played at **Harrup Park in Mackay**, starting **Saturday, August 22** at 10am local time. Opening batter **Jake Weatherald** was dropped after **six Tests** without the runs selectors wanted, with **Matthew Renshaw** recalled to open alongside Travis Head. Captain Pat Cummins confirmed the rest of the XI — including Steve Smith, Marnus Labuschagne, Cameron Green, Alex Carey, Josh Inglis, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Scott Boland, Beau Webster, and spinner Nathan Lyon — stays unchanged from the Darwin loss. Mackay becomes the **12th** Australian venue ever to host a Test match.
key_points: Australia **dropped Jake Weatherald** after **six underwhelming Tests**, recalling **Matthew Renshaw** to open with Travis Head
The change follows Australia's **first-ever home Test defeat to Bangladesh** — a stunning 9-wicket loss in Darwin
Captain **Pat Cummins** confirmed the rest of the XI is **unchanged** for the Mackay Test
The match is at **Harrup Park**, Mackay's **first-ever** Test venue — the **12th** Australian ground to host a Test
Spinner **Nathan Lyon**, under selection scrutiny, was **retained** despite a recent lean patch

depth.background: Bangladesh stunned Australia in the first Test of the series in **Darwin**, winning by **9 wickets** to claim their **first-ever Test win on Australian soil** in just their **third attempt** there and their first Test in the country in **23 years** — one of the biggest upsets in recent Test cricket, made more remarkable given Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 in a warm-up match the week before. That result has put Australia's team and selectors under real pressure heading into the second Test, since a team that dominates at home rarely gets beaten by a side seen as one of the weaker Test nations.

stories.title: India and UK hold 25th defence talks, deepen R&D ties under the 'Vision 2035' roadmap
stories.what_happened: India's Defence Secretary **Rajesh Kumar Singh** and the UK's Permanent Under Secretary for Defence co-chaired the 25th India-UK Defence Consultative Group meeting on **August 21**. The two sides reviewed progress on defence-industrial R&D through the **India-UK Vision 2035** initiative and their joint **Ten-Year Defence Industrial Roadmap**, and agreed to widen military-to-military cooperation through more joint exercises, training, and capacity-building between the two armed forces.
key_points: India and the UK held their **25th Defence Consultative Group** meeting — a bilateral dialogue running for decades
Talks centred on **defence-industrial R&D cooperation** under the **India-UK Vision 2035** framework
Both sides agreed to expand **joint military exercises and training**
The meeting sits alongside a shared **Ten-Year Defence Industrial Roadmap** the two countries are building together

depth.background: A **Defence Consultative Group (DCG)** is a recurring, senior-official-level dialogue between two countries' defence ministries meant to keep military cooperation on track between the bigger political summits — India and the UK have run theirs for many years, and this was the **25th edition**. It comes as India has spent this same week signing or reviewing defence and security arrangements with **Japan** and **Singapore** too, part of a broader pattern of India spreading its defence and technology partnerships across several countries rather than leaning on any single one.

stories.title: Ravindra Jadeja and coach Gautam Gambhir share a laugh in Colombo — months after Jadeja defied his orders in India's worst Test defeat
stories.what_happened: Returning to India's Test set-up for the first time since the Guwahati defeat, Ravindra Jadeja was filmed sharing a light-hearted moment with Gautam Gambhir during a training session in Colombo, playfully imitating Kuldeep Yadav's bowling action while the coach looked on and smiled. The moment is notable because it comes months after reports that the pair had clashed: in the second Test against South Africa in Guwahati, with India chasing an unlikely **549** on the final day, Gambhir reportedly ordered the batting line-up to play purely defensively, but Jadeja played his natural attacking game regardless, top-scoring with **54 off 87 balls** including four fours and two sixes. India were bowled out for just 140, losing by **408 runs** — a result so damaging that 'Sack Gambhir' trended on Indian social media in its aftermath. The public, friendly exchange in Colombo suggests any tension between the two has eased as India look to close out the Sri Lanka series 2-0.
key_points: Jadeja and head coach Gautam Gambhir were seen sharing a **light-hearted moment** at training in Colombo, mimicking Kuldeep Yadav's bowling action.
It's Jadeja's **first India appearance since a tense Test loss to South Africa in Guwahati** earlier this year.
In that match, India collapsed to **140 all out chasing 549**, losing by **408 runs** — reportedly after Jadeja ignored Gambhir's order to bat purely defensively.
Jadeja top-scored in that innings with **54 off 87 balls**, the only Indian batter to show real intent.
'**Sack Gambhir**' trended on social media after the Guwahati defeat, with the coach facing heavy public criticism.

depth.background: Gautam Gambhir was appointed India's head coach in mid-2024, succeeding Rahul Dravid, and has developed a reputation as an intense, sometimes combative presence around the team. Ravindra Jadeja is one of India's most experienced all-rounders and had reportedly clashed with Gambhir's instructions during India's home Test series loss to South Africa, when India collapsed for 140 chasing an improbable 549 on the final day in **Guwahati** — their heaviest home Test defeat in years, which triggered fierce public criticism of Gambhir's methods.

stories.title: Kuldeep Yadav and KL Rahul skip Colombo training as his place in India's XI hangs by a thread
stories.what_happened: With India already 1-0 up after their 165-run win in Galle, attention has shifted to the second Test in Colombo starting **August 23**, where India's team combination is reportedly in flux. Both Kuldeep Yadav and senior batter **KL Rahul** were absent from the team's first training session in Colombo, with the reason for their absence not disclosed by the team management. The timing has fueled speculation given reports already circulating that India are considering dropping Kuldeep for uncapped spinner **Saransh Jain** after his modest Galle numbers. India's spin-bowling coach, **Sairaj Bahutule**, has pushed back on the concern publicly, saying Kuldeep 'remains in good form' and backing him to be part of the XI. The team is due to finalise its playing eleven in the coming days before the Test begins.
key_points: Kuldeep Yadav and **KL Rahul** both missed India's first training session in Colombo, with **no reason disclosed**.
Kuldeep bowled **25 overs for just one wicket** in the first Test at Galle, which India still won by **165 runs**.
Uncapped spinner **Saransh Jain** is reportedly in line to debut in Kuldeep's place for the second Test.
India's spin-bowling coach **Sairaj Bahutule** has publicly backed Kuldeep, saying he remains 'in good form' despite the numbers.
The second Test starts **August 23** at the SSC ground in Colombo, with India already 1-0 up in the series.

depth.background: India won the first Test of this series against Sri Lanka at Galle by **165 runs**, but the win papered over a shaky bowling performance from frontline spinner Kuldeep Yadav, who managed only **one wicket from 25 overs** while uncapped debutant Manav Suthar ran through Sri Lanka's batting for a ten-wicket match haul. India have historically leaned on Kuldeep as a genuine wicket-taking spin option in home and subcontinent conditions, so a poor outing raises real selection questions heading into the second Test.

thread.previously: We reported India were considering dropping Kuldeep Yadav for the 2nd Test in Colombo after an underwhelming first Test, with uncapped spinner Saransh Jain in line to debut.
thread.changed: Kuldeep and senior batter KL Rahul both missed India's first training session in Colombo, with no reason given, adding fresh uncertainty just two days before the Test — even as the team's spin coach publicly backed Kuldeep to keep his place.

stories.title: Hardik Pandya trade drama widens: seven IPL teams are circling Mumbai's captain — and MI now denies it's even happening
stories.what_happened: Reports over the past week say seven of the IPL's ten franchises — most prominently Kolkata Knight Riders, Chennai Super Kings, Delhi Capitals, Lucknow Super Giants and Rajasthan Royals — have made early enquiries about trading for Hardik Pandya ahead of the 2027 season, with KKR the reported frontrunner and reportedly willing to offer him the captaincy. But Mumbai Indians pushed back directly, with an insider telling reporters 'nothing is happening' and that no franchise had actually approached them. CSK's CEO Kasi Viswanath issued a similar denial about his own team's interest. The renewed speculation follows Mumbai Indians' ninth-place finish in IPL 2026, Pandya's second season as captain, which reopened questions about whether the franchise needs a leadership reset.
key_points: **Seven of the ten IPL franchises** — reportedly including KKR, CSK, Delhi Capitals, LSG and Rajasthan Royals — have made preliminary enquiries about trading for Hardik Pandya ahead of IPL 2027.
**KKR** is seen as the frontrunner, reportedly willing to hand Pandya the **captaincy** if a trade goes through.
A Mumbai Indians insider pushed back hard: **'Nothing is happening... No one has approached us, and we haven't spoken to anyone.'**
CSK's own CEO **Kasi Viswanath** separately denied his team's interest, calling the Pandya-to-Chennai chatter **'untrue.'**
Speculation intensified after **Mumbai Indians finished ninth** in IPL 2026 under Pandya's captaincy, reviving reset talk.

depth.background: Hardik Pandya has captained Mumbai Indians since 2024, when he took over the leadership from Rohit Sharma in a move that split fan opinion at the time. Since then, MI's results under Pandya have been inconsistent, and each disappointing season reopens speculation about his future. The **IPL trade window** is different from the league's annual open auction: it's a private negotiation between two franchises over a player still under contract, and it can only go through with that player's own consent.

thread.previously: We reported Hardik Pandya was closing in on a move to KKR, with the captaincy attached, as speculation built around a trade ahead of IPL 2027.
thread.changed: The rumor mill has widened to seven franchises circling Pandya, but Mumbai Indians and CSK have now both explicitly denied that any real trade talks are underway — the story is far less settled than it looked.

stories.title: India orders telcos to strictly enforce the 9-SIM-per-person limit from August 24
stories.what_happened: The Department of Telecommunications has told telecom operators to **strictly enforce** the existing cap on SIM cards per customer — **9 nationally**, **6** in Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and the North-Eastern states — starting **August 24, 2026**. Under the new process, operators must check the DoT's centralized **Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP)**, which aggregates subscriber records from every operator, before issuing a new SIM to see whether an applicant has already hit their limit; from **August 23** the platform will also show a representative photo of the subscriber to help with identity verification. If a connection is activated beyond the limit — even for a single day — it must be **suspended immediately** until the issue is resolved. Operators have until **November 30** to fully align their internal systems with the DIP.
key_points: From **August 24**, telecom operators must actively check and block customers trying to exceed India's legal SIM-card limit.
The limit has stood since **2012**: a maximum of **9 mobile connections per person** nationwide, and **6** in Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and the North-East.
Operators must use the government's **Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP)**, which pools subscriber data across every telecom company to spot repeat offenders.
From **August 23**, DIP will even surface a subscriber's photo to help operators verify identity before issuing a new SIM.
Any connection activated over the limit must be **suspended immediately** until resolved; full technical compliance is due by **November 30**.

depth.background: Indian law has capped how many mobile connections one person can hold since **2012**, largely as a fraud- and crime-prevention measure — SIM cards bought in bulk, often on fake or stolen identities, are a common tool for phone scams, OTP fraud and other cybercrime in India. Enforcement has historically been patchy because no single telecom operator could see how many SIMs a customer already held with *rival* operators. The government's Department of Telecommunications has been building the Sanchar Saathi citizen platform and its underlying Digital Intelligence Platform specifically to close that gap by giving every operator a shared, real-time view across the whole industry.

stories.title: England seamer Kate Cross announces retirement after being left out of the T20 World Cup squad
stories.what_happened: Cross confirmed that the current season will be her last as a professional cricketer, ending a career that brought her 102 international caps and 140 wickets for England across Tests, ODIs and T20Is, plus 239 wickets for Lancashire across all formats. Her career highlight came on Test debut in Perth in 2014, where she took match figures of 6-70 to help England successfully defend the Ashes in Australia. In 2024 she reached the milestone of 400 career wickets across First-Class, List A and T20 cricket, and climbed to a career-high world No. 2 in the ICC's ODI bowling rankings. The announcement follows her being left out of England's squad for the 2026 T20 World Cup and losing her central contract at the end of last summer — she said she'd felt she 'wasn't good enough' to continue after that setback. In her own words: 'This summer is going to be my last playing professional cricket. It's incredibly hard to imagine ever saying goodbye to playing the sport that has been such a huge part of my life and shaped me into the person I am today.'
key_points: **Kate Cross** will retire from professional cricket at the end of the 2026 season.
She made her England debut in **2013** and went on to win **102 caps** across all formats, taking **140 wickets**.
Her standout moment: **6 wickets in the match** on her Test debut in Perth, helping England retain the Ashes.
Cross was **left out of England's squad for the 2026 T20 World Cup** and lost her central contract last summer.
She said it's 'incredibly hard to imagine' saying goodbye to a sport that **'shaped me into the person I am today.'**

depth.background: Kate Cross made her senior county debut for Lancashire aged just 13 and became the first female player to enter the Lancashire Academy a year later, building a career that spanned well over a decade at the top of English women's cricket. She debuted for England in 2013 and delivered one of her career-defining performances on her Test debut in Perth in early 2014, where match figures of 6-70 helped England retain the Ashes on Australian soil. In recent years, though, she fell out of England's central contract list and, more recently, missed selection for the 2026 T20 World Cup squad — signs that her international career was drawing to a close even before Friday's announcement.

stories.title: Pakistan collapse to an innings defeat inside 3 days, piling more pressure on stand-in captain Salman Agha
stories.what_happened: England completed a crushing innings-and-103-run victory over Pakistan at Headingley, wrapping up the match in under three days. Pakistan collapsed twice: bowled out for **171** in their first innings, then **135** in their second, unable to survive even 38 overs the second time round. England had posted **366 for 8** in reply to Pakistan's first innings, with contributions from Harry Brook (91), Jordan Cox (73), Root (66) and Zak Crawley (51). **Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue** shared 16 wickets between them across the match — eight apiece — while Jofra Archer added three more scalps. The win is the joint-second fastest of Root's 66-Test captaincy reign, underlining just how one-sided the contest became. Pakistan now travel to Lord's for the second Test starting the following Thursday, with Agha's captaincy under fresh scrutiny after back-to-back batting collapses.
key_points: England won the 1st Test at Headingley by **an innings and 103 runs**, inside just three days.
Pakistan were bowled out twice — for **171 and then 135** — after England posted 366 for 8.
**Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue** took eight wickets each across the match; **Jofra Archer** chipped in with three more.
It's the **joint-second fastest win** of Joe Root's 66-match tenure as England Test captain.
Pakistan's stand-in captain **Salman Agha**, filling in for the injured Babar Azam, now faces mounting scrutiny.

depth.background: Pakistan arrived at Headingley already weakened, with regular captain Babar Azam ruled out with a hand injury and Salman Agha elevated to lead the side in his place. Agha's leadership had already come under the microscope after Pakistan's batting looked fragile on the rain-hit opening day, when England bowled them out cheaply first time round. England, under Joe Root's captaincy, have built a reputation this era for aggressive, fast-scoring 'Bazball' cricket that tends to bowl out fragile opposition batting line-ups quickly once on top.

thread.previously: We reported that Pakistan's batting collapse on the rain-hit opening day at Headingley — bowled out for 171 — had already put stand-in captain Salman Agha's leadership under scrutiny.
thread.changed: Pakistan collapsed again in their second innings, folding for 135 to lose by an innings and 103 runs inside three days — turning early concern about Agha's captaincy into a much bigger crisis heading into the Lord's Test.

stories.title: Charter plane crashes at a remote US military radar site in Alaska, killing all 8 aboard
stories.what_happened: A Cessna 441 charter aircraft departed Anchorage on Thursday bound for the Cape Newenham radar site and crashed just before reaching its destination, around 12:15 p.m. local time. All eight people aboard — two pilots and six passengers — were killed, according to the US military, which oversees the radar site. The charter, operated by Security Aviation, had been booked by the US Army Corps of Engineers, and two of the passengers killed were USACE employees traveling to the site for work. The crash site sits roughly 450 miles west of Anchorage, in one of the most remote parts of the state, complicating recovery and investigation efforts. No cause has been confirmed publicly as of Friday.
key_points: A charter Cessna 441 crashed near **Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site**, about **450 miles west of Anchorage**, killing all 8 people aboard.
The flight, chartered by the **US Army Corps of Engineers**, had two pilots and six passengers, including two USACE employees.
It crashed around **12:15 p.m. Thursday**, local time, shortly before reaching its destination, operated by charter company Security Aviation.
Cape Newenham is part of a network of remote radar sites that **tracks aircraft in Alaska's airspace and along its borders** — relevant to US homeland air defense.
The cause of the crash has **not yet been determined**; investigators are examining the wreckage in a remote, hard-to-reach location.

depth.background: Alaska's vast, sparsely populated interior is served by small charter aircraft for tasks ordinary infrastructure can't reach — ferrying engineers, contractors, and supplies to remote military and civilian sites. Cape Newenham is one of a chain of Cold War-era **Long Range Radar Sites** built to watch for aircraft approaching North America from the north and west, a role that has taken on new relevance amid heightened US vigilance around North Korean and Russian military activity. Small-plane crashes are a recurring hazard in Alaska given the terrain, weather, and reliance on short backcountry runways.

stories.title: India and Singapore hold 4th Ministerial Roundtable, deepening trade and tech ties
stories.what_happened: India's top economic and foreign-policy ministers — **Sitharaman, Jaishankar and Goyal** — travelled to Singapore for a three-day visit culminating in the **4th ISMR** on August 20, meeting Singapore's Deputy PM **Gan Kim Yong** and other senior ministers. The two sides discussed strengthening their **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**, with a specific focus on advanced manufacturing, digital cooperation, sustainability, and physical/digital connectivity. Alongside the ministerial talks, a **Business Roundtable** convened companies from both countries to explore new investment and Global Capability Centre opportunities.
key_points: Union Ministers **Nirmala Sitharaman (Finance)**, **S. Jaishankar (External Affairs)** and **Piyush Goyal (Commerce)** led India's delegation to the **4th India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable** in Singapore.
Singapore's side was led by **Deputy PM Gan Kim Yong**, alongside ministers covering security, foreign affairs, digital policy and finance.
Talks focused on deepening the countries' **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** — spanning **advanced manufacturing, digitalisation, sustainability and connectivity**.
A parallel **4th India-Singapore Business Roundtable** brought companies together to explore investment and **Global Capability Centre** opportunities.
Singapore is already one of India's **largest sources of foreign investment**; the roundtable aims to convert this dialogue into concrete deals.

depth.background: The **India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR)** is a periodic high-level dialogue format — this was its fourth edition — meant to fast-track cooperation between the two countries beyond routine diplomacy. Singapore has long served as a **financial and logistics gateway** connecting India to Southeast Asia and global capital markets, and hosts many multinational firms' regional headquarters and India-facing back offices known as **Global Capability Centres (GCCs)**.

stories.title: British Columbia's Bald Range wildfire: evacuation lifted for almost all of Summerland, but 150 structures are gone
stories.what_happened: The fire ignited on August 7 and within three hours had already burned **5,000 hectares**; by August 10 it covered 15,600 hectares, and the province declared a state of emergency ordering roughly 20,000 people out of Summerland and Peachland. An 80-year-old woman died attempting to evacuate the Meadow Valley area northwest of Summerland as the fire advanced. Over the following two weeks, roughly 500 firefighting personnel battled the blaze, which peaked at **22,693 hectares** by August 20. Preliminary estimates put the damage at about **150 structures** damaged or destroyed, with around 40 of those in Summerland proper and the rest scattered outside town — officials cautioned the count doesn't yet distinguish homes from sheds and outbuildings. Evacuation orders have now been lifted for roughly 90% of Summerland's properties, letting most residents return home even as some areas remain on alert.
key_points: The **Bald Range fire** broke out on **August 7** near Summerland, BC and exploded to **5,000 hectares within three hours**.
At its peak it forced roughly **20,000 people** to evacuate Summerland (pop. 12,000) and nearby Peachland (8,000), under a declared state of emergency.
An **80-year-old woman died** while trying to evacuate the Meadow Valley area — the fire's only reported fatality.
About **150 structures were damaged or destroyed**, roughly 40 of them in Summerland itself.
By August 20, evacuation orders were lifted for almost all of Summerland as the fire's growth slowed, though it has now burned **22,693 hectares** (about 227 sq km).

depth.background: British Columbia has faced increasingly severe wildfire seasons in recent years as hotter, drier summers linked to climate change extend the fire season and make blazes harder to control. The Bald Range fire started in rugged terrain near **Summerland**, a town of about 12,000 in the Okanagan Valley wine region, and grew explosively in its first days, prompting Prime Minister **Mark Carney** to put the Canadian military on standby to help provincial firefighting crews.

stories.title: Israel's top court unanimously strikes down the government's bid to shut down Army Radio
stories.what_happened: Israel's High Court of Justice ruled **unanimously** that the cabinet's decision to close Army Radio was unlawful, finding it was driven by an **'extraneous and improper consideration'** — specifically, that some ministers wanted the station gone because its content didn't align with their politics. The government had voted in December 2025 to shut the station by March 1, but the court had already frozen that closure pending its final ruling. Defense Minister Israel Katz, who led the closure push, called the verdict based on **'foreign and invalid judgment'** and said the court had placed its own view above that of **'elected government ministers, who unanimously believed there was no place for a civilian radio station with political content within the IDF.'** The ruling means Army Radio keeps broadcasting for now — a defeat for a government that has repeatedly clashed with Israel's judiciary over how far it can go in reshaping state institutions.
key_points: The High Court ruled the closure was based on an **'extraneous and improper consideration'** — that ministers disliked the station's coverage
The full cabinet had **unanimously** voted in **December 2025** to shut the 70-plus-year-old station by March 1
Defense Minister **Israel Katz** blasted the ruling, saying the court put its judgment **'above that of the elected government'**
It's the latest flashpoint in Israel's **judiciary-versus-government standoff** that has simmered since the 2023 judicial-overhaul push
Army Radio (**Galei Tzahal**) keeps broadcasting for now while the underlying legal fight continues

depth.background: Army Radio, or **Galei Tzahal**, is a unique Israeli institution: a station run by the military but staffed largely by civilian journalists, on air since **1950**. In December 2025 the Netanyahu cabinet unanimously voted to shut it down, with Defense Minister **Israel Katz** arguing a station carrying political commentary had no place inside the IDF's chain of command. Critics — including the station's own journalists and press-freedom groups — said the real motive was retaliation for coverage the government didn't like, pointing to years of friction between the coalition and outlets it sees as unsympathetic. The High Court had already frozen the closure with an interim order while it heard the case.

stories.title: A magnitude-6.7 earthquake shakes Peru's southern Andes, injuring at least two
stories.what_happened: A magnitude-6.7 earthquake struck Peru's southern Andes on Thursday afternoon, according to the **US Geological Survey (USGS)**. The epicenter was 38 kilometers northwest of the city of Upahuacho in Parinacochas province, at a depth of 66.7 kilometers. At least two people were injured, and the quake damaged homes, health centers, and schools in the affected area. Shaking was felt across a wide radius, including in the Ica and Arequipa regions of southern Peru.
key_points: The quake struck at **1 p.m. local time (18:00 GMT)** on Thursday.
It was centered **38 km northwest of Upahuacho**, in the Parinacochas province of the Ayacucho region.
At least **2 people were injured** and homes, health centers, and schools were damaged.
The quake had a depth of **66.7 km** and was felt as far away as Ica and Arequipa.
Peru sits on the **Pacific 'Ring of Fire'**, making quakes like this routine but never risk-free.

depth.background: Peru lies along the Pacific 'Ring of Fire,' a horseshoe-shaped zone circling the Pacific Ocean where most of the world's earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur, because it traces the edges of tectonic plates that are constantly grinding against each other. The Ayacucho region, in Peru's southern highlands, is largely rural and mountainous, with older adobe-and-brick construction that is especially vulnerable to shaking. Peru has a history of far more destructive quakes, including a 2007 magnitude-8.0 quake near Ica that killed hundreds, which is the scale authorities watch for whenever a strong tremor hits.

stories.title: US sanctions Hezbollah and brands it an Iranian proxy as Trump's 'economic D-Day' campaign takes its first concrete step
stories.what_happened: On August 20, the US Treasury imposed fresh sanctions on **Hezbollah**, the Iran-backed Lebanese militant group, and officially redesignated it as an **Iranian proxy** — a legal label that unlocks broader secondary sanctions on anyone who deals with it. Vice President JD Vance told reporters that economic pressure is now the administration's **primary lever** against Tehran, since further bombing has failed to end the war outright. The move came as the **USS George Washington** carrier strike group arrived in the region even as the **USS Abraham Lincoln**, which has been deployed for months, began heading home — a partial military drawdown running alongside the new economic push. Iran's foreign ministry immediately condemned the sanctions as **'unlawful,'** and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned it could deploy more destructive weapons if fighting resumes. Oil markets reacted: global crude climbed toward **$94 a barrel**, the highest level since late July, as traders priced in a longer Hormuz standoff.
key_points: The Trump administration imposed **new sanctions on Hezbollah** and formally redesignated it an **Iranian proxy**.
VP JD Vance called economic pressure the US's **'most effective tool'** against Iran, calling it a **'delicate dance.'**
Two US aircraft carriers are in motion: the **USS George Washington** arrived in the Middle East as the **USS Abraham Lincoln** heads home.
Global crude oil rose toward **$94 a barrel**, its highest since late July, as the Strait of Hormuz standoff drags on.
Iran's foreign ministry called the pressure campaign **'unlawful'**; the IRGC threatened more 'destructive' weapons if the war restarts.

depth.background: Since late February 2026, the US and Israel have waged an air war against Iran that culminated in the assassination of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, and Iran has responded by effectively **blockading the Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway that roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas passes through — with mines and attacks on tankers. With outright military escalation stalling and a negotiated end to the war elusive, Trump said this week he is pivoting back to the tool he used before the war: **economic strangulation of Iran's economy**, betting that months of bombing have already pushed Tehran toward a breaking point. Just yesterday, Trump declared an **'Economic D-Day'** against Iran, threatening to sanction any country that keeps doing business with it.

thread.previously: Yesterday Trump declared an 'Economic D-Day' against Iran, threatening to sanction any country that keeps trading with Tehran, as Washington pivoted from military strikes toward financial pressure.
thread.changed: Today that threat became action: the US sanctioned Hezbollah and formally tied it to Iran, VP Vance called economic pressure the 'most effective tool' available, and oil climbed toward $94 a barrel on the news.
