stories.title: Amit Shah chairs Southern Zonal Council as states press him on delimitation and water-sharing
stories.what_happened: Home Minister **Amit Shah** chaired the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting on **August 20, 2026**, in Tamil Nadu, bringing together chief ministers and senior ministers from the five southern states. The agenda centred on **inter-state river water disputes**, demands for greater **central tax devolution** (the share of nationally collected taxes states receive back), and simmering anxiety over the coming **delimitation** exercise. Shah used the platform to praise the region's economic contribution — from **IT and AI to space, pharmaceuticals and automobiles** — while state leaders pushed back on issues they say the Centre has been slow to resolve.
key_points: Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** chaired the **31st Southern Zonal Council** meeting on **August 20** in Kovalam/Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu.
Chief Ministers and senior leaders from **Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Kerala** attended, alongside Telangana's representation.
Southern leaders pressed for faster resolution of **inter-state river water-sharing disputes** and a fairer share of **central tax devolution**.
States also raised concerns about the upcoming **delimitation** exercise — the redrawing of Lok Sabha seats — fearing it could **cut the South's political weight** for controlling population growth.
Shah highlighted the South's outsized contribution to **IT, AI, space, pharma, and agriculture**, calling it a major national growth engine.

depth.background: **Zonal Councils** are statutory forums (five across India, grouping neighbouring states) created to let states thrash out inter-state disputes — water, boundaries, taxes — with the Union government as mediator, chaired on rotation by the Union Home Minister. The Southern Zonal Council covers **Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana** and nearby Union Territories. Delimitation and water-sharing are long-running sore points for the South: southern states industrialised earlier and controlled population growth more successfully than many northern states, which they fear will now be used against them if parliamentary seats are reallocated purely by current population.

stories.title: Modi says 1937 Vande Mataram edit 'sowed the seeds of Partition' — Congress says he's insulting Tagore
stories.what_happened: PM Narendra Modi said that 'important stanzas of Vande Mataram — its very soul — were removed' in 1937, and argued that this **'divisive mindset'** was part of what eventually 'sowed the seeds of Partition' — the 1947 split of British India into India and Pakistan. Congress hit back by pointing to the actual **CWC resolution of October 28, 1937**, which recommended only the first two stanzas for official use, a call made on Tagore's advice and endorsed by a cross-section of Congress leadership including Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Subhas Chandra Bose, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Govind Vallabh Pant, and Acharya Narendra Dev. Congress said Modi's framing effectively insults Tagore, who proposed the edit. Home Minister Amit Shah accused Congress of 'appeasement' politics that he said fed the two-nation theory — the ideological basis for Pakistan's creation — and BJP's Jairam Ramesh countered that the BJP's nationalism is 'fake.' The clash comes shortly after Parliament passed a law granting Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the National Anthem, and after all six stanzas were sung in the Lok Sabha for the first time as the Monsoon Session closed on August 13.
key_points: PM Modi said the **stanzas dropped from Vande Mataram in 1937** removed its 'very soul' and reflected a **'divisive mindset'** that helped cause Partition.
Congress cites the actual **1937 Congress Working Committee (CWC) resolution**, drafted on **Rabindranath Tagore's advice**, as the source of the two-stanza tradition.
That 1937 decision was endorsed by **Nehru, Sardar Patel, Subhas Chandra Bose, Maulana Azad** and others — not one faction.
Home Minister **Amit Shah** called Congress's stance **'anti-national'**; Congress's Jairam Ramesh called BJP's nationalism **'fake.'**
The row follows Parliament's recent move giving Vande Mataram the **same statutory protection as the National Anthem**.

depth.background: 'Vande Mataram' ('I bow to thee, Mother') is a 19th-century poem by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay that became a rallying song of India's independence movement, later adopted as the country's **National Song** (distinct from the National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'). Only the poem's first two stanzas are commonly recited in official settings — a practice that traces back to a **1937 Congress Working Committee resolution**, taken on the advice of Nobel laureate **Rabindranath Tagore**, because the later stanzas invoke the Hindu goddess **Durga** in ways some felt could alienate non-Hindu Indians in a national song meant to unite everyone against British rule.

stories.title: NFL owner and ex-US ambassador Woody Johnson buys into Lawrence Stroll's Aston Martin F1 team
stories.what_happened: Aston Martin's Formula 1 team announced that Robert Wood 'Woody' Johnson, the billionaire owner of the NFL's New York Jets, has acquired a minority stake in the team and joined its board of directors as vice chairman. The size of his stake was not disclosed. Team principal-owner Lawrence Stroll brought Johnson in specifically to help grow the team's commercial presence in the United States; the team stressed Johnson will have no role in daily operations. In a statement, Johnson said: **'During my time as US Ambassador to the United Kingdom, I have developed a deep appreciation for Aston Martin's rich history, as well as Lawrence Stroll's strategic vision.'** Johnson already owns a 43% stake in Premier League club Crystal Palace and is a major Trump donor.
key_points: **Robert 'Woody' Johnson**, owner of the **New York Jets**, acquired a **minority stake** in Aston Martin's F1 team.
He joins the team's **board as vice chairman**, but will **not** be involved in day-to-day management.
Johnson, 79, is a **Johnson & Johnson heir** and served as **US Ambassador to the UK from 2017-2021**.
He also owns a **43% stake in Crystal Palace** football club.
Team owner **Lawrence Stroll** brought him in to help drive the team's **commercial growth in the US market**.

depth.background: Aston Martin's F1 team is privately owned by a consortium led by billionaire Lawrence Stroll — it is a separate company from Aston Martin Lagonda, the publicly traded British luxury carmaker whose name and badge it licenses. F1's popularity in the United States has surged over the past several years, driven partly by the Netflix series 'Drive to Survive' and new US races, prompting a wave of American investors to buy stakes in F1 teams. Woody Johnson is a long-time Republican donor and was appointed US Ambassador to the United Kingdom by President Trump during his first term, giving him deep personal ties to Britain, where the Aston Martin team is based (Silverstone).

stories.title: FBI says a New York woman plotted to bomb the state Capitol for ISIS
stories.what_happened: The **FBI arrested Jessica Bowie, 35**, of Albany on Wednesday, accusing her of plotting an ISIS-inspired bombing of the **New York State Capitol** building. According to the Justice Department, an FBI informant communicated with Bowie from **July 16 through August 17**, during which she allegedly said she wanted to "target my state capitol," which she noted was less than two miles from her home. She is accused of surveilling the building from multiple vantage points and planning to disguise an explosive as a food delivery order. She was arrested after allegedly buying what she believed was a live explosive device from undercover agents. Prosecutors say she also discussed fleeing the country after the attack and later returning to carry out a second attack in **Times Square on New Year's Eve**. She is charged with **attempting to provide material support to a foreign terrorist organization**.
key_points: **Jessica Bowie, 35**, of Albany was charged with attempting to provide material support to **ISIS**
She allegedly planned to disguise a bomb as a **food delivery** and detonate it at the New York State Capitol
An FBI informant messaged with her from **July 16 to August 17**, and she was arrested **Wednesday** after buying what she believed was a real explosive device
She reportedly pledged allegiance to ISIS in **May 2026** after converting to Islam five years ago
Prosecutors say she also floated a follow-up attack in **Times Square on New Year's Eve**

depth.background: The **Islamic State (ISIS)**, though militarily defeated as a territorial "caliphate" in Syria and Iraq years ago, still radicalizes people online and encourages so-called "lone wolf" attacks in Western countries — people with no direct contact with ISIS fighters who plan attacks on their own after being inspired by propaganda. US federal law enforcement runs regular **sting operations**, where undercover agents or informants pose as fellow extremists online to identify people moving from talk to action, then arrest them before an attack happens. The **New York State Capitol** in Albany houses the state legislature and is a symbol of government authority, making it an attractive target for anyone seeking maximum attention.

stories.title: Bessent to unveil 'the toughest sanctions in history' on Iran this Monday
stories.what_happened: Bessent announced Thursday that the Treasury Department will hold a press conference **this coming Monday** to detail a new round of sanctions he describes as among the **toughest ever imposed on any nation**. He told reporters the goal is 'the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world,' explicitly saying both US allies and rivals — including **China** — will be forced to choose whether to keep doing business with Iran or with the US-led coalition. Separately, the **State Department** has already sanctioned six entities and one individual it accuses of helping Iran move illicit funds using cryptocurrency, moving ahead of Monday's bigger announcement. Bessent argues the cumulative effect of these measures should cause Iran's economy to **'collapse.'**
key_points: Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** says Monday's sanctions package will be among the **toughest ever imposed** on any country.
He's calling it **'the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world'** and says allies and adversaries alike will have to pick a side.
The State Department has already sanctioned **six entities and one individual** accused of moving Iranian funds through crypto.
Bessent claims the new measures are designed to make Iran's economy **'collapse.'**
It comes as ship traffic through the **Strait of Hormuz** has fallen to roughly **8 vessels a day**, down from about 130 before the war began.

depth.background: The US and Iran have been in an escalating standoff since a US-Israel military campaign against Iran began in **February 2026**, after which Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz — a narrow waterway through which a huge share of the world's oil and gas passes — 'closed' and began attacking ships and laying mines. Washington has already leaned heavily on sanctions (financial penalties that cut a country off from global trade and banking) to pressure Iran, and Trump has separately claimed the US now has **'total control'** of the strait. Treasury Secretary Bessent is the official in charge of designing and enforcing US economic sanctions.

stories.title: Mohammad Rizwan refuses to sign his PCB contract after being demoted and stripped of the ODI captaincy
stories.what_happened: Pakistan's star wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan has refused to sign the PCB's newly announced central contract for the coming season, becoming the only one among 30 contracted players to hold out. The board restructured its grading system, eliminating the elite Category A entirely and placing Rizwan — along with Babar Azam — in Category B instead. Sources say Rizwan has put two demands to the board: reinstating Category A for senior, high-performing players, and giving national captains clearly defined authority and stability, free from board interference. The PCB has reportedly rejected both demands and does not plan to renegotiate. The dispute follows Rizwan's removal as ODI captain, which came after head coach Mike Hesson wrote to the board describing him as **'difficult to deal with'** and prone to complaining about squad selection during a tour of the West Indies.
key_points: Rizwan is the **only one of 30 contracted players** who has not signed the PCB's new central contract.
The board scrapped the top **Category A** grade entirely, demoting Rizwan (and Babar Azam) to **Category B**.
He's reportedly demanding **Category A be reinstated** and that captains get **clear autonomy** over team decisions.
The PCB has **rejected his demands** and says it won't renegotiate or revisit the decision.
Head coach **Mike Hesson** reportedly recommended removing Rizwan as ODI captain, calling him **'difficult to deal with.'**

depth.background: In Pakistan cricket, the PCB (Pakistan Cricket Board) issues annual central contracts that rank players into pay grades — historically topped by 'Category A' for the country's biggest stars. Rizwan had been Pakistan's ODI captain and one of its most consistent performers across formats in recent years, alongside Babar Azam. The PCB's central contract system has been a recurring flashpoint in Pakistan cricket, with frequent leadership changes and player grievances over pay, selection, and board interference — a pattern that has repeated across multiple board regimes.

stories.title: Max Verstappen extends his Red Bull contract to 2030, ending exit speculation before his home race
stories.what_happened: Verstappen and Red Bull announced Thursday that he has signed a new contract extension running through **2030**, replacing his previous deal (through 2028) which reportedly included performance clauses that could have allowed an earlier exit. The announcement came deliberately ahead of his **home Dutch Grand Prix** at Zandvoort — his last home race at that specific circuit, since it's dropping off the calendar. Verstappen had previously said he'd considered stepping back from F1 altogether, citing a desire for more family time and frustration with the current generation of battery-reliant F1 cars, but said he remains motivated to help Red Bull **"get back to the top again."**
key_points: Four-time champion **Max Verstappen** signed a new deal keeping him at **Red Bull through 2030**, announced Thursday, August 20.
His previous contract ran through **2028** but reportedly had **performance clauses** that could have let him leave earlier if Red Bull kept underperforming.
The news lands just before his **emotional home race** at Zandvoort, which is dropping off the F1 calendar after this year.
Verstappen had openly **questioned whether he'd stay in F1 at all**, citing family time and frustration with the 2026 cars' heavy reliance on electrical battery power.
He said Red Bull has **"the best people"** and he's committed to helping the team **"get back to the top again"** after a season of struggling to match Mercedes' pace.

depth.background: **Max Verstappen** has won four consecutive F1 drivers' championships with Red Bull, but the team has struggled to match Mercedes' pace in the 2026 season under new technical regulations that lean more heavily on hybrid/electric power. That underperformance, combined with Verstappen's stated frustration with the new car era, had fuelled persistent speculation he could seek a move to a rival team once his contract's performance-linked exit clauses kicked in. Zandvoort, the Dutch Grand Prix venue, is Verstappen's home race and is leaving the F1 calendar after this edition, adding emotional weight to the timing.

stories.title: Anthropic's investors are reportedly targeting a $2 trillion IPO in October — the largest ever
stories.what_happened: According to Bloomberg and other outlets, Anthropic's investors are pushing for the company to go public in **October 2026** at a valuation of **$2 trillion or more** — a figure that would make it the **biggest IPO in history**, eclipsing SpaceX. The company confidentially filed IPO paperwork with the SEC back in **June** and is expected to file publicly by the **end of August**. Its **annualized revenue run rate** (current monthly revenue multiplied by 12) reached **$65 billion** at the end of July, and backers expect that to climb to **$100–120 billion by the end of 2026** — more than **ten times** its level at the start of the year. **Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley** are reportedly running the offering, which could raise more than **$60 billion**. The one wrinkle: revenue growth slowed in June after **US export controls** temporarily restricted sales of Anthropic's top AI models.
key_points: Anthropic's backers are said to be targeting a **$2 trillion valuation** for an **October IPO**, which would make it the **largest public listing in history**, topping SpaceX's record.
The AI company confidentially filed its **S-1** (the core IPO disclosure document) with the US SEC in **June**, and could file publicly as soon as **end of August**.
Its annualized revenue **run rate hit $65 billion** by end of July, and backers reportedly expect **$100–120 billion by year-end** — over **10x** where it started 2026.
**Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley** are the lead underwriters ("bookrunners") on a deal that could raise upward of **$60 billion**.
Growth actually **slowed in June** after the **US Commerce Department** imposed a temporary export control on Anthropic's most advanced AI models.

depth.background: **Anthropic**, the maker of the Claude chatbot, is one of a handful of AI labs (alongside OpenAI and Google DeepMind) racing to build the most capable AI systems, and has raised money at eye-watering valuations — its last private round (Series H) reportedly valued it near **$965 billion**. Going public via an **IPO** (initial public offering — a company's first sale of shares to the general public on a stock exchange) would let ordinary investors buy into that growth, but also expose the company to public quarterly scrutiny for the first time. SpaceX currently holds the record for the largest-ever IPO benchmark investors are measuring Anthropic against.

stories.title: Somali pirates hijack a suspected Iranian 'shadow fleet' oil tanker off Yemen
stories.what_happened: On Thursday, six armed individuals hijacked the oil tanker SIBU 1 roughly **136 nautical miles east of Al Mukalla, Yemen**, according to UKMTO. The tanker broadcast a distress call before the attackers signaled intent to sail it toward Bosaso in Somalia. SIBU 1 flies an Eritrean flag but is believed to be part of Iran's sanctions-evading shadow fleet, having repeatedly delivered fuel to a Houthi-controlled terminal at Ras Isa. It was one of **29 vessels the US Treasury's OFAC sanctioned in December 2025** for moving hundreds of millions of dollars of Iranian petroleum. This is the second tanker hijacking in the region in just four days, and the 13th attack of the year — more than double the total for all of 2025.
key_points: The Eritrea-flagged tanker **SIBU 1** was seized by **six armed men** east of Yemen's coast.
It is the **second hijacking in four days** — the worst piracy surge off Somalia in **over a decade**.
SIBU 1 is at least the **13th vessel attacked** this year in the area, versus just **five in all of 2025**.
The US Treasury had already **sanctioned the ship in December 2025** as part of Iran's oil-smuggling 'shadow fleet'.
Attackers reportedly plan to sail it toward **Bosaso, Somalia**, a known pirate staging port.

depth.background: A 'shadow fleet' is a group of aging, often unregistered or falsely-flagged tankers that sanctioned oil exporters like Iran and Russia use to sell crude while dodging Western sanctions and insurance rules. SIBU 1 had been routinely ferrying fuel to a Yemeni port controlled by the **Houthi militia**, an Iran-backed group. Somali piracy, which was largely stamped out by international naval patrols a decade ago, has been quietly resurging in 2026 as those patrols thinned out and instability in Yemen created cover. The **UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO)** body, which tracks these waters, confirmed the distress call.

stories.title: Kolkata hotel fire that killed 9 Bangladeshi nationals: leaseholder arrested, owner still on the run
stories.what_happened: A fire tore through **Hotel Shikha Inn**, one of several hotels packed into a four-storey building on Kolkata's Mirza Ghalib Street, shortly after **2 am on August 19**. Nine people died, including a 4-year-old child, and several others were injured; all the victims confirmed dead so far are **Bangladeshi nationals** who were in Kolkata for medical treatment. Preliminary reports pointed to a possible **air-conditioner explosion** on an upper floor, though officials have not confirmed a cause. This week, Kolkata Police **arrested the hotel's leaseholder, Abu Zafar**, from Entally Main Market and detained two staff members for questioning, while the building's original owner, **Bireshwar Mitra, remains at large**. Police have set up a Special Investigation Team to determine whether the hotel was operating without adequate fire-safety clearances.
key_points: A pre-dawn fire at **Hotel Shikha Inn** on Kolkata's Mirza Ghalib Street killed **9 people**, including a 4-year-old child, all Bangladeshi nationals in the city for medical treatment
The blaze broke out around **2 am on August 19** in a four-storey building housing the hotel
Kolkata Police arrested the hotel's leaseholder, **Abu Zafar**, and detained **two staff members** for questioning
The hotel's original owner, **Bireshwar Mitra**, remains absconding as of this week
A **Special Investigation Team (SIT)** has been formed; the exact cause of the fire is still unconfirmed

depth.background: Kolkata's older, densely packed commercial districts — like the area around Mirza Ghalib Street — are lined with budget hotels that cater heavily to medical tourists from **Bangladesh**, who travel to Indian cities for treatment unavailable or unaffordable at home. Many of these buildings are decades old, converted from other uses, and fire-safety enforcement in India's crowded urban cores has long lagged behind the pace of construction — a gap that has produced a string of deadly hotel and building fires across Indian cities in recent years. A **leaseholder** runs the day-to-day hotel business, while the **owner** holds the underlying property, and both can face liability if the building itself was unsafe.

stories.title: RBI's own meeting minutes spook bond investors — a rate hike is suddenly back on the table
stories.what_happened: When the RBI released the minutes of its August Monetary Policy Committee meeting this week, they showed a markedly more hawkish undertone than the 'hold' decision suggested. Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta explicitly raised the possibility of a rate hike later in the year, while an executive director stopped just short of doing so. External members Ram Singh and Saugata Bhattacharya both flagged the potential need for the RBI to recalibrate policy quickly if inflation pressures persisted. Bond traders, who had been positioned for rates staying flat or eventually falling, reacted by selling government bonds — pushing the 10-year yield up as much as 4 basis points to 6.86% and 5-year yields up 8 basis points to 6.53%. Wall Street and local desks have since revised their rate-path forecasts: Goldman Sachs's Santanu Sengupta now expects quarter-point hikes in December and February, and Ashika Institutional Equities called the RBI's December meeting 'live' — meaning a hike is a real possibility for the first time in nearly four years.
key_points: Minutes from the RBI's **August rate meeting**, released this week, showed several committee members flagging inflation risk — a sharp shift in tone from the 'extended pause' markets had priced in.
Deputy Governor **Poonam Gupta** raised the possibility of a hike later this year; external members **Ram Singh and Saugata Bhattacharya** also flagged the need for swift policy recalibration.
The benchmark **10-year government bond yield jumped as much as 4 basis points to 6.86%**, and 5-year yields rose **8 bps to 6.53%**, as traders repriced the outlook.
**Goldman Sachs** now expects quarter-point hikes in **December and February**; a Nomura economist said the hawkish tone challenged her own call for an extended pause.

depth.background: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** held its policy rate — the **repo rate** — unchanged at **5.25%** at its August meeting earlier this month, with a 'neutral' stance that markets read as leaving room to cut later if needed. But the RBI also publishes detailed **minutes** of its rate-setting committee's internal discussion a couple of weeks after the decision — and those minutes often move markets more than the headline decision itself, because they reveal how divided or convinced the committee actually was.

stories.title: Ajinkya Rahane retires from all cricket, leaving KKR without a captain
stories.what_happened: Rahane announced his **retirement from international cricket and all formats with immediate effect** via a social-media post, saying **'today, I feel the timing is right for me to move on.'** Over his career he represented India in **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is**. Because the announcement covers **all formats**, it also ends his **IPL** playing days — and his tenure as **KKR captain**, a role he'd held for **two seasons**. That immediately opens up a **captaincy vacancy at Kolkata Knight Riders** heading into IPL 2027, with reports already floating names like Rinku Singh as a possible successor. The exit marks the end of a steady, understated career built more on temperament than flash.
key_points: Former India captain **Ajinkya Rahane, 38**, retired from **all formats** with immediate effect.
He announced it via **social media**: 'the timing is right for me to move on.'
He played **85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is** since his 2011 debut.
His exit also ends his **IPL** career — he was **KKR's captain** for two seasons.
It leaves **Kolkata Knight Riders** hunting a new leader for 2027.

depth.background: **Ajinkya Rahane** was one of India's most dependable middle-order Test batters of the last decade, remembered above all for **captaining India to a historic 2021 series win in Australia** while stand-in skipper. In recent years he moved into a franchise-elder role, leading the **Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR)** in the IPL for the past **two seasons**. At 38, with international selection long behind him, a retirement decision had been widely anticipated — the question was timing. His departure closes a **15-year career** that began with his India debut in **August 2011**.

stories.title: Franco Colapinto's breakout 2026 season has Alpine closing in on a 2027 extension — but nothing's signed yet
stories.what_happened: Franco Colapinto is enjoying his **best Formula 1 season to date**, closing the performance gap to and at times beating teammate Pierre Gasly, and that form has intensified talks over a **2027 contract extension** at Alpine. Team advisor **Steve Nielsen** said publicly that 'everyone wants more' from Colapinto before the team commits, tempering the growing expectation that an extension is coming. Multiple outlets now report Colapinto is 'ever closer' to staying, with his manager reportedly discussing an unusually structured contract length, but as of **August 21** no official announcement has been made. Colapinto himself has downplayed the contract talk, saying resolving his 2027 future is 'not the principal objective' right now compared with helping make the car faster. The 23-year-old was dropped by Williams entering this season after a difficult partial 2024-25 stint, making this year's turnaround a genuine redemption arc.
key_points: Colapinto is having his **best F1 season yet**, regularly matching or beating teammate Pierre Gasly and scoring points consistently
Alpine sporting boss **Steve Nielsen** says the team still wants **'more'** from him before committing, even as reports call an extension increasingly likely
As of **August 21**, no official contract announcement has been made — this remains a live, unresolved decision
Colapinto downplays the pressure, saying a new deal is **'not the principal objective'** right now versus making the car faster
His popularity across Argentina and the Spanish-speaking world — comparisons to F1 legend **Juan Manuel Fangio** — makes him valuable to Alpine beyond lap times

depth.background: **Franco Colapinto** burst onto the F1 scene as a mid-2024 Williams substitute driver and became an instant fan favorite, particularly across Latin America, for his aggressive racecraft. He didn't keep the Williams seat for 2026, instead moving to **Alpine**, where a marked improvement in form this season has put him firmly in the conversation for a longer-term future at the team. Alpine, owned by Renault, has been rebuilding after a difficult few years and is weighing driver stability against wanting to see continued improvement before locking in a multi-year commitment.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty snap a seven-day losing streak as global bond jitters ease
stories.what_happened: The **BSE Sensex** and **NSE Nifty 50** staged a strong recovery on **Thursday**, snapping a **seven-day losing streak**. The Sensex gained **628 points (0.82%)** to close at **77,537.72**, while the Nifty rose **154 points (0.64%)** to **24,231.85**. The rally was driven by **easing concerns over US bond yields**, short covering (traders buying back stocks they had bet against), and fresh buying in large heavyweight stocks. **Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)**, who had been selling, turned net buyers, purchasing **₹407.99 crore** of Indian equities in the prior session.
key_points: **Sensex** jumped **628 points (0.82%)** to close at **77,537.72**
**Nifty 50** rose **154 points** to settle at **24,231.85**, ending a **seven-day losing streak**
Foreign investors (FIIs) turned net buyers, purchasing **₹407.99 crore** of Indian equities
The rebound came as **US bond-market stress eased**, lifting risk appetite globally

depth.background: Indian markets had been sliding for over a week, weighed down by rising **US Treasury yields** — which make US bonds more attractive relative to riskier emerging-market stocks — along with elevated crude oil prices near **$92 a barrel** and broader geopolitical jitters. A losing streak this long is unusual and had started to worry traders about whether the rally in Indian stocks this year was running out of steam.

stories.title: Delhi ramps up security and infrastructure prep for the BRICS Summit it hosts next month
stories.what_happened: Delhi's Lieutenant Governor, **Taranjit Singh Sandhu**, chaired a review meeting on **August 20** covering security, traffic management, civic infrastructure and emergency medical arrangements ahead of the **BRICS Summit 2026**, which India will host in Delhi on **September 12–13**. This is the **18th BRICS Summit**, held under India's chairship around the theme **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.'** Sandhu directed key departments and civic bodies to tighten security protocols, streamline traffic across the city, maintain infrastructure, and deploy comprehensive emergency medical readiness across summit venues and the transit corridors leaders' motorcades will use. He stressed that all agencies must work in 'multi-agency coordination' and finish their assigned tasks on time, with preparations to continue without interruption until the summit.
key_points: Delhi's Lieutenant Governor **Taranjit Singh Sandhu** chaired a review of security, traffic and infrastructure readiness for the **BRICS Summit 2026**.
India hosts the **18th BRICS Summit** in Delhi on **September 12–13** — its first time chairing the bloc's annual leaders' summit.
The LG ordered every civic and security agency into **multi-agency coordination** covering venues and transit corridors.
India's chairship theme is **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.'**
Preparations extend beyond security and traffic to **emergency medical readiness** ahead of world leaders' arrival.

depth.background: BRICS is a grouping of major emerging economies — originally **B**razil, **R**ussia, **I**ndia, **C**hina and **S**outh Africa — that has since added more members and positions itself as a voice for the 'Global South' alongside Western-led forums like the G7. The bloc holds an annual leaders' summit, with the host and chair rotating each year; hosting is a chance for that country to help set the agenda and showcase itself to visiting heads of state. India has run major global summits before — it hosted the G20 leaders' summit in Delhi in 2023 — and treats these events as high-stakes logistics operations given the security needs of dozens of foreign leaders converging on one city.

stories.title: Scientists built an AI that predicts how well your body will respond to a vaccine — before you even get the shot
stories.what_happened: The study pooled blood samples from thousands of participants, including both healthy volunteers and people with weakened immune systems from conditions like **HIV, multiple myeloma, and autoimmune disease**. Researchers fed the data — antibody levels against dozens of unrelated microbes — into a deep-learning model, which found that people with higher baseline levels of antibodies to common germs like Staphylococcus aureus, RSV, and human respirovirus 3 tended to mount stronger COVID-19 vaccine responses. The team is calling these 'sentinel' antibodies, since they seem to signal overall immune readiness rather than anything specific to the vaccine itself. Roughly 5–6% of otherwise healthy people turned out to be weak responders, while some immunosuppressed participants surprised researchers with robust responses — suggesting readiness is about the immune system as a connected whole, not any one number.
key_points: Researchers analyzed **8,687 blood samples from 4,089 people** to find a pre-vaccine antibody 'fingerprint' that predicts immune response.
People with higher pre-existing antibodies to unrelated everyday bugs like **Staph aureus and RSV** — dubbed 'sentinel' antibodies — turned out to have stronger COVID-19 vaccine responses.
About **5–6% of healthy people** had unexpectedly weak vaccine responses, while some immune-suppressed patients (HIV, cancer, autoimmune disease) responded strongly — defying assumptions.
A **deep-learning model** spotted the predictive pattern across many antibody measurements at once — a signal invisible to any single test.

depth.background: Not everyone's immune system reacts the same way to the same vaccine — some people build strong, lasting protection, others barely respond, and doctors have long struggled to know which is which **before** the shot is given rather than after. Researchers set out to see whether a person's *existing* antibody profile — built up from a lifetime of ordinary infections — could hint at how 'ready' their immune system is to mount a strong response to something new, like a vaccine.

stories.title: Sri Lanka's batting line-up is gutted by injuries and a concussion-substitution rule, days before the Colombo Test
stories.what_happened: Sri Lanka heads into the second Test against India in Colombo with its batting line-up badly depleted by injuries. **Kusal Mendis** is unavailable with a hamstring injury picked up during last month's Lanka Premier League, and coach **Gary Kirsten** confirmed he **'is not going to be available for a while.'** Veteran **Dinesh Chandimal** suffered a concussion while fielding in the first Test and was replaced under ICC concussion-substitute protocols by Pasindu Sooriyabandara — a rule that also bars a concussed player from returning to action for **seven days**, ruling Chandimal out of the second Test too. **Pathum Nissanka**, still working back from wrist surgery in June, is also considered unlikely to play. The timing is brutal for Sri Lanka: it already trails the series **1-0** after losing the first Test in Galle by **165 runs**, and now must try to level things up fielding a batting order missing three of its most experienced players.
key_points: Three key batters are out for the second Test: **Kusal Mendis** (hamstring), **Dinesh Chandimal** (concussion) and likely **Pathum Nissanka** (wrist surgery recovery)
Chandimal was concussed while fielding and replaced by Pasindu Sooriyabandara — under ICC rules, a **concussion substitute can't play for 7 days**, ruling him out
Mendis picked up his hamstring injury during the **Lanka Premier League** last month and coach Gary Kirsten says he **'is not going to be available for a while'**
India already leads the two-match series **1-0**, having won the first Test in Galle by **165 runs**
Sri Lanka must now field a batting line-up missing three of its most experienced players against a red-hot Indian attack

depth.background: Sri Lanka is hosting India for a two-match Test series, with the first Test in **Galle** ending in a **165-run win for India**. Sri Lanka's top order has been thin on experience for some time, making its senior batters — wicketkeeper **Kusal Mendis**, opener **Pathum Nissanka**, and veteran **Dinesh Chandimal** — disproportionately important to its chances of competing. Head coach **Gary Kirsten**, the former India and South Africa batting great now coaching Sri Lanka, has been trying to rebuild the side's Test-match depth and consistency after a difficult run of results.

stories.title: Death toll in Central African Republic gold mine collapse passes 100, rescuers call finding survivors 'a miracle'
stories.what_happened: A gold mine collapsed on **Tuesday** in the village of Zamboye, in CAR's Nana-Mambéré prefecture near the Cameroon border, when several underground tunnels being dug by artisanal miners caved in. Rescue crews have since recovered the bodies of **more than 100 people**, with the toll rising steadily as debris is cleared. Bertrand Be Yangué, a member of the local Zamboye youth council helping coordinate the response, said finding anyone still alive under the rubble would be a 'miracle,' given how many people remain unaccounted for. Authorities have opened an investigation into what caused the collapse and whether anyone can be held criminally responsible for how the site was being operated.
key_points: A gold mine collapsed in the village of **Zamboye**, near the Cameroon border, after underground tunnels caved in
The confirmed death toll has risen to **more than 100**, with several people still missing under the rubble
A local aid worker said finding anyone alive at this point "would be a **miracle**"
The Central African Republic has thousands of people working in unregulated, **artisanal small-scale mining**, where collapses like this are disturbingly common
An investigation into the cause of the collapse — and possible **criminal liability** for whoever operated the site — is underway

depth.background: The **Central African Republic (CAR)** is one of the world's poorest and least stable countries, with large parts of its territory historically controlled by armed rebel groups rather than the central government, including areas rich in gold and diamonds. Because formal mining companies rarely operate safely or profitably in these contested zones, much of the country's mineral wealth is dug up by hand through **artisanal mining** — informal, often unlicensed digging using basic tools and no engineering oversight. Tunnel collapses, flooding, and cave-ins are a recurring hazard in this kind of mining across Central and West Africa, but this collapse's scale — over 100 dead — makes it one of the deadliest in recent memory.

stories.title: North Korea fires a barrage of missiles hours after Trump says he'll meet Kim this year
stories.what_happened: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area around 5pm local time on Thursday, August 20. The missiles flew roughly 300 km into North Korea's eastern coastal waters and caused no reported damage. The launch came just hours after Trump told reporters he expected to meet Kim Jong Un 'later this year,' and one day after North Korea **publicly shrugged off** a US decision to scale back upcoming joint military drills with South Korea — a gesture Washington had intended as a goodwill signal. Japan's government also confirmed detecting the launch and lodged no additional response beyond monitoring.
key_points: North Korea launched **about 10 short-range ballistic missiles** toward its eastern waters on Thursday
The missiles flew roughly **300 km (185 miles)** before splashing into the sea, South Korea's military said
The launch came hours after **Trump said he expects to meet Kim Jong Un** later in 2026
It also followed North Korea **dismissing a US offer to scale back** joint military drills with South Korea
No casualties or territorial violations were reported — the missiles stayed in North Korean-controlled waters

depth.background: Donald Trump met Kim Jong Un three times during his first term — in Singapore, Hanoi, and at the DMZ in 2019 — but the summits never produced a deal on North Korea giving up its nuclear weapons, and diplomacy stalled for years afterward. Since returning to office, Trump has repeatedly said he wants to revive that **personal relationship** with Kim, arguing it could prevent conflict even without full denuclearization. North Korea, meanwhile, has kept testing and expanding its missile arsenal, using launches like this one both as weapons tests and as **signals of leverage** ahead of any renewed talks.

stories.title: Odisha announces ₹1,000-crore flood relief package as toll from record rains mounts
stories.what_happened: Odisha Chief Minister **Mohan Majhi** announced a **₹1,000-crore special relief package** on Thursday for people affected by the state's worst flooding in years. The floods have hit **over 9.4 lakh people** across **1,381 villages** in **74 blocks** spanning **six districts**, with more than **3.7 lakh people evacuated** to safer locations. **550 relief camps** have been set up to provide food and shelter, backed by **45 ODRAF teams, 8 NDRF teams, and 65 Fire Services teams**. Under the new package, farmers who lost **33% or more** of their crops will get an agricultural input subsidy for up to two hectares of land. The state has recorded **1,100mm of rainfall** since June — about **34% above normal** and the highest total in **25 years**.
key_points: Odisha's government announced a **₹1,000-crore relief package** for flood-hit families
Over **9.4 lakh people** across **1,381 villages** in **six districts** have been affected
More than **3.7 lakh people** have been evacuated, with **550 relief camps** now running
The state has received **1,100mm of rain** since June — **34% above normal** and the highest in **25 years**

depth.background: Odisha has been battered by an unusually intense monsoon this year, driven by a slow-moving depression system that formed over the Bay of Bengal and has repeatedly dumped heavy rain on the state. Farmers, already dealing with earlier flooding this season, have seen crops wiped out for a second time in some districts, and rescue teams have been stretched thin evacuating cut-off villages.

thread.previously: We reported that a depression system from the Bay of Bengal was pushing floodwaters into parts of Odisha, cutting off villages, with more rain still expected.
thread.changed: Odisha's government has now announced a ₹1,000-crore relief package after confirming over 9.4 lakh people across six districts have been affected, with more than 3.7 lakh people evacuated.

stories.title: SEBI scraps notarization hurdles for foreign investors, easing the door into Indian markets
stories.what_happened: SEBI **streamlined the onboarding process** for foreign portfolio investors by permitting the use of **digitally signed power-of-attorney documents**, eliminating the earlier requirement for **notarization and consularization**. The new regulations are set to **take effect on August 20, 2026**. In practice, an overseas fund that wants to invest in India can now complete a key piece of its registration paperwork **electronically**, rather than shipping physical documents abroad for stamps and consulate verification. The move lands at a moment when Indian markets are **wary** — domestic bonds have been under pressure after the RBI's hawkish policy minutes and rising oil prices — so making it simpler for foreign money to enter is timely. It is a technical, plumbing-level reform rather than a headline stimulus, but it lowers a real barrier that funds have long complained about.
key_points: New rules let foreign investors use **digitally signed** power-of-attorney documents.
The old requirement to **notarize and consularize** paperwork is dropped.
The change takes effect **August 20, 2026**.
Aim: cut red tape and **speed up onboarding** of foreign portfolio investors.
Comes as India courts **foreign inflows** amid a jittery bond market.

depth.background: **SEBI** is the Securities and Exchange Board of India — the regulator that polices the country's stock and bond markets, similar to the SEC in the US. **Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs)** are overseas funds that buy Indian stocks and bonds; their money is a big swing factor for Indian markets, so making it easier for them to register matters. Until now, an FPI's legal paperwork — like a **power of attorney** (a document authorizing someone to act on your behalf) — had to be **notarized** and **consularized** (stamped by a notary and then verified by an Indian consulate abroad), a slow, costly process. Cutting that friction is part of a broader push to make India a more welcoming, competitive destination for global capital.

stories.title: Russia's overnight barrage kills a dozen in Kyiv as its missile war on Ukraine hits its bloodiest stretch since the invasion began
stories.what_happened: In the early hours of **August 20**, Russian forces launched a fresh wave of ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, striking residential and other buildings and triggering fires across the capital. UN OCHA and local officials reported **at least a dozen people killed** and close to 50 injured. It came days after a separate assault killed 17 people when Ukrainian defences failed to intercept a single one of the ballistic missiles fired at the city, managing to stop only drones. Ukrainian officials say the pattern reflects a deliberate Russian strategy: Moscow appears to be probing and exploiting the exact gap in Ukraine's air defences — interceptors for ballistic missiles — that allies have been slowest to fill. July's death toll of 377 civilians was already the worst monthly total in more than four years of war, and August's attacks suggest the trend is worsening rather than easing.
key_points: Russian ballistic missiles and drones hit Kyiv overnight, killing **at least a dozen civilians** and wounding nearly 50, per UN humanitarian office OCHA.
Ukraine has effectively **run out of Patriot interceptors** — the only weapon in its arsenal that can shoot down Russian ballistic missiles.
**July was the deadliest month since April 2022**, with 377 civilians killed as Russian missile volumes surged.
Kyiv's top drone commander says Moscow plans to push toward **200 missiles per attack**, more than double earlier barrages.
President Zelenskyy says lives 'could have been saved' had allies resupplied interceptor stocks faster.

depth.background: Russia has bombarded Ukrainian cities with missiles and drones since its **2022 invasion**, but the campaign has intensified sharply through 2026 as Moscow leans harder on long-range strikes while ground fighting grinds on. Ukraine's air-defence net relies heavily on **US-made Patriot batteries** — the only system that reliably intercepts ballistic missiles — but the interceptor rounds they fire are expensive, slow to manufacture, and controlled by Washington's allocation decisions. Kyiv has spent months pleading with the US and NATO allies to speed up interceptor supplies, with mixed results, even as President Trump has periodically floated and then walked back pledges to let Ukraine build Patriot interceptors domestically.

stories.title: China sentences Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison for a $2 billion fraud
stories.what_happened: A court in **Shenzhen** sentenced Hui Ka Yan to **life in prison** on Thursday, closing one of the most dramatic chapters of China's property crisis. Judges found that Evergrande, under Hui's direction, engaged in large-scale financial fraud by **inflating the company's assets while concealing its true liabilities** from investors and regulators. The court also fined companies linked to Hui more than **$2 billion** and ordered him to forfeit all his personal assets. He was additionally stripped of all political rights, a common punishment in China for serious economic crimes. Evergrande collapsed in 2020 with more than **$300 billion in liabilities**, the largest corporate debt failure in the world at the time, and its unraveling triggered a broader crisis across China's property sector that is still playing out.
key_points: Hui Ka Yan, founder of collapsed property giant **Evergrande**, sentenced to **life in prison** by a Shenzhen court
Companies tied to him fined more than **$2 billion** for large-scale financial fraud
He pleaded guilty in **April** to inflating Evergrande's assets while hiding its liabilities
Evergrande collapsed in **2020** owing more than **$300 billion**, the world's most indebted developer
Hui was stripped of **all political rights** and ordered to forfeit his personal assets

depth.background: Evergrande was once China's biggest property developer, a symbol of the country's decades-long real-estate boom that helped power its economic growth. When Chinese regulators cracked down on excessive borrowing in the property sector in **2020**, the company's debt-fuelled model collapsed, leaving it unable to pay contractors, homebuyers, or bondholders. Hui Ka Yan, its billionaire founder, was accused of directing the company to falsify its books for years to keep money flowing in even as the business unraveled. He pleaded guilty in **April 2026** to fraud and misuse of funds during his time as chairman.

stories.title: Nevada clears Tesla, Uber and Waymo to run up to 8,000 robotaxis in Las Vegas
stories.what_happened: On **August 20**, the Nevada Transportation Authority voted unanimously to grant Tesla, Uber and Waymo permits to run commercial, paid autonomous-vehicle service across Clark County, home to Las Vegas. The permits let the three companies put up to **8,000 robotaxis** on the road combined over the next 12 months: Tesla can scale to as many as **5,000** vehicles, while Waymo and Uber were each capped at **1,000** — Uber's fleet will actually run through partnerships with Hyundai's self-driving unit Motional and Amazon-owned Zoox, rather than Uber's own cars. This is separate from, and vastly larger than, the **10-vehicle** state DMV testing permit Tesla had received just days before for supervised trials. Despite the generous cap, Tesla's own robotaxi chief engineer, Eric Early, said the company would be 'extremely happy' to reach **2,500** cars in the first year — about half of what it's now allowed. Local taxi and limousine operators pushed back at the hearing, warning regulators about market oversaturation and congestion in Las Vegas's already-busy tourist corridor.
key_points: Nevada's Transportation Authority unanimously approved permits for **Tesla, Uber and Waymo** to run paid robotaxi service in Clark County (Las Vegas).
Combined, the three companies can deploy up to **8,000 driverless taxis** over the next 12 months.
Tesla's ceiling is **5,000 vehicles**; Waymo and Uber (via Motional and Zoox) were each capped at **1,000**.
Tesla's own robotaxi chief engineer admits the company will likely field only **~2,500** cars in year one — far under its cap.
Local taxi operators objected at the hearing, warning of **oversaturated, gridlocked roads** on the Las Vegas Strip.

depth.background: Nevada has spent years positioning itself as one of the most permissive US states for autonomous-vehicle testing. Just days earlier, Tesla received a separate, much smaller Nevada DMV permit — capped at only **10 vehicles** — for supervised testing; a Transportation Authority permit like this one is the much bigger, separate approval a company needs before it can legally *charge the public* for driverless rides. Waymo already runs commercial robotaxis in cities like Phoenix and San Francisco, while Tesla has spent years promising a 'Cybercab' robotaxi business that investors are still waiting to see at real scale. Las Vegas — dense, tourist-heavy, and open around the clock — is now set to become one of the most closely watched live tests of competing self-driving bets.

stories.title: Nvidia strikes a $7 billion deal for AI coding startup Poolside — without buying it
stories.what_happened: Nvidia agreed to pay Poolside **$6 billion** for a non-exclusive license to its 'Model Factory' platform, which generates AI models tailored for software development. Alongside the licensing fee, Nvidia is investing **$1 billion in equity** directly into Poolside, valuing the startup at **$12 billion** before the new money. As part of the arrangement, **109 of Poolside's roughly-similar-sized staff** received job offers to move to Nvidia, though Poolside's founders will remain and keep running the company independently. The deal was first reported by tech-industry outlets citing a letter Poolside sent to its investors. Poolside can still license its technology to other buyers since the Nvidia deal is non-exclusive, unlike a typical acquisition that would lock the technology to one buyer.
key_points: Nvidia is paying **$6 billion** to non-exclusively license Poolside's AI model-building technology, its 'Model Factory'.
Nvidia is also investing **$1 billion** directly into Poolside at a **$12 billion** pre-money valuation.
**109 Poolside employees** received job offers to join Nvidia as part of the arrangement.
Poolside's founders explicitly said **'this is not an acquisition and it is not an acquihire'** — the startup keeps operating independently.
The license is **non-exclusive**, so Poolside can still sell its AI coding models to other companies too.

depth.background: Poolside is an AI startup that builds large language models specialized in writing, debugging, and optimizing software code — essentially AI co-pilots for programmers. Nvidia, the dominant maker of the chips that train and run AI models, has increasingly used its cash pile to strike deals that secure access to cutting-edge AI software and talent without the regulatory scrutiny a full acquisition would trigger. This 'license-plus-investment' structure has become a favored workaround in the AI industry — Google's move with Windsurf and other similar deals set the template — letting a giant like Nvidia effectively absorb a startup's technology and staff while the startup remains a separate legal entity.

stories.title: Israel's defense minister publicly warns Erdogan against 'dangerous adventures' in Syria
stories.what_happened: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said publicly today that Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is 'dragging Turkey into dangerous adventures in Syria,' warning that 'Israel will not allow any entity to threaten its security.' The comments follow an Israeli airstrike two days ago — eight hits on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib province, near the Turkish border — which cratered the runway and damaged the facility but caused no casualties. Israel says the strike was meant to stop Turkey from deploying troops and advanced weapons there. Turkey's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations as 'untenable,' and Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said he personally told Israel there were no plans for a Turkish base — that the site was simply being rehabilitated for Syria's own air force. Reporting also suggests the strike has created **friction between Netanyahu and the Trump administration**, with US Syria envoy Tom Barrack reportedly calling it an unnecessary escalation.
key_points: Israeli Defense Minister **Israel Katz** accused Turkish President **Erdogan** of dragging Turkey into 'dangerous adventures' in Syria — Israel's sharpest public words yet in the standoff.
The warning follows Israel's **airstrikes two days earlier** on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase near the Turkish border, which cratered the runway but caused no casualties.
Turkey's Foreign Ministry called Israel's allegations **'untenable'**, and Syria's foreign minister said no Turkish base was planned — the site was only being repaired for Syria's own air force.
The strike reportedly put Israeli PM **Netanyahu at odds with the Trump administration**, whose Syria envoy called it an 'unnecessary escalation'.
Both countries are the **strongest militaries in the Middle East**, and neither has a clear channel to de-escalate — raising the risk of miscalculation.

depth.background: Since Syria's Assad regime fell, outside powers have been jockeying for influence over what replaces it, and **Turkey and Israel have emerged as the two biggest rivals** in that contest. Turkey backs Syria's new government and has discussed deploying military assets there; Israel sees any Turkish military footprint near its border as a direct threat and has struck Syrian sites it believes could host Turkish forces. The two countries don't have full diplomatic relations and communicate largely through public statements and, at times, back-channel US mediation — which makes moments like this especially prone to escalating faster than either side intends.

stories.title: Gold races toward record highs in India, crossing ₹1.58 lakh per 10 grams
stories.what_happened: Gold prices in India pushed toward record territory in trading today, with 24-carat gold crossing **₹1.55 lakh per 10 grams** nationally and the MCX October futures contract touching an intraday high of **₹1,58,750** (22-carat gold traded near ₹1,45,191). Silver also surged, up more than ₹4,000 on the day. The move follows a decline in **US bond yields** after the US Treasury announced it would double its buyback of long-term securities, making non-yielding gold comparatively more attractive to investors, layered on top of ongoing safe-haven demand tied to the **Strait of Hormuz/Iran-US standoff** and volatile global markets. Gold is now up over 10% in the past month and more than 59% over the past year, though still below its all-time high of ₹1,69,349 set on March 2, 2026.
key_points: **24-carat gold crossed ₹1.55 lakh** per 10 grams nationally, with MCX futures touching an intraday high near **₹1,58,750**.
Silver jumped too, rising over **₹4,000** on the day.
Gold is now up more than **10% in the past month** and over **59% over the past year** — still short of its March all-time high of ₹1,69,349.
The rally is being driven by **falling US bond yields** (after the US Treasury doubled its buyback of long-term debt) and safe-haven buying tied to **Strait of Hormuz tensions**.
Dealers say record prices are **dampening actual jewelry demand** even as investment demand stays strong.

depth.background: Gold tends to rise when investors get nervous about the world economy or geopolitics, because unlike a stock or bond it pays no interest but also can't default — making it a classic 'safe haven.' It also tends to rise when interest rates or bond yields fall, since gold competes with interest-bearing assets for investors' money and looks relatively more attractive when those yields drop. India is one of the world's largest gold buyers, especially around weddings and festivals, so price moves like this ripple directly into household budgets, not just investment portfolios.

stories.title: Max Verstappen signs Red Bull contract extension through 2030, ending exit speculation
stories.what_happened: Red Bull announced today that Max Verstappen has signed a contract extension keeping him with the team through the end of the **2030 season**, two years beyond his previous deal and with the exit clauses removed. New team principal Laurent Mekies called it 'fantastic news for everyone at Red Bull... his impact on our team and on Red Bull's motorsport story has been transformational.' The announcement comes the day before Verstappen's home Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, and follows a stretch of reported tension over his future — as recently as this week, Verstappen had reportedly been resisting signing anything beyond a single year, wary of the team's push to lock him in longer term.
key_points: **Max Verstappen** has signed a new Red Bull deal running through the **end of 2030** — two years beyond his previous 2028 contract.
The extension **removes the performance-related exit clauses** that had fueled months of speculation he could leave.
The announcement lands the day before his **home Dutch Grand Prix** at Zandvoort, ending talk of a possible move to McLaren.
It comes despite a **rough 2026 season** — Verstappen is currently sixth in the standings and winless through the first half of the year.
The deal follows **major turnover at Red Bull**, with Christian Horner, Helmut Marko, and Adrian Newey all having left and Laurent Mekies now running the team.

depth.background: Verstappen, a four-time world champion with 71 career wins, had been at the center of prolonged contract uncertainty this year. His existing deal, running to 2028, carried performance-related exit clauses, and reports emerged that his management had held talks with McLaren about a possible 2027 move — talks that intensified as Red Bull went through a leadership shake-up with the departures of team boss Christian Horner, advisor Helmut Marko, and design chief Adrian Newey.

thread.previously: Verstappen was reportedly resisting Red Bull's push for a long-term commitment, wanting only a one-year deal and to keep his exit clause intact, after the team had tabled a five-year, ~$80 million-a-season offer to scrap it.
thread.changed: He has now signed — extending through 2030 and giving up the exit clauses entirely, ending the standoff before his home race.
