stories.title: India and Japan sign a maritime security pact as defence ministers meet in New Delhi
stories.what_happened: Rajnath Singh hosted Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi in New Delhi for a bilateral meeting focused on strengthening defence cooperation and promoting stability in the Indo-Pacific. The two ministers signed a **Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation**, formalizing plans to deepen operational cooperation on maritime security in a 'practical and effective manner.' Ahead of the formal talks, Koizumi laid a wreath at the Gaurav Stambh war memorial, visited the Indian Navy's indigenous stealth destroyer **INS Chennai**, and held discussions with Indian Navy Chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and the Western Naval Command. Koizumi said afterward he would 'devote all my efforts to turn discussions into outcomes.'
key_points: Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh** and Japan's **Shinjiro Koizumi** met in New Delhi to deepen defence ties.
The two sides signed a **Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation**.
Both ministers committed to deeper cooperation for a **'free and open Indo-Pacific'**.
Talks also covered closer **defence equipment and technology collaboration** under the 'Make in India' push.
Koizumi visited the **indigenous warship INS Chennai** and met India's Navy chief before the formal meeting.

depth.background: India and Japan have steadily deepened defence and security ties over the past decade, largely as a hedge against China's growing assertiveness in the Indo-Pacific region — the vast maritime zone stretching from the eastern coast of Africa through the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Both countries are part of the informal 'Quad' grouping with the US and Australia, built around similar concerns about freedom of navigation and security in these waters. Regular defence-minister meetings like this one are how the two governments turn broad strategic alignment into concrete agreements — from maritime patrols to shared equipment standards.

stories.title: India's home World Championships end in heartbreak as PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen both crash out
stories.what_happened: PV Sindhu's campaign ended on Thursday when she lost a tight three-game round-of-16 match to China's third seed Wang Zhi Yi, 21-11, 15-21, 21-17, after having opened with straight-game wins over lower-ranked opponents. Lakshya Sen was eliminated even earlier, in the second round, losing 21-19, 19-21, 17-21 to the USA's unseeded Garret Tan — a result being described as one of the tournament's biggest upsets. The two losses mean India's singles medal hopes at its own World Championships are over before the semifinal stage, a disappointing outcome given the home-crowd advantage and India's rising profile in the sport. India's other hopes now rest on the doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty and rising singles player Ayush Shetty, both of whom are still through to the pre-quarterfinals.
key_points: Badminton's **BWF World Championships** are being held in New Delhi — India's **first time hosting since 2009**.
**PV Sindhu**, a two-time Olympic medallist chasing a record **6th World Championship medal**, lost her round-of-16 match **21-11, 15-21, 21-17** to China's Wang Zhi Yi.
**Lakshya Sen**, a 2021 bronze medallist, suffered a shock **second-round exit** to unseeded American Garret Tan.
Both losses end India's singles medal hopes at a tournament being played in front of a home crowd for the first time in 17 years.
Doubles pair **Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty**, and young singles player **Ayush Shetty**, remain alive in the draw.

depth.background: The World Championships are badminton's most prestigious event outside the Olympics, held annually and rotated among cities that bid to host it. India last hosted the tournament in **2009** in Hyderabad, so this New Delhi edition — running August 17–23 at the Indira Gandhi Arena — is a rare chance for Indian players to compete for a world title in front of a home crowd. Sindhu, now 31, has won more World Championship medals (five) than any other woman in the sport's history and came in hoping to add a sixth. Sen made his name with a bronze at the delayed 2021 edition and has been tipped as India's best men's singles hope since.

stories.title: India moves to collapse GST into just two tax slabs, promising cheaper daily essentials
stories.what_happened: On **August 20**, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman attended a meeting of the state-ministers' panel (the **GoM**) to walk through the Centre's proposal for restructuring GST. The core idea: shrink the current multi-slab structure down to just **two main rates, 5% and 18%**, with a **40% special rate** reserved for a short list of luxury or "sin" goods such as tobacco and high-end cars. Sitharaman described the exercise as a "**system-cleaning reform**" — the aim is fewer disputes over which rate applies where, and lower sticker prices on goods that move from a higher slab, like 12% or 28%, down into the new 5% or 18% bands. The proposal builds directly on PM Modi's August 15 Independence Day pledge to deliver "next-generation" GST reforms. The plan is not final: it still needs the **full GST Council** — which includes every state's finance minister plus the Centre — to formally approve the new rate structure before it takes effect.
key_points: Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** presented the Centre's plan to a panel of state ministers on **August 20** to simplify India's Goods and Services Tax.
The proposal collapses today's multiple GST slabs into just **two main rates — 5% and 18%** — plus a **40% special rate** for a handful of luxury/sin items.
It follows PM **Modi's Independence Day announcement** on August 15 of "next-generation" GST reforms.
The stated goal is a **"system-cleaning" reform** that lowers prices on everyday goods and cuts compliance headaches for businesses.
The plan still needs sign-off from the full **GST Council** — the state-and-centre body that has final say — before it becomes law.

depth.background: India's GST — the single nationwide tax that replaced a maze of state and central taxes in 2017 — has long been criticized for having **too many rate slabs** (5%, 12%, 18%, 28%, plus special rates), which makes compliance confusing and invites disputes over which rate applies to which product. The government has periodically simplified it since; this latest push is being pitched as the next big leap — **"GST 2.0"** — squeezing most goods into just two main brackets. It was set in motion when PM Modi flagged "next-generation" GST reform in his **Independence Day speech from the Red Fort** on August 15, and the **Group of Ministers (GoM)**, a panel of state finance ministers who negotiate rate changes before the full GST Council votes, met on August 20 to go through the Centre's specific proposal.

stories.title: Elon Musk's Starlink reapplies to India's space regulator for a 30,000-satellite Gen 2 network
stories.what_happened: Starlink has filed a **fresh application** with IN-SPACe seeking approval for its next-generation **Gen 2** satellite constellation — roughly **30,000 satellites**, more than six times the size of its already-approved Gen 1 network. The new filing includes **direct-to-device connectivity**, technology that would let satellites talk directly to regular smartphones without any special dish or antenna. This is Starlink's second attempt at Gen 2 approval in India: its first application was turned down because some of its proposed features and frequency bands clashed with Indian telecom regulations. Right now, no non-geostationary satellite operator — not Starlink, not rival **Eutelsat OneWeb**, not the Reliance-Jio/SES joint venture — has actually begun commercial satellite-internet service in India, largely because security clearances and spectrum pricing are still unresolved across the industry.
key_points: Starlink has resubmitted its application to **IN-SPACe**, India's space regulator, for its **Gen 2** satellite constellation.
The new bid covers nearly **30,000 low-Earth-orbit satellites**, flying at **340-615 km altitude**.
It includes **direct-to-device (D2D)** tech — letting satellites connect straight to ordinary mobile phones, no special equipment needed.
Starlink's **first Gen 2 application was rejected** — some features and frequency bands didn't meet Indian rules.
Only its smaller **Gen 1 network (4,408 satellites)** has been cleared so far, back in **July 2025** — and still isn't commercially live.

depth.background: **Starlink**, owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, beams internet down from thousands of satellites orbiting close to Earth (**low-Earth orbit**, or LEO) instead of relying on cables or ground towers — useful for reaching remote areas ordinary broadband can't. India has been a difficult market to crack: the government requires foreign satellite operators to clear security, spectrum (radio frequency), and pricing approvals through **IN-SPACe**, the national space regulator, before they can operate. Starlink's smaller Gen 1 constellation got the green light over a year ago, in July 2025, but still hasn't launched commercial service in India — showing how slow this approval pipeline can be even after a plan is technically cleared.

stories.title: Sensor maker Tempsens opens a ₹650-crore share sale and is six times covered on day one
stories.what_happened: Tempsens Instruments (India) opened its share sale for bidding on **Thursday 20 August 2026**, and by the end of the first day the issue was **5.95 times subscribed**. The breakdown was lopsided: the **non-institutional** bucket of wealthy individual investors was covered **12.51 times**, **retail** **6.48 times**, and the **institutional** bucket just **0.05 times** — as is typical on day one. The offer totals **₹650 crore**, made up of a **fresh issue of ₹95 crore** that goes to the company itself and an **offer for sale of ₹555 crore**, which is existing shareholders cashing out rather than new money for the business. The price band is **₹285 to ₹300 per share**, with a lot size of **50 shares**, so the smallest application is about **₹15,000**. Bidding closes on **24 August**, allotment is expected **25 August**, and the shares are due to list on the BSE and NSE on **28 August**.
key_points: Issue was **5.95 times subscribed** on day one
Wealthy individual investors bid **12.51x**; retail **6.48x**; institutions only **0.05x**
Total size **₹650 crore** — **₹95 crore** new money, **₹555 crore** sold by existing owners
Price band **₹285–₹300** a share; minimum application about **₹15,000**
Bidding closes **24 August**, listing expected **28 August**

depth.background: An **IPO (initial public offering)** is the moment a private company first sells shares to the public and lists on a stock exchange. In India, the offer is split into buckets: **retail** (ordinary small investors), **NII/HNI** (wealthy individuals and firms bidding large amounts) and **QIB** (qualified institutional buyers — mutual funds, insurers, foreign funds). **Subscription** counts how many times over the shares on offer have been bid for; **5.95x** means investors asked for nearly six shares for every one available. Institutions almost always bid on the final day, so a near-zero QIB number on day one is normal, not a warning. **Tempsens Instruments (India)**, founded in **1990**, makes temperature sensors, electrical heating systems and specialised cables — unglamorous industrial hardware that sits inside factories, steel plants and power stations.

stories.title: SEBI will pilot putting corporate bonds on a shared digital ledger, working with the RBI
stories.what_happened: **Amarjeet Singh**, a whole-time member of the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** — the regulator for India's stock and bond markets — said on **Thursday 20 August 2026** that SEBI will run a pilot to test **tokenisation of bonds**. The pilot will examine whether a **shared ledger** can allow the security and the cash to transfer **simultaneously**, removing the reconciliation step that sits between the two today. It will also test whether **coupon payments** — the regular interest a bond pays its holder — and other servicing events can be handled automatically by **smart contracts**, which are small programs that execute a payment when a pre-set condition is met. Crucially, the pilot is being run **in coordination with the Reserve Bank of India**, because the cash leg of any settlement sits under the central bank's remit, not SEBI's. SEBI framed the effort as part of a wider push to build a **deeper corporate bond repo market** — the short-term market in which bonds are used as collateral for cash loans, and which is what gives a bond market day-to-day liquidity.
key_points: SEBI whole-time member **Amarjeet Singh** announced the pilot on **Thursday**
It will test **tokenised bonds** — bond ownership recorded on a shared digital ledger
**Automated coupon payments** via smart contracts are part of the trial
Run **in coordination with the RBI**, so securities and money can move together
Aim is a **deeper corporate bond repo market** and lower reconciliation costs

depth.background: India's stock market is deep and liquid; its **corporate bond market is not**. A corporate bond is simply a loan to a company that can be bought and sold, but in India most bonds are bought and then held to maturity, so there are few buyers and sellers on any given day. One reason is plumbing: settling a bond trade means one system updating who owns the security and a separate system moving the cash, with people reconciling the two afterwards. **Tokenisation** means recording ownership as an entry on a **shared digital ledger** that all parties see at once, so the security and the money can change hands in the same instant. Regulators worldwide have been running versions of this experiment for several years; India is now joining with a supervised pilot rather than a free-for-all.

stories.title: A 33-year-old who has waited a decade may take Kuldeep Yadav's place in the Colombo Test
stories.what_happened: Reports on **20 August 2026** indicated India are set to hand **Saransh Jain** his **Test debut** in the second Test against Sri Lanka in **Colombo**, starting **23 August**. He would come in for **Kuldeep Yadav**, who had a difficult first Test in **Galle**: **25 overs, 103 runs conceded, one wicket**, unable to find rhythm on a surface that offered spin. Jain, now **33** and playing for **Madhya Pradesh**, carries a substantial first-class record — **188 wickets in 54 matches at 27.30**, plus **2,223 runs** including **two centuries and 14 fifties** — and was the standout performer of Madhya Pradesh's **2025-26 Ranji Trophy** campaign with **30 wickets**. He earned the call-up as a replacement for the injured **Washington Sundar**. India go into the match **1–0 up**, having won in Galle by **165 runs** on the back of **Manav Suthar's ten-wicket haul**, with **Shubman Gill** captaining after being passed fit from a finger injury and **Jasprit Bumrah** absent with a knee problem.
key_points: **Saransh Jain**, 33, is set for a Test debut in Colombo from **23 August**
He would replace **Kuldeep Yadav**, who took **1 for 103** off 25 overs in Galle
Jain has **188 first-class wickets** at an average of **27.30** from 54 matches
He was called up only as cover for the **injured Washington Sundar**
India lead the two-Test series after winning the first by **165 runs**

depth.background: **Kuldeep Yadav** is a left-arm wrist-spinner — a rare, high-risk, high-reward type of bowler who turns the ball away from right-handers using his wrist rather than his fingers. He has been in and out of India's Test side for years precisely because that method produces either match-winning spells or expensive ones. **Saransh Jain** is the opposite kind of cricketer: an **off-spinner** who turns the ball with his fingers, a dependable lower-order batter, and a **Madhya Pradesh** domestic professional who has been grinding through the **Ranji Trophy** since his early twenties without an India cap. He was named in this squad only because **Washington Sundar** was injured — the classic route by which a long-serving domestic player finally gets a look.

stories.title: BCCI moves the Duleep Trophy final out of its own academy so fans can actually watch it
stories.what_happened: The BCCI confirmed on **20 August 2026** that the final of the **2026-27 Duleep Trophy**, scheduled for **6 to 10 September**, has been moved from the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru to the **M.A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai**. The stated reason is spectator access: the CoE carries **restrictions on crowd attendance**, and the board decided the tournament's showpiece deserved a venue where fans can turn up. The **rest of the tournament stays at the CoE**, beginning on **Sunday 23 August** with East Zone against North East Zone and North Zone against West Zone. The board is also widening coverage — **all matches will be streamed live**, with television coverage of one quarter-final, one semi-final and the final. The six zonal sides are led by **Ishan Kishan (East)**, **Kanhaiya Wadhawan (North)**, **Ruturaj Gaikwad (West)** and **Tilak Varma (South)**, among others.
key_points: Final shifted from Bengaluru's **Centre of Excellence** to Chennai's **Chepauk**
Reason: the academy has **restrictions on public access** — no real crowds
Final runs **6–10 September**; the tournament starts **23 August**
Every match will be **streamed live**, with TV for a quarter-final, semi-final and the final
Six zonal teams, captained by **Ishan Kishan, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Tilak Varma** and others

depth.background: The **Duleep Trophy** is India's oldest surviving zonal first-class competition, in which teams representing **North, South, East, West, Central and North East** zones play multi-day cricket. For the last few seasons the **BCCI** — the Board of Control for Cricket in India, which runs the domestic game — has staged it at the **Centre of Excellence (CoE)** in Bengaluru, the board's own training academy. That is convenient for pitch control and player management, but the CoE is a **closed campus**: it was built as a training facility, not a stadium, and it cannot let large numbers of the public in. The result has been a marquee domestic final played in front of almost nobody. **Chepauk** — the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai — is one of India's oldest Test grounds and seats tens of thousands.

stories.title: RBI's hawkish August minutes rattle India's bond market, putting rate hikes back on the table
stories.what_happened: Minutes from the RBI's early-August policy meeting, released this week, showed a **notably more hawkish tone** than the headline decision suggested. While the MPC left the repo rate unchanged at **5.25%** for a fourth consecutive meeting, the minutes revealed that roughly half the committee is now leaning toward raising rates rather than holding or cutting them, driven by rising concern about inflation. That shift caught investors off guard, since markets had been positioned for steady-to-lower rates. The **10-year government security yield** climbed to roughly **6.78%** and the **rupee slid past ₹95 to the dollar** as traders repriced the odds of tighter policy ahead. The RBI's own projections show it expects **CPI inflation** to rise through the year — from 4.7% in the second quarter to 5.9% in the third and 5.5% in the fourth — even as it raised its full-year **GDP growth forecast to 6.7%** from 6.6%, citing resilient consumer demand and strong exports.
key_points: Minutes from the RBI's August meeting show members growing more worried about **inflation risk**, opening the door to **rate hikes** despite holding the repo rate at **5.25%** for a fourth straight meeting.
Roughly **half the committee** now leans toward tightening policy ahead, a sharp reversal from the market's expectation of steady or falling rates.
The **10-year government bond yield** rose to around **6.78%** on the news.
The **rupee weakened past ₹95 per US dollar** as investors repriced the odds of higher borrowing costs.
The RBI still raised its **FY2026 GDP growth forecast to 6.7%**, citing resilient domestic demand and robust exports.

depth.background: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is India's central bank — its six-member **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** meets roughly every two months to set the **repo rate**, the interest rate at which it lends to commercial banks, which ripples through to loan and deposit rates across the economy. For most of this year the MPC has held rates steady, betting that inflation would stay contained while growth held up. The committee's published minutes — released with a lag after each meeting — are closely watched because they reveal the internal debate behind the headline decision, often moving markets more than the decision itself.

stories.title: India's newest stock listings are outperforming even as the overall IPO boom cools
stories.what_happened: New data shows that six companies which listed on Indian exchanges in August have seen their share prices climb between **9% and 81%** above their issue price, even as the broader Nifty 50 has been sliding for multiple sessions. **Behari Lal Engineering** became the latest example, debuting today with shares opening at **₹465** on the NSE — a **63.1% premium** to its issue price — and **₹458** on the BSE, up **60.7%**. This comes against a backdrop where India's total IPO fundraising for 2026 has fallen to about **$5.78 billion**, down roughly a fifth from **$7.32 billion** in the same period last year, after two record years in 2024 and 2025. Analysts at Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan still expect full-year 2026 proceeds to land above **$20 billion**, with Kotak Mahindra Capital and Goldman projecting up to **$25 billion**, partly on the strength of a pipeline that includes Reliance Jio, SBI Mutual Fund, PhonePe, boAt, Flipkart, and NSE's own long-awaited listing.
key_points: Six companies that listed on Indian exchanges in **August alone** have rallied between **9% and 81%** above their issue price.
**Behari Lal Engineering** debuted today with shares opening at a **63% premium** on the NSE and **61% premium** on the BSE.
Overall IPO fundraising is actually down about a fifth this year to roughly **$5.78 billion**, from record years of **$22.36 billion in 2025** and **$20.65 billion in 2024**.
Companies are **cutting deal sizes and accepting lower valuations** to get deals done, even as the listings themselves pop on debut.
Big-ticket IPOs still expected before year-end include **PhonePe, boAt, Flipkart, and the National Stock Exchange (NSE)** itself.

depth.background: India has just come off two record-breaking years for initial public offerings (IPOs — when a private company first sells shares to the public), with companies raising over $20 billion in both 2024 and 2025 as investors piled into India's growing economy. That pace has slowed sharply in 2026: with broader Indian markets under pressure from high oil prices and global bond yields, companies have been trimming how much they try to raise and accepting lower valuations just to get their listings done. Despite that caution at the fundraising stage, investor appetite for the shares once they actually start trading has stayed strong, creating an unusual split between a **cooling primary market** (new share sales) and a **hot secondary market** (trading once listed).

stories.title: England bowl Pakistan out for 171 on a rain-hit opening day at Headingley, piling pressure on a fragile batting line-up
stories.what_happened: On a rain-disrupted opening day at Headingley, England **bowled Pakistan out for just 171 runs**, with seamers **Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue combining for 10 wickets** to rip through the batting line-up. England then reached **112 for 2** in their reply by the close of play, already building a commanding position in the match despite the interrupted overs. The collapse extends a pattern of fragile batting performances that has plagued Pakistan's Test side through this difficult stretch, adding fresh scrutiny to the team just as it tries to stabilize under restored leadership.
key_points: Pakistan were bowled out for just **171** on the rain-interrupted opening day of the first Test at Headingley.
England seamers **Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue shared 10 wickets** between them.
England closed the day at **112 for 2** in reply, already well ahead in the match.
Play was repeatedly interrupted by rain, compressing the day's overs.
The result deepens the pressure on Pakistan's batting after a build-up already clouded by fitness and form concerns.

depth.background: England and Pakistan are playing the first of a **three-Test series** at Headingley in Leeds, with both sides entering out of form — Pakistan sit eighth in the World Test Championship table with only two wins in six matches, while England, seventh, are coming off a home series loss to New Zealand. **Joe Root** is captaining England for the first time since giving up the role in 2022, and **Babar Azam** returned as Pakistan's Test captain after being restored to the role, having been cleared to play despite a hand injury picked up in a warm-up match. Both boards are betting that bringing back experienced former captains can stabilize teams that have each been through recent turmoil.

thread.previously: We reported that England and Pakistan were starting a three-Test series at Headingley with two comeback captains, Joe Root and Babar Azam, both trying to stabilize teams that had been through recent turmoil, with Babar only just cleared to play after a hand injury.
thread.changed: Play has now happened — England bowled Pakistan out for 171 thanks to Robinson and Tongue's 10 combined wickets, and reached 112 for 2 in reply, putting England firmly on top after a rain-hit first day.

stories.title: Walmart posts its weakest US sales growth in six years and loses nearly a tenth of its value in a day
stories.what_happened: Walmart reported quarterly results before the US market opened on **Thursday 20 August 2026**. Total revenue came in at **$187.9 billion**, up **5.9%** from a year earlier and slightly ahead of the **$186.7 billion** expected, and adjusted earnings of **$0.81 per share** beat the **$0.74** forecast — a **19%** jump on the prior year. But **US comparable sales grew only 2.6%**, well short of the roughly **3.8%** analysts had penciled in, and the weakest such reading in **over six years**. Management blamed two things: **weaker pharmacy sales** as drug pricing came down, and shoppers making **'trade-offs'** because higher fuel prices are eating into household budgets. The company then guided third-quarter adjusted earnings to **$0.62–$0.64**, below the **$0.68** consensus. The stock fell about **9.7%** to roughly **$103**, and dragged Target and Costco lower with it.
key_points: US comparable sales rose just **2.6%**, against the **3.8%** analysts expected
First miss on that measure in **more than five years**
Shares fell about **9.7%**, to roughly **$103**
Revenue still **$187.9bn**, up **5.9%**, and profit beat forecasts
Next-quarter profit guidance of **$0.62–$0.64** came in **below the $0.68** expected

depth.background: Walmart is the largest retailer in the world and, because roughly **90% of Americans live within ten miles of one of its stores**, its results are treated as a live read on how ordinary US households are actually doing. **Comparable sales** — the measure investors watch hardest — strip out new store openings and count only sales at locations open at least a year, so they show whether existing shoppers are spending more or less. Walmart had beaten expectations on that measure for **more than five straight years**, including through the inflation shock, because when money is tight shoppers trade *down* to it rather than away from it. That long streak is exactly why breaking it landed so hard.

stories.title: Lando Norris unveils a colour-shifting 'stealth' helmet for the last Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort
stories.what_happened: On **Thursday 20 August 2026**, media day at the Dutch Grand Prix, Norris revealed a one-off helmet for the weekend. The shell is **gloss black**, covered in thin flowing contour lines rendered in a **holographic, iridescent material** that shifts colour depending on the angle you view it from — the reason it has been nicknamed a **'stealth'** helmet. The design references **Alienware**, the gaming-computer brand, and specifically the customisable coloured lighting that runs around its desktop machines. Norris's **LN4 monogram** appears in holographic silver on both sides. The reveal came the day before running starts at a weekend that carries two pieces of history at once: it is **Zandvoort's first-ever F1 sprint** and also the **last Dutch Grand Prix** on the calendar. Norris shared the press-conference session with **Nico Hülkenberg** and **George Russell**, while **Max Verstappen**, **Sergio Pérez** and **Arvid Lindblad** took the earlier slot.
key_points: Gloss-black shell in a **holographic, iridescent finish** that changes colour with viewing angle
Design inspired by **Alienware**, the gaming-PC brand, and its customisable lighting
His **LN4 monogram** sits in holographic silver on both sides
Revealed on **Thursday**, ahead of Zandvoort's **first and last F1 sprint**
It is the **final Dutch Grand Prix** on the current calendar

depth.background: Formula 1 drivers wear one helmet design for most of a season, so a **one-off livery** is a deliberate statement — usually saved for a home race, a milestone start, or a sponsor activation. **Lando Norris** drives for **McLaren** and has built an unusually gaming-heavy personal brand, streaming and racing online, which makes tie-ins with hardware brands a natural fit. **Zandvoort**, the seaside circuit north-west of Amsterdam, returned to F1 in 2021 on the back of Max Verstappen's popularity and is leaving the calendar after this weekend, which has turned the whole event into a farewell — and prompted several drivers, Verstappen included, to run special designs.

stories.title: Russia's biggest missile-and-drone barrage on Kyiv in weeks kills at least 12, hits a children's hospital
stories.what_happened: Overnight between August 19 and 20, Russia launched a combined wave of **168 drones**, roughly 46 cruise and air-to-ground missiles, and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles at Kyiv, with Ukraine's air force first flagging inbound missiles just before midnight. Strikes hit more than 12 locations across three city districts — Darnytskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, and Solomianskyi — damaging residential buildings, a school, warehouses, and a children's hospital. At least **12 people were killed and over 33 injured**, according to Kyiv's mayor and emergency services, with the toll still rising as rescue operations continued into the morning. Ukrainian air defense intercepted 145 of the drones and most of the cruise missiles, but **no ballistic missiles were shot down**. In response, Poland scrambled aircraft and activated its own air-defense systems near the Ukrainian border, while Romania's Defence Ministry reported radar detections of aerial targets nearby, prompting NATO-patrol jets and a helicopter to scramble.
key_points: Russia fired **168 drones**, dozens of cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight — one of its **largest strikes on the capital this month**.
At least **12 people were killed and 33+ injured**, with the toll rising as rescue crews kept digging through the morning.
A **children's hospital** in the Solomianskyi district had its windows blown out and cars set alight on its grounds; patients and staff were sheltering underground, so no one there was hurt.
Ukraine's air defense downed **145 of the 168 drones** and most cruise missiles — but **intercepted zero of the ballistic missiles**, the most destructive weapons used.
**Poland scrambled fighter jets** and Romania tracked aerial targets near Ukraine's border, showing how close the strikes are landing to NATO territory.

depth.background: Russia has hit Kyiv with large-scale missile-and-drone barrages several times this month already (August 1, 4, and 16), part of a pattern of intensifying strikes on the capital even as on-and-off ceasefire talk continues elsewhere in the war. Ukraine's best defense against ballistic missiles — the US-made **Patriot air-defense system** — depends on a limited supply of interceptors that Western allies have been slow to fully replenish, which is why Ukraine can shoot down the bulk of slower drones and cruise missiles but struggles against ballistic missiles specifically. The strike also lands just days after Ukraine itself launched one of its largest-ever drone attacks on the Moscow region.

stories.title: SEBI bars a JPMorgan unit and a Mumbai broker for rigging the Sensex's brand-new closing-price mechanism
stories.what_happened: SEBI passed an emergency ('ex-parte') interim order against **Copthall Mauritius Investment Limited**, a unit of **JPMorgan Chase & Co**, and **Mansi Share and Stock Broking Private Limited**, barring both from accessing Indian securities markets and impounding **₹3.67 crore** in alleged wrongful gains — about ₹2.96 crore from Copthall and ₹71.64 lakh from Mansi. The order concerns trading on **August 13, 2026**, a Sensex weekly options-expiry day, during the new Closing Auction Session. Both firms held Sensex options positions that would profit if the index closed higher. SEBI's order says Copthall placed extremely aggressive buy orders between 3:21pm and 3:25pm — accounting for **99.91% of buy-order value** in the first price spike — pushing prices about 3% above their reference level, while Mansi simultaneously placed large sell orders, then cancelled the entire quantity within seconds, a sequence SEBI flagged as a coordinated attempt to move the closing price. The order was signed by SEBI whole-time member Kamlesh Chandra Varshney.
key_points: India's market regulator **SEBI barred Copthall Mauritius** (a JPMorgan Chase unit) and **Mansi Share and Stock Broking** from the markets, impounding **₹3.67 crore** in alleged illegal gains.
It's the **first enforcement action** under India's new **Closing Auction Session (CAS)**, introduced just weeks ago on August 3 to stop exactly this kind of price-gaming.

SEBI says on **August 13**, Copthall placed aggressive buy orders — **99.91% of buy value** in one price spike — while Mansi placed and then abruptly cancelled large sell orders, together pushing the Sensex close ~3% off its natural level.
Both firms held **Sensex options** that would profit from exactly the price move they allegedly engineered.
It follows SEBI chief **Tuhin Kanta Pandey's public warning just a day earlier** that manipulating the new CAS would draw 'strict action'.

depth.background: India's stock exchanges long used a simpler method to set a stock or index's official 'closing price,' which traders could game by placing large orders in the final seconds of trading to move the close in their favor — a loophole regulators cracked down on after the high-profile **Jane Street case**, where a global trading firm was banned for allegedly doing exactly this. To fix it, SEBI introduced the **Closing Auction Session (CAS)** on August 3, 2026: a 20-minute window (3:15–3:35pm) where the closing price is set through a fairer auction process rather than the last trade. This case is the first real test of whether that fix actually works.

stories.title: Trump declares 'Economic D-Day' against Iran, threatening sanctions on any country that helps it
stories.what_happened: President Trump posted on Truth Social on Wednesday evening, August 19, that he was escalating economic pressure on Iran, calling it **'ECONOMIC D-DAY'** and describing it as the **'MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY.'** He said any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities provide any kind of lifeline to Iran would face 'TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences.' He specifically named the channels Iran has historically used to evade sanctions — **oil smuggling, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries and front companies** — as targets of the new measures. Trump said he had 'no choice' but to tighten the squeeze after Iran 'TRAGICALLY' let his 60-day deadline for a deal expire without an agreement. The announcement did not name specific countries or companies to be sanctioned.
key_points: Trump announced on Truth Social Wednesday evening that the US would launch its **'most crushing' economic operation ever** against a country
Any nation whose **banks, businesses, airports or government** help Iran will face 'tremendous' new US sanctions
The move specifically targets **oil smuggling, cash transfers, exchange houses and ship registries** Iran has used to dodge existing sanctions
It follows the **expiry of Trump's 60-day deadline** for a US-Iran deal, which he said Iran let pass 'tragically'
Comes as the US Navy already backs a **rerouting of Hormuz shipping** through Oman, sidelining Iran's own claimed route

depth.background: Since mid-2026, the US and Iran have been locked in an escalating standoff after talks aimed at a nuclear and shipping-security deal broke down. Trump had set a **60-day deadline** for Iran to reach an agreement, and separately threatened to 'bomb' Oman if it interfered with US efforts to keep the **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway that a fifth of the world's oil passes through — open on US-backed terms. Shipping data already show more than **80% of Hormuz traffic** now moves via the Omani route rather than the path Iran claims to control. Iran has for years faced US sanctions on its oil exports; this new push threatens to extend the pain to any outside country or firm that helps Iran evade them.

thread.previously: Trump had threatened to bomb Oman if it interfered with US efforts to control Hormuz shipping, as his 60-day deadline for a US-Iran deal expired without an agreement.
thread.changed: Trump has now followed through with a concrete escalation: a threat of sweeping US sanctions on any country or company that helps Iran evade existing sanctions, which he's calling 'Economic D-Day.'

stories.title: The Fed publishes today's minutes from the meeting where three policymakers revolted
stories.what_happened: The Federal Reserve is releasing its official minutes from the July 28-29 FOMC meeting this afternoon, the standard three-week-lagged transcript-style summary the Fed publishes after every rate decision. Markets already know the headline outcome — a hold at **3.50%-3.75%** with three dissents for a hike — but the minutes are the first place the Fed explains, in its own words, the reasoning of both the majority and the dissenters. Analysts are watching specifically for how much weight policymakers put on **tariff-driven price increases** versus the risk of over-tightening into a softening jobs market, since that balance will shape expectations for the Fed's next meeting on September 15-16. The July dissent was the first time in roughly a decade that three FOMC members pushed in the same direction against the majority, so the minutes carry more market-moving weight than a typical release.
key_points: The Federal Reserve releases the **official minutes** from its July 28-29 meeting today, its standard **three-week-later** disclosure.

That meeting saw **three regional Fed presidents** — Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie Logan — dissent in favor of an immediate rate **hike**, the first same-direction triple dissent in **a decade**.
The minutes are expected to spell out **why** each dissenter wanted to raise rates, giving markets their clearest look yet at how deep the split runs.
Traders currently price roughly a **50/50** chance the Fed holds rates steady again at its **September 15-16** meeting.
Any hawkish language in the minutes could push **bond yields** and the dollar higher; dovish language could do the opposite.

depth.background: At its July meeting, the Fed's rate-setting committee (the **FOMC**) voted to hold its benchmark interest rate at **3.50%-3.75%** for a fifth straight meeting, but three of its members broke ranks to argue for a hike instead — an unusually visible crack in a body that normally moves in near-unanimous lockstep. The Fed publishes a detailed account of each meeting's discussion **three weeks later**; today is that day for July's meeting. Since the vote, softer-than-expected inflation and jobs data have shifted market sentiment back toward the Fed holding steady, but the dissent itself signaled real disagreement inside the institution that sets the price of borrowing for the entire US economy.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported that three regional Fed presidents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissented at the July meeting to push for a rate hike instead of a hold — the first three-way same-direction dissent in a decade — and that markets were already jittery, with stocks dipping and gold rising.
thread.changed: Today the Fed publishes the actual minutes explaining that dissent in detail, giving markets their first real look at the dissenters' reasoning rather than just the fact that they dissented.

stories.title: Pakistan's latest batting collapse puts stand-in captain Salman Agha's leadership under the microscope
stories.what_happened: On the opening day of the first Test at Headingley, Pakistan looked settled after **Abdullah Shafique and Imam-ul-Haq** put on **91 runs** together — the only real resistance of the innings — before the middle and lower order collapsed, losing their last **eight wickets for just 74 runs** to be bowled out for **171** in 48.1 overs. England's seamers **Ollie Robinson** and **Josh Tongue** took five wickets apiece, exploiting conditions that, while difficult, were described by observers as not unplayable. England responded by reaching **112 for 2** by the close of a rain-affected day, taking firm control of the match. The collapse immediately became the story of the day, with observers noting Pakistan's now-familiar pattern of promising partnerships undone by sudden capitulations, unfolding under a stand-in captain thrust into the role by injury.
key_points: Pakistan collapsed from a promising **91-run partnership** to being bowled out for just **171** on day one at Headingley, losing their **last 8 wickets for 74 runs**.
**Salman Ali Agha** is standing in as captain after **Babar Azam** was ruled out with a hand injury, putting him in charge for a must-not-lose opener.
England's **Ollie Robinson (5/51)** and **Josh Tongue (5/46)** did the damage, bowling Pakistan out in just **48.1 overs**.
It's the latest in a pattern: Pakistan were also routed by **Bangladesh** and have struggled repeatedly against high-quality pace bowling overseas this year.
England closed day one at **112/2**, already in firm control of the match.

depth.background: Pakistan's Test side has been searching for stability all year, cycling through injury absences and leadership changes while struggling against quality seam bowling away from home. Babar Azam, the team's talisman, was ruled out of this series opener with a hand injury, handing the captaincy to all-rounder **Salman Ali Agha** — himself no stranger to controversy, having previously picked up ICC demerit points for on-field conduct. This tour of England, running from **August 19 to September 13**, was seen as a chance for Pakistan to prove their overseas game had improved after a rocky year that included a heavy ODI series defeat in Bangladesh.

stories.title: RBI survey: Indians grow warier about jobs and prices, even as they stay upbeat on their own income
stories.what_happened: The RBI released the July 2026 round of its household surveys on Wednesday, showing that consumer sentiment on the broader economy, employment prospects, and price levels **weakened compared to the previous round**. At the same time, households' views on their own personal income growth and spending plans **held up and stayed positive** — a split between how people see the country's economic direction versus their own household finances. The survey drew responses from urban households across 19 cities and rural households across 31 states and union territories.
key_points: RBI's July survey found households turned **more cautious about the broader economy, jobs, and inflation**
Despite that, respondents stayed **optimistic about their own income growth and spending**
The survey covers **19 cities** (urban) and **31 states/UTs** (rural) via RBI's confidence indices
Results were released **the same week as RBI's hawkish August policy minutes**, adding to rate-outlook debate
The findings feed directly into the **Monetary Policy Committee's** thinking on interest rates

depth.background: Every two months, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) surveys thousands of households through its **Urban Consumer Confidence Survey**, **Rural Consumer Confidence Survey**, and **Inflation Expectations Survey of Households** — asking ordinary people how they feel about jobs, prices, and their own finances, both right now and a year ahead. These aren't hard economic data; they're a **sentiment gauge** the RBI uses alongside official statistics to judge whether consumers are pulling back or spending confidently, which feeds into decisions on interest rates. This round adds context to the RBI's already-hawkish August policy minutes covered in this feed, which pointed to interest rate hikes being back on the table.

thread.previously: We reported that the RBI's August policy minutes showed a hawkish tilt, rattling India's bond market and putting the possibility of rate hikes back on the table.
thread.changed: New household survey data shows consumer sentiment on the economy and inflation has also weakened, giving the RBI's hawkish stance fresh supporting evidence from the ground.
