stories.title: Russians are pulling billions of dollars out of their banks, fearing the Kremlin will seize deposits for the war
stories.what_happened: According to reporting citing central bank data, Russian depositors withdrew about **$3.4 billion** in cash in the first two weeks of August 2026 alone, adding to **$11.8 billion** pulled out in June and July. The flight from bank deposits is being driven by fears that President **Vladimir Putin** could freeze or confiscate savings to fund the war in Ukraine, alongside worries that inflation is eating away at the real value of money left in accounts. Russian banks, needing to replace that lost liquidity, raised deposit interest rates to a local high of **13.76%** on August 5 to lure savers back. The Bank of Russia has meanwhile had to step in directly, injecting more than **2 trillion rubles** (about **$26.9 billion**) in short-term loans to credit institutions through July, pushing total bank debt to the central bank close to **$80 billion** — nearly double where it stood at the end of last year. Sberbank projects the shift from savings into cash could total nearly **₽3.8 trillion** by year-end.
key_points: Russian depositors pulled roughly **$3.4 billion** from banks in the first two weeks of August, on top of **$11.8 billion** withdrawn in June and July combined
Many are pulling cash because they fear Vladimir Putin could **seize deposits** to help pay for the war in Ukraine
Banks are competing hard for the cash that's left — deposit rates hit a local peak of **13.76%** on August 5
Russia's central bank has pumped credit institutions with over **2 trillion rubles** (about **$26.9 billion**) in loans just to keep them liquid
Sberbank estimates cash withdrawals could reach **₽3.8 trillion** (~€42.6 billion) by the end of the year

depth.background: Russia's economy has been running a wartime budget for over four years, funded partly by government bonds that banks are expected to buy. For that system to work, banks need a steady inflow of ordinary people's savings. Since Russia's 2022 mobilization panic, trust in the banking system has been fragile, and inflation plus tightening Kremlin control over financial transactions have made Russians increasingly wary of leaving money in accounts they can't easily access.

stories.title: Wall Street is jittery over an unusual three-way revolt inside the Federal Reserve
stories.source: Rio Times Online — Global Economy Briefing
stories.what_happened: At its **July FOMC meeting**, the Federal Reserve voted to hold its benchmark rate at **3.50%–3.75%** — the fifth consecutive meeting without a change. But the vote wasn't unanimous: three regional Fed presidents — **Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie Logan** — dissented, arguing the Fed should instead raise rates by a quarter point to fight persistent inflation pressure. Analysts note this is the first time in **a decade** that three FOMC members have dissented in the same direction at once, an unusually visible crack in the committee's normal consensus. Since then, softer-than-expected July inflation and jobs data have shifted trader sentiment back toward the Fed holding steady at its next meeting on **September 15–16**, with prediction-market odds of a September hike hovering near 50/50. In today's trading, the **S&P 500 slipped roughly 0.5% to about 7,745**, gold rose toward **$4,398 an ounce** as investors sought safety, the dollar index eased to about **99.56**, and the 10-year Treasury yield sat near **4.73%**.
key_points: At its July meeting the Fed held its key interest rate at **3.50%–3.75%** for a fifth straight meeting.
**Three policymakers dissented** — all wanting to raise rates instead — the first time three officials have dissented in the same direction in **a decade**.
Markets are now split on whether the Fed hikes at its **September 15–16 meeting**, with prediction markets showing roughly a coin-flip.
Today's tape reflects the unease: the **S&P 500 slipped about 0.5%**, gold pushed toward **$4,400/oz**, and the dollar softened.
Softer July jobs and inflation data have since pulled the odds of a September hike back down, but the disagreement inside the Fed hasn't gone away.

depth.background: The **Federal Reserve** sets the US benchmark interest rate at meetings of its rate-setting committee, the **FOMC**, roughly every six weeks. Normally, the committee's votes are near-unanimous — dissent is rare because a divided Fed can unsettle markets by signaling internal disagreement about where the economy is headed. For most of 2026 the Fed has been cutting or holding rates to support a cooling job market, even as some officials worried that inflation, stoked partly by tariffs and Middle East-driven oil price spikes, hasn't fully come under control.

stories.title: Carlos Sainz nears a new one-year Williams deal for 2027, reversing course after rejecting their earlier offer

stories.title: Iran calls the drone strike on Iraqi Kurdistan's government a 'false-flag' plot, denying responsibility
stories.what_happened: Iraqi Kurdistan's government said two drones targeted Prime Minister Masrour Barzani's office and the residence of the head of the region's Parastin intelligence agency, and that Kurdistan's Counter-Terrorism Service traced the drones' origin to Iranian territory. Iran's government pushed back hard: Foreign Minister Araghchi condemned the attack as **reckless** while insisting Iran had nothing to do with it, and ministry spokesman Baghaei called it a **'highly suspicious'** incident that could be a false-flag operation designed to incriminate the Islamic Republic and sour Iran-Kurdish relations. No one has claimed responsibility, and the two sides' accounts of who launched the drones remain directly contradictory.
key_points: Iraqi Kurdistan accuses Iran of striking PM **Masrour Barzani's office** and an intelligence chief's residence with drones; no casualties were reported.
Iran's Foreign Ministry now calls the incident a **'false-flag' plot**, urging Kurdish authorities not to be fooled into blaming Tehran.
The claim and counter-claim land right as the **US-Iran ceasefire has just expired**, with no new deal in place.
No group has claimed responsibility, and neither side's version has been independently verified yet.

depth.background: Iraqi Kurdistan is a semi-autonomous region in northern Iraq with its own government, security forces and long, complicated relationships with both Iran and the US. Iran has previously struck targets inside Iraqi Kurdistan that it says shelter its armed opponents, so an accusation like this is not new territory — but doing it right as the ceasefire with the US collapses raises the stakes considerably. A 'false-flag' operation means staging an attack to make it look like someone else did it, in order to manipulate public opinion or provoke a response against that other party.

thread.previously: Iran's 60-day ceasefire with the US expired with no deal, and hours later two drones struck the office of Iraqi Kurdistan's Prime Minister Masrour Barzani and the residence of the region's intelligence chief; Kurdish authorities said the drones had been launched from Iranian territory.

stories.title: India opens the BRICS Civil Forum in Delhi, the last major public event before it hosts the leaders' summit next month
stories.what_happened: Civil-society representatives from BRICS countries gathered in New Delhi for a two-day forum. Government officials framed India's chairship as guided by a **'people-centric and humanity-first' approach**, positioning the forum's recommendations to feed into the official 'sherpa track' — the working-level negotiations that produce the summit's final declaration. The forum caps off a year of preparatory meetings across Indian cities covering BRICS's three pillars: political and security cooperation, financial collaboration, and people-to-people partnership.
key_points: The **BRICS Civil Forum** is being held August 17-18 in New Delhi, gathering civil-society voices from BRICS nations.
MEA Economic Relations Secretary **Sudhakar Dalela** said the forum's inputs will feed into the **BRICS Leaders' Summit**.
India's 2026 chairship has already run **over 350 meetings** across Indian cities in the run-up to the summit.
The main event — the **18th BRICS Summit** — will be held in Delhi on **September 12-13, 2026**.
This year's chairship theme is **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.'**

depth.background: **BRICS** is a bloc of major emerging economies — originally Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, since expanded to include more members and partner countries (sometimes called 'BRICS Plus'). Each year a different member holds the rotating chairship and hosts the annual leaders' summit; India holds it in 2026 and will host the summit in its own capital for the first time since 2021. The Civil Forum is a lower-profile, people-centric event that precedes the formal summit, meant to bring non-government voices — NGOs, academics, community groups — into the process.

stories.title: Tata Sons' board splits over how to handle N Chandrasekaran's exit as chairman
stories.what_happened: N Chandrasekaran informed the Tata Sons board on **August 12** that he will not seek another term as chairman once his current tenure concludes on **February 20, 2027**. In the days since, the board has reportedly split over how to formally respond: some directors want to hold a **vote** to accept or reject that decision, while others believe he should be **persuaded to reconsider** and stay on. Separately, the **Sir Dorabji Tata Trust** — one of the two trusts that control Tata Sons — wrote to the board arguing that directors' duty now is to focus on succession planning, not on relitigating whether Chandrasekaran should stay, and has asked the board to begin constituting a **selection committee** to find his replacement. The board is expected to take up the matter formally at a meeting in **mid-September**.
key_points: Tata Sons chairman **N Chandrasekaran** told the board on **August 12** that he does not want another term when his tenure ends on **February 20, 2027**.
The board is now divided: some directors want the decision **put to a formal vote**, others want to **ask him to reconsider**.
The **Sir Dorabji Tata Trust** has written to the board urging it to accept the decision and start building a **selection committee** for his successor.
It follows a **February 24 board meeting** where four of six directors backed extending Chandrasekaran, but **Noel Tata** — chairman of Tata Trusts — did not support it.
Tata Sons' board is expected to meet again in **mid-September** to formally address the succession question.

depth.background: Tata Sons is the holding company that controls the sprawling Tata Group — from Tata Motors and Tata Steel to Air India and TCS — making its chairman one of the most powerful executives in Indian business. N Chandrasekaran has led Tata Sons since 2017, and Tata Sons' controlling shareholders are two charitable trusts (the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust), whose leadership effectively decides who runs the group. This succession question has been building since a **February 24, 2026** board meeting where a proposed five-year extension for Chandrasekaran failed to win unanimous backing, with Noel Tata — chairman of Tata Trusts and a Tata Sons board member — declining to support it. stories.title: India's telecom giants are quietly softening you up for a big price hike later this year
stories.what_happened: Instead of announcing a headline price increase, Bharti Airtel has quietly discontinued several popular prepaid packs, including its ₹299 entry-level plan and its ₹319, ₹579 and ₹649 options, effectively pushing customers toward pricier alternatives. Jio and Vodafone Idea are widely expected to make similar quiet adjustments over the coming weeks as part of the same run-up. Telecom analysts tracking the sector expect this to be the precursor to a broader, industry-wide tariff hike of **12% to 20%**, with the increase most likely landing between **late October and December** — deliberately timed to avoid the Dussehra and Diwali festive shopping season, when a visible price jump would draw the most public anger. Neither the central government nor telecom regulator **TRAI** is expected to step in, since tariff-setting is left to the operators.
key_points: Airtel has already **scrapped several popular prepaid plans**, including its ₹299 entry-level and ₹319, ₹579 and ₹649 packs.
Jio and Vodafone Idea are expected to make similar quiet moves in the coming weeks.

depth.background: India's big three telecom operators — **Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea** — together serve over a billion mobile connections and have raised tariffs together in near-lockstep in past cycles, most recently in 2024. Jio in particular is under pressure to show stronger revenue growth ahead of a potential IPO, while Vodafone Idea has been financially fragile for years and badly needs higher average revenue per user to survive. Because switching your SIM is easy and cheap in India, operators typically raise prices together rather than one at a time, so as not to lose customers to a rival.

stories.title: BCCI's selectors are furious at the board's own secretary over a Rohit Sharma retirement denial

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia then went public saying there had been no such discussion and that Rohit would continue as a regular member of the side for as long as he remained part of India's plans — a statement selectors are said to have found frustrating, since it publicly contradicted their own call without consulting them first. That tension now feeds into a separate, higher-stakes conversation: Agarkar's own three-year term as chairman of selectors runs out in September, and under the current rules he's eligible for a one-year extension. The BCCI is reportedly keen to keep him in the role through the 2027 World Cup given his record — two ICC titles during his tenure — but a formal decision is expected only after the board meets him directly, with some reports floating VVS Laxman as an alternative if talks don't go smoothly.
key_points: Selectors had reportedly told **Rohit Sharma** they planned to move on from him after the England ODI series.
BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** then publicly said Rohit remains a **'regular member'** of the ODI team, contradicting that plan.
The selection committee, led by **Ajit Agarkar**, is said to be unhappy the board undercut their call in public.

Rohit Sharma, India's ODI captain for years, has already retired from Tests, and speculation about his ODI future has followed him through this year as India builds toward the 2027 ODI World Cup. stories.title: Bihar announces 32,388 new teacher vacancies — days after neighboring Jharkhand's exam system blew up

stories.title: Jharkhand's protest leader ends his hunger strike victorious — now he's demanding a law to make exams leak-proof
stories.what_happened: After the Jharkhand Cabinet's late-night cancellation of the JSSC-CGL exam, Mahto broke his 16-day hunger strike and announced he is escalating rather than ending the movement: a **'second phase'** demanding the government enact a formal law guaranteeing leak-proof examinations, rather than relying on case-by-case cancellations. stories.title: Tata Sons' annual meeting is adjourned for lack of quorum, days after its chairman announced he's leaving

Chandrasekaran** announced he will step down in **February**, meaning the group's board and trusts are simultaneously managing a leadership succession and this procedural stumble. key_points: **Tata Sons' AGM was adjourned** on August 18 after it failed to meet its quorum requirement.
The trigger: representatives of the **Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT)** couldn't attend because the trust's board itself couldn't convene, blocked by a regulatory restriction.

stories.title: Jharkhand cancels a major recruitment exam after weeks of student protests and a 16-day hunger strike
stories.what_happened: On the night of **August 17-18**, Jharkhand's Cabinet, led by Chief Minister **Hemant Soren**, announced it was cancelling the JSSC-CGL exam and all other recruitment tests conducted by the private contractor **TDPL (TSR Data Processing Private Limited)**, and ordering an investigation. Shortly after midnight, protest leader **Mahto broke his 16-day hunger strike** at Ranchi's Sadar Hospital in front of state ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari; two other student leaders who had also been fasting, Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti, ended their strikes too. The government's move came just ahead of an **August 18 deadline** protesters had set, warning that lakhs of students would march on the Chief Minister's house if demands weren't met. The cancellation, while a win for protesters demanding a clean process, creates a new problem: some candidates who **passed the exam legitimately** and have already started government jobs say the blanket cancellation is unfair to them, and may **challenge it in court**.
key_points: The Jharkhand government **cancelled the JSSC-CGL exam** and all recruitment tests run by contractor TDPL, after weeks of protests.
Student leader **Mahto ended a 16-day hunger strike** at a Ranchi hospital right after the cabinet's announcement.
Protesters had accused the exam of being **rigged or leaked**, and given the Hemant Soren government a deadline of **August 18** to act.
The cancellation **hurts candidates who passed fairly** and some have already joined government jobs — several may now sue.
The protest, which began **July 25**, is the latest flashpoint in India's recurring exam-integrity crisis.

depth.background: India's recruitment exams for government jobs are enormously high-stakes — a single posting can be a ticket out of poverty for a family, and millions compete for a small number of seats. That makes any hint of a **rigged or leaked exam** explosive, since it means years of preparation and money spent on coaching were wasted on a corrupted process. Jharkhand's JSSC-CGL (Combined Graduate Level) exam had been mired in allegations of irregularities, sparking a student movement led by figures like Mahto that escalated into a hunger strike outside government buildings in the state capital, Ranchi.

stories.title: Rishabh Pant returns to Delhi Capitals in a blockbuster swap that sends Kuldeep Yadav to Lucknow
stories.what_happened: Delhi Capitals and Lucknow Super Giants **officially completed a trade** ahead of IPL 2027: **Rishabh Pant returns to Delhi Capitals**, the team he represented for nine seasons and 111 matches (2016-2024, the most appearances by any player in DC's history), while **Kuldeep Yadav moves to Lucknow Super Giants** after five seasons and 72 wickets in 65 matches for Delhi. On the financial side, Pant rejoins DC at a **revised fee of ₹15 crore**, down sharply from the **₹27 crore** LSG paid to sign him in the 2025 mega auction. Kuldeep moves at his **existing ₹13.5 crore fee**. The fee gap means **LSG gains roughly ₹13.5 crore** in extra purse space for the next auction, while **DC's purse is reduced by ₹1.5 crore**.
key_points: **Rishabh Pant** is heading back to **Delhi Capitals**, the franchise he played nine seasons for, in a trade with Lucknow Super Giants.
**Kuldeep Yadav** moves the other way to **Lucknow Super Giants**, after five seasons taking 72 wickets for Delhi.
Pant rejoins DC at a **cut fee of ₹15 crore**, down from the **₹27 crore** LSG paid for him in the 2025 mega auction — roughly a **44% pay cut**.
Kuldeep moves at his existing **₹13.5 crore** fee, leaving LSG with **~₹13.5 crore extra** in their purse for the next auction, while DC loses ₹1.5 crore from theirs.
Pant made **111 appearances for Delhi** from 2016-2024, the most of any player in the franchise's history.

depth.background: The IPL (Indian Premier League) allows franchises to **trade contracted players** between seasons, subject to negotiated fees that adjust each team's remaining auction budget ('purse'). Rishabh Pant, one of India's most recognizable wicketkeeper-batters, spent nearly a decade as the face of Delhi Capitals before a big-money move to Lucknow Super Giants in the 2025 mega auction. Kuldeep Yadav, a left-arm wrist-spin bowler, had been one of Delhi's most effective bowlers over five seasons. This trade effectively **reunites Pant with his old franchise** while Delhi gives up a key bowler to make it happen.

stories.title: 46 Manipur militants surrender arms as ex-CM says Amit Shah gave a 'positive response' on NRC-before-Census demand
stories.what_happened: Security forces in Manipur accepted the surrender of **46 cadres** belonging to the KCP-Taibanganba faction, a splinter of the banned Kangleipak Communist Party, who handed over their arms as part of the state's ongoing effort to wind down armed groups active during the ethnic conflict. Separately, former Chief Minister **N. Biren Singh** said Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** gave a "positive response" to his demand that the **National Register of Citizens (NRC)** be updated in Manipur before the next national **Census** goes ahead. The demand comes from the "Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation" group, which called a two-day strike starting at midnight on August 17 to press the point, arguing that counting the population for the Census before verifying citizenship status would distort future seat delimitation and resource allocation in the state.
key_points: **46 cadres** of the banned KCP-Taibanganba faction surrendered with their weapons to security forces in Manipur
Former CM **N. Biren Singh** says Union Home Minister **Amit Shah** responded positively to demands for an NRC update before the Census
The demand is tied to a two-day strike called by the **"Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation"** group, starting midnight August 17
Manipur has been gripped by ethnic conflict between the **Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities** since May 2023
The NRC-before-Census demand is politically explosive, since it would count residents by citizenship status before the next national headcount

depth.background: Manipur has been under a state of near-continuous ethnic conflict since May 2023, when clashes broke out between the majority **Meitei** community, concentrated in the Imphal Valley, and the **Kuki-Zo** tribal communities in the surrounding hills, over land rights, reserved-tribe status, and political representation. The violence killed hundreds and displaced tens of thousands, and the state was placed under President's Rule after N. Biren Singh resigned as Chief Minister earlier this year amid criticism of his handling of the crisis. Various armed groups — some claiming to represent one community or the other, others left over from decades-older insurgencies like the banned **Kangleipak Communist Party (KCP)** — have used the instability to operate in the hills, and the central government has periodically pushed peace talks and surrender-and-rehabilitation schemes to wind them down.

stories.title: BCCI expands anti-corruption monitoring to every state T20 league after a TNPL player smuggled in an undeclared phone
stories.what_happened: The BCCI announced it is expanding **ACSU anti-corruption monitoring to cover every match in every state-run T20 league**, a first for the board, after detecting a rise in unauthorized approaches to players, franchise owners and team officials by suspected bookmakers. The immediate trigger was an incident in the **Tamil Nadu Premier League (TNPL)**, where a player was fined **₹1 lakh** and suspended after being caught carrying an undeclared mobile phone into the restricted players' area — a rule breach because unmonitored phones are one of the easiest ways for a player to be contacted or to pass on information during a match. BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** publicly backed a zero-tolerance approach, saying even a relatively minor breach like undeclared phone possession would now draw firm action, framing it as part of a broader effort to close gaps bookmakers could exploit across the many state leagues that have sprung up in recent years.
key_points: BCCI's **Anti-Corruption and Security Unit (ACSU)** will now cover **every match** in state-run T20 leagues, not just marquee tournaments
The trigger: a **Tamil Nadu Premier League (TNPL)** player was fined **₹1 lakh** and suspended for carrying an undeclared phone into the restricted players' area
BCCI has detected a **rise in unauthorized approaches** to players, owners and officials by suspected bookmakers across state leagues
BCCI secretary **Devajit Saikia** is publicly pushing a **zero-tolerance stance**, even for minor breaches like phone possession
State T20 leagues have multiplied across India in recent years, creating far more matches for corruption units to realistically police

depth.background: India's **state T20 leagues** — like the Tamil Nadu Premier League (TNPL), Karnataka Premier League, and similar tournaments in other states — have multiplied over the past decade as a lower-tier, franchise-style feeder circuit below the IPL, giving domestic players exposure and a bit of extra income. Because these leagues involve far more matches, smaller budgets, and less scrutiny than the IPL, they've long been seen as a softer target for match-fixing approaches by bookmakers, who typically try to recruit less-well-paid or less-experienced players. The BCCI's **Anti-Corruption and Security Unit (ACSU)** exists to police exactly this kind of risk — restricting player phone access during matches, monitoring betting patterns, and investigating approaches — but has historically concentrated its heaviest resources on the IPL rather than the many state leagues.

stories.title: Allahabad High Court slams UP government for taking Ram Mandir temple land without paying the agreed price
stories.what_happened: The **Allahabad High Court** ruled that the Uttar Pradesh government must deposit **Rs 1.21 crore, plus 8% annual interest**, as the unpaid balance owed for 1,512 square metres of temple land at Sugriv Kila in Ayodhya. A bench of **Justice Shekhar B. Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary** heard the petition filed on behalf of the deity Shri Thakur Ram Janki Sugrivji Virajman Mandir. The court's order details that a **sale deed was executed on December 22, 2023**, valuing the land at Rs 1.38 crore — but the state took over the land for developing the Ram Janma Bhoomi Temple without paying that price. The bench criticized the government for a contradictory legal position: **acquiring the land under the 2023 sale deed while simultaneously arguing in court that the deity's title was invalid** and the land should never have been sold in the first place.
key_points: The court ordered UP to pay **Rs 1.21 crore plus 8% annual interest** for **1,512 sq metres** of land at Ayodhya's Sugriv Kila.
The land belongs to the deity **Shri Thakur Ram Janki Sugrivji**, taken over for developing the **Ram Janma Bhoomi Temple** complex.
A **sale deed was signed in December 2023** for Rs 1.38 crore, but the state never paid the agreed price, the court found.
Judges **Shekhar B. Saraf and Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary** criticized the state for challenging the deity's ownership **while simultaneously taking the land.**
The order highlights a **legal contradiction**: the government questioned the temple's title to sell, even as it used that same sale deed to take possession.

depth.background: Ayodhya's Ram Mandir, consecrated after decades of legal and religious dispute culminating in a 2019 Supreme Court verdict, has driven a wave of **land acquisition** around the temple site for redevelopment — widened roads, a temple corridor, and related infrastructure. Landowners, including religious trusts and deities (which can legally hold property in India through a court-appointed manager), have separately been in disputes with the state over **fair compensation** for land taken for this expansion. This case involves land at 'Sugriv Kila,' tied to the deity Shri Thakur Ram Janki Sugrivji, represented in court as 'Virajman' — a legal status meaning the deity itself is treated as the petitioner.

stories.title: England hands its Test team to a foreign coach for the first time in the Bazball era — and it's not who Ben Stokes wanted
stories.what_happened: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has named **Stephen Fleming** as its new men's Test head coach on a four-year contract through September 2030, marking his first job coaching at international level despite a long, successful franchise-cricket coaching career. He replaces Brendon McCullum in the Test role specifically — McCullum remains in charge of England's white-ball teams — and arrives as Joe Root simultaneously takes back the Test captaincy he gave up in 2022. Fleming does have prior ties to English cricket, having previously played for Middlesex, Yorkshire, and Nottinghamshire (captaining Notts to a county title in 2005) and coached Southern Brave in The Hundred.
key_points: **Stephen Fleming**, the former New Zealand captain and longtime Chennai Super Kings coach, is England's new men's Test head coach.
He signed a **four-year deal** with the ECB running through **September 2030** — his first-ever international coaching job.
He replaces **Brendon McCullum**, who stepped down from the Test role after England's series loss to New Zealand in June but stays on to run England's white-ball teams.
The appointment comes as **Joe Root** simultaneously returns as full-time Test captain.
It's a pointed twist: former captain **Ben Stokes** recently said he'd like the England head coach job **one day** — it just went to someone else, now.

depth.background: England's Test side has been coached by fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum since 2022, alongside captain Ben Stokes, in a partnership that produced the aggressive 'Bazball' era and transformed the team's results and public profile. That era effectively ended when Stokes stepped back from the Test captaincy and McCullum, after a home series defeat to New Zealand in June, chose to step down from the Test coaching role specifically while remaining in charge of England's white-ball (ODI and T20) sides. **Stephen Fleming** built his post-playing reputation primarily in franchise cricket, most notably as the long-serving head coach of the Chennai Super Kings in the IPL, rather than in international coaching.

stories.title: Keith Barker retires at 39 after a knee injury cuts short his comeback season at Warwickshire
stories.what_happened: Keith Barker has announced his retirement from professional cricket after a **17-season career**, ending a comeback stint at **Warwickshire** — the county where he made his name — that was cut short by a persistent **knee complaint**. Across ten seasons at Edgbaston (2009-2018) he took **357 wickets** and scored **six first-class centuries**, and was part of the side that won the **2012 County Championship**. After moving to Hampshire for the 2019 season, he added a further **191 wickets and 1,975 runs**, cementing his reputation as one of county cricket's most dependable all-rounders.
key_points: Left-arm all-rounder **Keith Barker** has retired from professional cricket after a **17-season career**.
He returned to **Warwickshire** this summer at age 39 hoping for one more good year.
A persistent **knee complaint** forced the decision, cutting the comeback short.
At Edgbaston alone (2009-2018) he took **357 wickets** and scored **six centuries**, helping win the **2012 County Championship**.
At Hampshire (from 2019) he added **191 more wickets** and nearly **2,000 runs**.

depth.background: **Keith Barker** spent a decade at **Warwickshire** (2009-2018), becoming one of the county's most reliable all-rounders and helping the club win the **County Championship title in 2012**. He then moved to **Hampshire** ahead of the 2019 season, continuing to perform as a genuine batting-and-bowling all-rounder. This year, at 39, he rejoined Warwickshire on a short-term deal for one more season.

stories.title: Trump threatens to bomb Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, as the 60-day US-Iran deadline expires without a deal
stories.what_happened: President Trump said in a Fox News interview with Trey Yingst that the US would **'bomb the [expletive] out of'** Oman if it 'gets in the way' of American efforts to reopen and control shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. His comments came as the **60-day memorandum of understanding** between the US and Iran — meant to produce a lasting deal — expired this week without one. At the same time, **Iran's foreign ministry said Tehran had separately reached an agreement with Oman** on managing shipping traffic through the strait, even describing the talks as continuing but complex. Shipping data show the practical toll of the standoff: **only 13 ships** passed through Hormuz over the weekend, including just three on Sunday, compared with dozens on a normal day. Trump added that no further talks with Iran were currently scheduled.
key_points: Trump said **'we'll bomb the [expletive] out of them'** if Oman interferes with US efforts in the Strait of Hormuz, in a Fox News interview.
The **60-day window** for a US-Iran deal, agreed back in June, **expired this week** with no resolution.
Iran says it has reached a **separate agreement with Oman** over shipping traffic through the strait, even as Trump threatens Oman.
Shipping through Hormuz has **nearly ground to a halt** — only **13 ships** passed through over the weekend, a fraction of normal traffic.

depth.background: The **Strait of Hormuz** is a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly **one-fifth of the world's oil** passes through — making it one of the most important chokepoints in the global economy. The US and Iran agreed a **60-day ceasefire and negotiation window** in June after weeks of strikes, but that truce has been unraveling for days: Iran declared a 'fully offensive' posture as the ceasefire lapsed and seized a UAE-owned tanker. **Oman** has historically played the role of neutral back-channel between Washington and Tehran, hosting talks neither side could hold directly — which is what makes Trump now threatening Oman itself such an unusual escalation.

thread.previously: We reported that Iran declared a shift to a 'fully offensive' posture in the Strait of Hormuz as its ceasefire with the US formally lapsed, and that Iran had seized a UAE-owned oil tanker in the days after.
thread.changed: The 60-day window the US and Iran had set in June to reach a deal has now expired with no agreement. Trump responded by threatening to bomb Oman — a neutral country that has long mediated between Washington and Tehran — if it 'gets in the way' of US efforts in the strait, even as Iran said it has separately struck its own arrangement with Oman on shipping traffic.

stories.title: ISRO to end its 7-month launch freeze in September with the GISAT-1A earth-imaging satellite
stories.what_happened: ISRO is set to return to the launch pad in the **first week of September** with **GISAT-1A (also called EOS-05)**, an earth-observation satellite designed for high-frequency imaging of large areas of India, launching aboard a **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle)**. This will be the agency's first launch since the **PSLV-C62 mission carrying EOS-N1 failed on January 12, 2026** — a gap of nearly **seven months**, one of ISRO's longest pauses between launches in recent memory. The announcement signals that ISRO's internal investigation into the January failure has concluded and its launch operations are being cleared to resume.
key_points: ISRO's next launch, the **GISAT-1A (EOS-05)** satellite, is targeted for the **first week of September** aboard a **GSLV rocket**.
It will be ISRO's **first launch since January 12**, when the **PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission failed**.
The gap is nearly **seven months** — one of the longest pauses between launches for ISRO in recent years.
GISAT-1A is built for **high-frequency imaging** of large areas of the Indian landmass, useful for disaster response and security monitoring.

depth.background: **ISRO (the Indian Space Research Organisation)** is India's national space agency, responsible for satellite launches, navigation, and space science. After a launch failure, agencies typically pause all missions to investigate the root cause before flying again — both to protect expensive payloads and to rebuild confidence in the rocket. ISRO's PSLV-C62 mission carrying the EOS-N1 satellite failed on **January 12, 2026**, triggering this extended freeze. GISAT-class satellites sit in geostationary orbit, letting them watch the same stretch of Indian territory continuously, unlike satellites that pass overhead only briefly.

stories.title: Cadillac denies Sergio Perez is leaving for Williams, as his camp opens talks for a 2027 seat
stories.what_happened: Reports emerged that **Sergio Perez's management has opened discussions with Williams** about a potential 2027 race seat, contingent on Carlos Sainz not remaining there. **Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss** moved quickly to shut the rumours down, stating **'we have great confidence in our relationship with Checo, and he will also be racing in the Cadillac next year.'** The complication is that Perez's current agreement with Cadillac effectively only guarantees his seat for **2026**, leaving the picture beyond that genuinely open. Perez, for his part, has been **openly critical of the pace of Cadillac's development** as the team remains without a single point through the opening half of the season.
key_points: Perez's management has **opened talks with Williams** about a **2027 seat** — contingent on Carlos Sainz not staying there.
Cadillac CEO **Dan Towriss** dismissed the rumours, saying Perez **'will also be racing in the Cadillac next year.'**
Perez's current Cadillac deal effectively **only covers 2026**, leaving his future beyond that unresolved.
Perez has been **openly critical of Cadillac's slow development**, with the rookie team still **pointless** heading into the summer break.

depth.background: **Cadillac** is Formula 1's brand-new entrant for the 2026 season, built around veteran drivers **Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas** after Perez's earlier exit from Red Bull. A debut season with zero championship points has fuelled speculation about whether Cadillac's top driver might look elsewhere, especially with **Williams** — where Carlos Sainz's own future beyond 2026 remains uncertain — seen as a possible landing spot.

stories.title: Russia kills 9 and injures 43 across Ukraine in a single day, as a jet-powered drone slams into an Odesa shopping center
stories.what_happened: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched **128 drones** overnight into August 17-18, part of a barrage that, combined with other strikes, **killed at least 9 people and injured 43** across Ukraine over the day. A **jet-powered 'Shahed-type' drone** struck a shopping center and post office on the outskirts of Odesa, injuring seven people — including a couple and their 8-year-old son who were inside at the time — with five hospitalized; a nearby shoe factory was also damaged. Ukraine continued its own long-range campaign in parallel: Moscow mayor Sergey Sobyanin said **63 Ukrainian drones** were intercepted over Moscow Oblast during the latest exchange. The strikes extend a pattern seen two days earlier, when Russia hit Kyiv's Pochaina book market and a major steel plant, and Ukraine answered with roughly 600 drones toward Moscow and other Russian regions.
key_points: Russia fired a reported **128 drones** at Ukraine overnight, part of attacks that killed **9 and injured 43** in one day.
A **jet-powered 'Shahed-type' drone** hit a shopping center and post office near Odesa, injuring 7, including an **8-year-old child**.
A nearby shoe factory was also damaged; five of the injured needed hospital treatment.
Ukraine kept up its own strikes on Russia — Moscow's mayor said **63 Ukrainian drones** were shot down over Moscow Oblast.
The exchange extends the war's **largest reciprocal drone campaign in months**, first reported two days earlier.

depth.background: Since mid-August both sides have escalated **long-range drone and missile strikes** on targets far from the front line — Russia hitting Ukrainian cities and infrastructure, Ukraine hitting Moscow-area targets and Russian industry. Two days earlier, Russia had bombarded Kyiv's historic Pochaina book market and an ArcelorMittal steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, while Ukraine responded with roughly **600 drones** aimed at Moscow, in what officials called one of its largest aerial attacks of the war. Diplomacy over ending the war remains stalled.

thread.previously: We reported Russia hit Kyiv's Pochaina book market and a Kryvyi Rih steel plant, killing at least 19 combined, while Ukraine answered with roughly 600 drones toward Moscow in one of its largest attacks of the war.
thread.changed: The exchange has continued rather than cooled: a fresh overnight barrage killed 9 and injured 43 across Ukraine, including a jet-powered drone hitting a shopping center near Odesa, while Ukraine kept striking the Moscow region.

stories.title: Alex Albon extends his Williams contract through 2027, betting on the team despite its 2026 slump
stories.what_happened: Williams announced on **Tuesday, August 18** that Alex Albon has signed a **one-year contract extension**, formally committing him to the team through the end of the **2027 F1 season**. The move removes ambiguity created by exit clauses in his prior deal, which some in the paddock had read as leaving his future open given Williams' poor 2026 form. Team principal **James Vowles** said he was 'delighted' that Albon has 'continued to put his faith in Williams' despite this year's struggles. The announcement lands during F1's summer break, just before the sport resumes at the Dutch Grand Prix, and as Albon's current teammate Carlos Sainz's own contract situation for 2027 remains unresolved, with reports of him weighing a fresh Williams offer against other options including Aston Martin interest for Sergio Perez's old seat.
key_points: Williams confirmed **Alex Albon** signed a **one-year extension** keeping him at the team through the **2027 season**.
It comes as Williams has **slumped to 9th** in the constructors' standings, down from 5th in 2025.
Team principal **James Vowles** said he was 'delighted' Albon kept his faith in the team through the 'blip.'
The move resolves exit-clause uncertainty that had put Albon's own future in doubt.
It narrows the 2027 driver market just as teammate **Carlos Sainz's** own seat talks remain unresolved.

depth.background: **Alex Albon**, a British-born Thai driver, has been Williams' talisman during its multi-year rebuild since returning to F1 with the team in 2022, helping guide it back up the grid. Williams surged to **5th in the constructors' championship in 2025** but has slumped badly in 2026 with its FW48 car, dropping to 9th — a stumble team boss James Vowles has called a 'blip.' Albon's prior contract already carried language covering 2027, but built-in **exit clauses** left real uncertainty about whether he would stay.

stories.title: Houthis claim a missile strike on a Saudi warship and four escort vessels in the Red Sea
stories.what_happened: Houthi military spokesman **Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree** announced on August 17 that Yemeni forces fired ballistic missiles at a **Saudi military landing ship and four escort or patrol boats** in the Red Sea, off the port of Mocha near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Saree claimed the landing ship **"caught fire completely"** and that some of the escort vessels sank while others burned. The claim was carried by multiple outlets, including Iran's Press TV, the Jerusalem Post, and Middle East Eye, but as of this writing **no Saudi government, military, or coalition source has confirmed, denied, or otherwise addressed the specific incident** — a notable silence, since Saudi authorities have confirmed other Houthi attacks in the past. The claim follows the Houthis' July declaration of a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia, and comes less than a week after a separate, confirmed Houthi attack near the same strait killed six people on August 12.
key_points: Yemen's Houthi military spokesman claims **ballistic missiles** hit a Saudi landing ship and **four escort boats** off Mocha, near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait
The Houthis say the landing ship **"caught fire completely"** and some escorts sank — but **Saudi Arabia has issued no confirmation or denial**
The claim follows a Houthi-declared **naval blockade of Saudi Arabia** announced in July, in retaliation for what they call a Saudi-backed siege on Yemen
It comes just days after a separate, deadly Houthi attack near the same strait **killed six people** on August 12
No independent journalists or satellite imagery have verified any damage — this is currently a **one-sided claim**, not a confirmed event

depth.background: The Houthis are an Iran-aligned armed movement that controls much of northern **Yemen**, including the capital Sanaa, after a decade-long civil war against the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government. Since 2023 they have repeatedly used missiles and drones to attack shipping near the **Bab el-Mandeb Strait** — a narrow chokepoint at the southern end of the Red Sea that a huge share of Europe-Asia trade passes through — framing the attacks as solidarity campaigns tied to regional conflicts. In July 2026 they escalated further, declaring a formal **naval blockade against Saudi Arabia** itself, accusing Riyadh of enforcing a blockade on Yemen; Saudi Arabia denies this. This claimed strike would be the most serious naval escalation in that campaign so far, targeting a Saudi military vessel directly rather than commercial shipping.

stories.title: Ravindra Jadeja joins cricket's most exclusive all-rounder club — only the 4th player ever to reach 4,000 runs and 350 wickets
stories.what_happened: On **Day 3 of the Galle Test** against Sri Lanka (August 17), Ravindra Jadeja picked up his 350th Test wicket, making him the **first Indian left-arm bowler** to reach that mark — with the next-best Indian left-armer, Zaheer Khan, a distant second on 311. Combined with his batting tally, Jadeja simultaneously became the **4th player in the history of Test cricket** to record both 4,000 runs and 350 wickets, joining Kapil Dev (5,248 runs, 434 wickets), Ian Botham (5,200 runs, 383 wickets) and Daniel Vettori (4,531 runs, 362 wickets). He reached the milestone in his **90th Test**, the second-fastest of the four to do so, behind only Botham's 83 matches. He is also now the 5th Indian bowler overall past 350 Test wickets, joining Anil Kumble (619), Ravichandran Ashwin (537), Kapil Dev (434) and Harbhajan Singh (417). The feat came fittingly in **India's 600th-ever Test match**.
key_points: Jadeja became the **first Indian left-arm bowler** to reach 350 Test wickets, during Day 3 in Galle.
He's only the **4th player in Test history** — after Kapil Dev, Ian Botham and Daniel Vettori — to combine 4,000 runs and 350 wickets.
He reached the double in **90 Tests**, the second-fastest ever behind Botham's 83.
He's now the **5th Indian overall** to 350 Test wickets, behind Kumble, Ashwin, Kapil Dev and Harbhajan Singh.
The milestone came in India's **600th Test match**, adding symbolic weight to the achievement.

depth.background: Ravindra Jadeja, now **37**, debuted for India in 2012 and spent years being underestimated as 'just' a containing bowler and lower-order hitter, even as his numbers quietly piled up across more than a decade. The exclusive club of Test all-rounders who've reached both **4,000 runs and 350 wickets** includes some of the sport's greatest names — England's Ian Botham, South Africa/New Zealand great Daniel Vettori, and India's own Kapil Dev, long considered the gold standard of Indian all-round cricket. Reaching that double is rare because it demands both **longevity** (staying fit and selected for well over a decade) and genuine two-way excellence, not just being good at one skill.

stories.title: Nvidia backs up to $105 billion in financing for OpenAI's giant new Ohio data center
stories.what_happened: A securities filing revealed on **August 17** that Nvidia will guarantee **up to $105 billion** in financing tied to a new OpenAI data center campus at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in **Pike County, Ohio**. **SB Energy**, a SoftBank subsidiary, will build and operate the site and lease it to OpenAI for 20 years; Nvidia will be the site's exclusive chip supplier. Nvidia is separately investing **$1.5 billion** directly into SB Energy to back its build-out as an AI infrastructure developer, and SB Energy/SoftBank plan to add at least 10 gigawatts of new power generation with a further **$4.2 billion** invested in Ohio's power grid to support it. The first phase, 4.25 gigawatts of compute, is expected online in 2028, with an option for an additional 3.75 gigawatts later. The number is notably smaller than the roughly **$250 billion** guarantee Nvidia and OpenAI were reportedly discussing earlier this year, after the Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia was set to cut its exposure to under $120 billion amid investor concern about how much of its own balance sheet Nvidia was putting behind demand for its own chips. Nvidia's stock traded roughly flat on the news.
key_points: Nvidia will guarantee **up to $105 billion** in lease and power payments for a new OpenAI data center in Pike County, **Ohio**.
The site is being built by **SB Energy** (a SoftBank company), which will lease the finished campus to OpenAI for **20 years**.
Nvidia is also putting **$1.5 billion** directly into SB Energy itself, calling it a bet on AI-infrastructure building, not just chip sales.
The first phase brings **4.25 gigawatts** of computing power online in **2028**, with an option to nearly double that later.
This is a scaled-down version of an earlier plan that reportedly ran as high as a **$250 billion** guarantee, after investors pushed back on the size of Nvidia's exposure.

depth.background: OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, has been on a spending spree to secure the physical computing power — chips, buildings, and electricity — needed to keep training and running ever-larger AI models. Because building a data center this size costs tens of billions of dollars up front, OpenAI doesn't have the cash to pay for it outright, so it leans on partners like **Nvidia** to backstop the financing: essentially, Nvidia promises to make good on the lease and power payments if something goes wrong, which lets banks and investors feel safe lending the money to build the site. Nvidia benefits because it becomes the guaranteed, exclusive supplier of the chips that fill the finished data center — more AI infrastructure built anywhere means more Nvidia chips sold. This deal is part of a broader pattern this year of **circular-looking financing** in AI, where the same handful of companies (Nvidia, OpenAI, Microsoft, Oracle, SoftBank) keep investing in and lending to each other.

stories.title: Supreme Court pauses Allahabad High Court probe into Rahul Gandhi's assets
stories.what_happened: On **17 August 2026**, a Supreme Court bench led by **Chief Justice of India Surya Kant**, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, heard Gandhi's challenge to the Allahabad High Court's orders. The bench directed the High Court to **defer its scheduled August 20 hearing** until the Supreme Court examines the matter further, and ordered the CBI or any other investigating authority **not to submit any report** to the High Court in the meantime. During the hearing, the judges questioned why the High Court had passed its orders **without giving Gandhi a chance to be heard** — a basic fairness requirement in law. Gandhi has filed two petitions: one challenging the High Court's orders directly, and a separate **transfer petition** asking that the entire case be moved from the Allahabad High Court to the Delhi High Court. Both petitions were filed on August 7 and taken up together today.
key_points: SC tells Allahabad HC to **defer** its Aug 20 hearing
CBI, ED barred from filing any report **for now**
Complaint filed by a **Karnataka BJP worker** in 2026
Court asks why Gandhi wasn't given a **hearing** first
Gandhi also seeks to **transfer** the case to Delhi HC

depth.background: **Rahul Gandhi**, the Congress leader and **Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha** (India's lower house of Parliament), is facing a **disproportionate assets** complaint — an allegation that someone's wealth exceeds what their known, legal income can explain. The complaint was filed by **S. Vignesh Shishir**, a BJP worker from Karnataka. In **May 2026**, the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court ordered the **CBI** (India's federal police agency) and the **ED** (the agency that probes financial crimes and money laundering) to verify the complaint and report back; in July, unhappy with the CBI's response, the court demanded a senior officer personally file a fresh affidavit on the probe's progress.

stories.title: Gujarat High Court orders immediate transfer of Surat's DCP after video shows police publicly flogging handcuffed accused
stories.what_happened: On **July 14**, video footage emerged showing a Surat DCP and a group of policemen publicly slapping and beating **handcuffed accused persons** and parading them through the streets. A lawyer filed a written complaint, and a division bench of Chief Justice **Sunita Agarwal** and Justice **D N Ray** took up the matter as a suo motu Public Interest Litigation. On **August 17**, the court ordered DCP **Rajdeepsinh Nakum's immediate transfer**, saying it was necessary to ensure the ongoing investigation into the incident is impartial. The court noted the officer's conduct broke explicit government circulars prohibiting public beating and parading of the accused, and pointed to both the Supreme Court's **D K Basu** guidelines and the Gujarat HC's own 2022 findings in a similar Kheda flogging case.
key_points: Gujarat HC ordered the **immediate transfer** of Surat DCP Rajdeepsinh Nakum to ensure an impartial probe.
Video showed police **publicly slapping, beating and parading handcuffed accused persons** in Surat on July 14.
The court took up the case as a **suo motu PIL** — acting on its own, after a lawyer's written complaint.
Nakum allegedly violated **government circulars that ban public beating and parading** of the accused.
The order leans on the Supreme Court's **D K Basu ruling**, a landmark judgment on how police must treat people in custody.

depth.background: Public 'flogging' or parading of accused persons by police — sometimes filmed and shared as a show of toughness — has surfaced as a recurring controversy in Gujarat, including a 2022 incident in Kheda that also drew judicial criticism. India's Supreme Court set binding rules for how police must treat anyone in custody in its **1997 D K Basu vs State of West Bengal** judgment, which followed cases of custodial abuse and death. Those rules require police to identify themselves, inform a relative of an arrest, and avoid using force beyond what's needed to make an arrest — public beatings and parading violate this directly.

stories.title: India's unemployment rate falls to 5.1% in July as more women join the workforce
stories.what_happened: Government PLFS data released this week showed India's unemployment rate for people aged 15 and above fell to **5.1% in July**, down from **5.5% in June**, marking one of the lowest readings in recent months. The improvement was led by rural India, where unemployment dropped to **4.5%** from 5%, while the urban rate held roughly steady at **6.7%**, barely changed from June's 6.6%. Alongside the falling unemployment rate, the **Labour Force Participation Rate** rose to **55.4%** from 54.4% the prior month, meaning a larger share of the working-age population is now either employed or actively job-hunting — with the data pointing to more women joining the workforce as a key driver.
key_points: India's unemployment rate dropped to **5.1% in July**, down from **5.5% in June**.
Rural unemployment fell more sharply, to **4.5%** from 5%, while urban unemployment stayed almost flat at **6.7%**.
The **Labour Force Participation Rate** — the share of people working or looking for work — rose to **55.4%** from 54.4%.
The improvement is driven partly by **more women entering the workforce**, according to the government data.
The figures come from the government's monthly **PLFS** jobs survey.

depth.background: India tracks employment through the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**, a monthly government survey that is the country's main official gauge of how many working-age people have jobs, are looking for jobs, or have dropped out of the job market entirely. A falling unemployment rate on its own can be misleading if it just means discouraged people stopped looking for work — economists watch it alongside the **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** to see whether more people are actually engaging with the job market, not fewer.

stories.title: Mercedes says grid penalties for title leader Antonelli and George Russell are now 'almost inevitable'
stories.what_happened: Mercedes has acknowledged that both Antonelli and Russell will almost certainly need grid penalties in the second half of the 2026 season because reliability failures in the first half burned through their allotted engine components faster than planned. Antonelli is already on his **fourth set** of power-unit components and Russell his **third**, meaning any further replacement triggers a penalty. Rather than debate whether to take the hit, the team is strategizing about **which race weekend** minimizes the damage — Mercedes team principal **Toto Wolff** has floated the **Italian Grand Prix at Monza** as a candidate, reasoning that even a back-of-grid start there is more recoverable than at a track like Zandvoort, Antonelli's title rival's home race. Mercedes has stated it will **not prioritize Antonelli's title campaign** over Russell when deciding the order.
key_points: Mercedes admits both **Kimi Antonelli** and **George Russell** will need grid penalties before the season ends.
Antonelli, the **championship leader with 219 points**, is already on his **fourth set** of engine components.
A grid penalty usually means starting **around 10 places back** — costly in a tight title fight.
Mercedes is choosing **when**, not if, to take the hit, with **Monza** floated as one option.
The team says it **won't favor Antonelli's title bid** over Russell when deciding whose penalty comes first.

depth.background: In Formula 1, each driver is allotted a limited number of engine parts (the 'power unit') for the entire season under FIA rules. Teams try to make each part last as long as possible, because fitting an extra one beyond the allowance triggers an automatic grid penalty at the next race — typically dropping a driver back around 10 places on the starting grid. **Kimi Antonelli**, a rookie in his first full title-contending season, currently leads the drivers' championship with **219 points**, a **50-point lead** over Lewis Hamilton.

stories.title: Iran's Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks send oil higher again, dragging down the Sensex, Nifty and rupee
stories.what_happened: A fresh wave of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz has pushed oil prices back up and rattled Indian markets. Starting **August 8**, an ADNOC tanker was struck by a missile the UAE blamed on Iran's IRGC; by **August 13-14**, two more ADNOC vessels had been hit — the UAE's Foreign Ministry called it 'piracy' and accused Iran of using the Strait as 'a tool of economic coercion.' Brent crude rose from **$86.91 a barrel on August 14 to $88.85 on August 17**, more than 5% in a week, as hopes of reopening the Strait faded and shipping traffic collapsed to just 8-15 transits a day versus roughly 130 before the conflict. Indian markets felt it directly: the **Sensex fell 71 points on Friday** and opened **287 points lower today (-0.37%) at 77,722**, with the Nifty down 61 points to 24,305 and PSU bank stocks under particular pressure, as traders cited renewed Hormuz-driven oil anxiety and foreign fund outflows. The rupee, which hit an all-time low of 96.84/USD in May during an earlier escalation, is trading near 95.4/USD — still vulnerable given India imports about 70% of its crude in dollars.
key_points: Brent crude climbed from **$86.91 to $88.85 a barrel** this week after **three attacks on ADNOC tankers** in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Sensex opened today down **287 points (-0.37%)** at 77,722; the Nifty fell **61 points** to 24,305.
Shipping traffic through the Strait has collapsed to **8-15 vessels a day**, down from about **130 a day** before the conflict.
India imports about **70% of its crude**, so a sustained oil spike widens its import bill and pressures the **rupee**, trading near 95.4/USD.
A 10% rise in global crude can lift India's headline inflation by roughly **0.2 percentage points**, trade economists estimate.

depth.background: This is the latest flare-up in a US/Israel-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz that has run since roughly February 2026 and repeatedly disrupted the world's most important oil chokepoint — a corridor that normally carries close to a quarter of the world's seaborne crude. The UAE's state oil company ADNOC has been targeted three times in the past week; Abu Dhabi has accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard of the attacks and called them 'piracy' and a violation of a UN Security Council resolution. India has partly cushioned itself from earlier spikes by buying discounted Russian crude, which now supplies roughly half its imports.

stories.title: A hotel fire kills at least 7 Shravan pilgrims in West Bengal's Tarapith; the owner is arrested as claims of a blocked exit emerge
stories.what_happened: A fire broke out around **5 a.m.** at the five-storey **Hotel Bideshini**, located beside a pond near the Tarapith police station, reportedly triggered by a **short circuit** that spread rapidly through the building. Most guests — including several children — were asleep at the time; eyewitnesses said smoke filled the area within minutes. Police and fire department personnel rescued **22 people**, but at least **7 pilgrims died**, with some later reports putting the toll as high as 8. The victims had travelled from different districts to perform puja during Shravan. Hotel owner **Kalyan Paul** was **arrested**, and police are investigating whether the hotel's firefighting systems met safety rules. Multiple survivors say a rear exit door was locked, preventing escape — directly contradicting claims Paul made earlier the same morning. Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** announced **ex-gratia payments of ₹2 lakh** for each victim's next of kin and **₹50,000** for the injured, from the PM's National Relief Fund.
key_points: A fire tore through **Hotel Bideshini** in **Tarapith, Birbhum district**, around **5 a.m.** on Monday
At least **7 people died**, most reports say, all of them **pilgrims** — some later reports put the toll at 8
**22 people were rescued** by police and fire crews as smoke filled the building within minutes
Hotel owner **Kalyan Paul** has been **arrested**; police are probing whether fire-safety rules were followed
Guests allege a **rear exit was locked**, contradicting the owner's earlier claims

depth.background: Tarapith is one of West Bengal's most visited pilgrimage towns, built around a centuries-old Kali temple, and draws heavy footfall during religious observances — the fire broke out on the **third Monday of Shravan**, a Hindu holy month when devotees travel from across the region to perform puja (worship rituals) there. Small pilgrimage-town hotels in India have repeatedly come under scrutiny for weak fire-safety compliance, a recurring issue after past hotel-fire tragedies elsewhere in the country.

stories.title: Carlos Sainz reportedly rejects Williams' 30 million euro offer, reopening his 2027 options
stories.what_happened: According to reports from Spanish outlet Marca and multiple F1 outlets, Sainz turned down Williams' latest contract proposal, said to be worth around **30 million euros a season**, because he wants a shorter-term deal that keeps his options open rather than locking in long-term. That has left talks ongoing rather than concluded, with Sainz reportedly considering whether **Red Bull, McLaren or Audi** could offer a more competitive package — with some reports suggesting he may be waiting to see whether Verstappen leaves Red Bull, which would open a seat there. The rejection has immediately revived talk that **Sergio Perez**, who Cadillac's leadership had firmly said would stay for 2027, could yet end up in the Williams conversation again.
key_points: Carlos Sainz has reportedly **rejected** a new Williams contract offer worth roughly **30 million euros per season**.
Sainz reportedly wants a **shorter deal with flexibility** to leave if a stronger seat opens up, rather than a long-term commitment.
Speculation now points to **Red Bull, McLaren or Audi** as possible alternative destinations for Sainz.
Some reports suggest Sainz is **waiting to see where Max Verstappen lands** before committing to his own next move.
The rejection **reopens the door** for Sergio Perez, who had been widely expected to lose out on the Williams seat.

depth.background: Sainz left Ferrari for Williams in 2025 and had appeared close to a new multi-year Williams deal for 2027, a move that was widely read as closing off Sergio Perez's main route back into a competitive seat after his exit from Red Bull. With this year's driver market unusually fluid — tied up in Verstappen's own Red Bull exit-clause saga — several drivers have reportedly been holding off on signing extensions until the bigger dominoes fall.

thread.previously: We reported that Carlos Sainz was closing in on a new Williams deal for 2027 — a move that would effectively shut Sergio Perez out of that seat, since Williams was seen as his likeliest landing spot after Cadillac.
thread.changed: That deal has now stalled: multiple reports say Sainz has turned down Williams' latest offer, reportedly worth around 30 million euros a season, because he wants a shorter contract with an exit route rather than a long-term commitment — reopening speculation about Red Bull, McLaren, Audi, and reviving Perez's own hopes of a Williams seat.

stories.title: Toto Wolff backs F1's V8 return as a 'purist' — but says the FIA's timeline is unrealistic
stories.what_happened: In an interview, Mercedes team principal **Toto Wolff** said he supports the idea of F1 returning to **V8 engines** in a future rules cycle, calling it 'the best consensus' and adding 'as a purist, I like it.' He said his preferred version would be a naturally aspirated V8 paired with some form of **energy-recovery system** — a lighter version of the hybrid technology used today — and built to run on **sustainable fuel**, rather than a straightforward throwback engine. However, Wolff pushed back on FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem's push for a **2029** introduction, calling that timeline unrealistic: 'Most manufacturers don't want to pay for a double program. A new engine in two years would cause costs to explode,' since teams would effectively have to develop two engines — today's and the new one — simultaneously.
key_points: Mercedes boss **Toto Wolff** says he supports F1 bringing back **naturally aspirated V8 engines**
FIA president **Mohammed Ben Sulayem** wants the switch as early as **2029**, ending the turbo-hybrid era that began in **2014**
Wolff calls that timeline **unrealistic**, warning a new engine in two years would make costs 'explode'
He wants the V8 paired with an **energy-recovery system** and **sustainable fuel**, not a pure retro engine
Most manufacturers reportedly don't want to fund **two engine programmes at once**

depth.background: Formula 1 has used complex, expensive **turbo-hybrid V6 engines** since 2014 — powerful and efficient, but criticised by some fans and insiders for sounding quieter and being harder (and pricier) to build than the raw V8s and V10s of earlier eras. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has been pushing to bring back a simpler, louder V8 for F1's next big engine cycle, aiming for as soon as **2029 or 2030/31**. Manufacturers like Mercedes, Ferrari, Honda and Audi have poured billions into today's hybrid engines and would need to plan and fund whatever comes next years in advance.

stories.title: South Korea and the US launch Ulchi Freedom Shield 2026, drilling for a North Korea reshaped by its own troops' combat experience in Ukraine
stories.what_happened: The US and South Korea began Ulchi Freedom Shield 2026 today, an **11-day exercise running August 17-27** that combines computer-simulated command-post training with live field maneuvers and South Korea's civil-emergency readiness drills. Around **18,000 South Korean troops** are taking part alongside American forces drawn from the roughly 28,500 US personnel stationed in the country. For the first time, the exercise has been explicitly redesigned around scenarios involving **drone warfare, GPS jamming, and cyberattacks** — a direct response to the real battlefield experience North Korean troops picked up fighting for Russia in Ukraine. This year's drills will also include a joint assessment of whether South Korea's military has reached the **'full operational capability'** needed to eventually take over wartime operational control from the US. In the run-up, North Korea fired what Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff assessed as a midrange ballistic missile from the Wonsan area on **August 12** — its **11th suspected ballistic missile test of 2026** — which flew roughly 700km before splashing into the sea, just six days after a prior launch. Pyongyang has formally condemned the drills as a rehearsal for 'aggressive war' and warned it will respond with a 'new level of deterrent' and 'overwhelming force,' while separately vowing to further strengthen its nuclear arsenal.
key_points: About **18,000 South Korean troops** join US forces for the **11-day** Ulchi Freedom Shield drill, Aug 17-27.
For the first time, the drills are built around **drone warfare, GPS jamming, and cyberattacks** — lessons North Korea learned fighting for Russia in Ukraine.
North Korea calls the exercise a rehearsal for **'aggressive war'** and threatens to respond with **'overwhelming force.'**
Pyongyang fired its **11th ballistic missile of 2026** on Aug 12, days before the drills began.
The drills double as a test of whether Seoul is ready to take over **wartime operational control** from the US.

depth.background: Ulchi Freedom Shield is the flagship annual joint military exercise between the United States and South Korea, run every year (with pandemic-era gaps) since succeeding the older 'Ulchi Freedom Guardian' drills. **North Korea has denounced every edition for years** as a rehearsal for invasion, and typically times missile tests to coincide with the drill period as a show of defiance. What's different in 2026 is that thousands of North Korean troops have spent the past two years fighting alongside Russian forces in Ukraine — gaining real combat exposure to **drone swarms, GPS spoofing, and cyberattacks** that Pyongyang's own military can now bring home. The drills also touch a decades-old sovereignty question for South Korea: when it will take over **wartime operational control (OPCON)** of its own forces, which the US-led Combined Forces Command has held since the Korean War armistice.

stories.title: Babar Azam declared fully fit, cleared to lead Pakistan against England after hand-injury scare
stories.what_happened: Following the finger blow in the Kent warm-up match, Babar Azam was advised rest and did not bat further in that fixture, sparking concern about his availability for the opening Test. The Pakistan Cricket Board said on **August 17** that Babar has since been through training in Leeds, has been **cleared by the medical team**, and returned to full training at **Headingley**. He is now confirmed fit and available to captain Pakistan in the upcoming three-match Test series against England, with the series opener at Headingley approaching.
key_points: Babar Azam has been **cleared by Pakistan's medical team** and returned to full training in Leeds.
He's now confirmed **fit and available** to captain Pakistan in the 3-match Test series against England.
The scare came from a blow to his finger during a **warm-up match** at Kent, off a delivery from pacer Manny Lumsden.
PCB had called the earlier withdrawal from the warm-up game **purely precautionary**, not serious damage.
It removes doubt just before the **first Test at Headingley, Leeds** begins.

depth.background: Babar Azam is Pakistan's Test captain and a central figure in the batting line-up, so any injury doubt around him ahead of a major series carries outsized weight. He was hurt on **August 14-15** during a tour warm-up match against a Professional County Club Select XI at Kent, when he was struck on the hand while batting and retired hurt after scoring 5 off 17 balls. At the time, the Pakistan Cricket Board said the decision to withdraw him from the rest of that practice game was a precaution, based on the team doctor's assessment, and stressed there was **no serious damage**.

thread.previously: Babar Azam was struck on the hand during a tour warm-up match at Kent and was withdrawn from the rest of the game as a precaution, casting doubt on his availability for the first Test.
thread.changed: Pakistan's medical team has now fully cleared him after training in Leeds, and he is confirmed fit to captain the side in the Headingley Test.
