stories.title: One of three missing workers found dead as Chamoli tunnel rescue enters its third day
stories.what_happened: Water and debris suddenly surged into an under-construction tail-race tunnel at the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti hydroelectric project near Mayapur-Pipalkoti around **7 pm on August 13**, after a landslide or underground cavity opened roughly 1.4-1.5 km inside the tunnel. **22 workers** were trapped; **19 were pulled out** during an overnight rescue operation, but 7 were confirmed dead and 3 remained missing the following day. On **Saturday, August 15**, one of the three missing workers was located and declared dead at hospital, bringing the confirmed toll to **8 dead**, with 2 workers still unaccounted for. Rescue teams — including the NDRF, SDRF and ITBP — have only advanced a few hundred metres into the tunnel because the water level inside remains around a metre or higher, and continuous rainfall is hampering efforts to pump it out and clear debris. Uttarakhand's disaster management minister, Madan Kaushik, visited the site and said search efforts would continue without pause until the remaining workers are found.
key_points: One of the **three workers still missing** after a Uttarakhand hydropower tunnel disaster was found Saturday and **declared dead at hospital** — taking the toll to 8, with 2 still missing.
The disaster struck on **August 13**, when water and debris rushed into a tunnel at the **Vishnugad-Pipalkoti hydroelectric project**, trapping 22 workers about 1.4-1.5 km inside.
**19 workers were pulled out alive** in the hours after the collapse; rescuers are still trying to reach the last two, over a kilometre inside the flooded tunnel.
Continuous rain and a **water level still around a metre or more** inside the tunnel are slowing NDRF, SDRF, ITBP and police rescue teams.
Uttarakhand's disaster management minister visited the site and said the **"rescue will continue till the end."**

depth.background: The Vishnugad-Pipalkoti project is a **444-megawatt hydroelectric dam** being built by **THDC India Limited** on the Alaknanda river in Chamoli district — a Himalayan region that has seen repeated tunnel and glacier disasters, most notably the deadly 2021 Tapovan glacial-burst flood that killed dozens of workers in a similar under-construction tunnel nearby. Tunnelling through the young, geologically unstable Himalayas is inherently risky: a sudden landslide or hidden underground cavity can let in enormous volumes of water and debris with almost no warning — which investigators believe is what happened here.

stories.title: Relentless storms flood the US Midwest; Indiana declares disaster and asks for federal help
stories.what_happened: A stretch of thunderstorms dumped more than **11 inches of rain** on parts of Indiana and Ohio over the past week, triggering flash flooding on top of damage from tornadoes and a derecho earlier in the week. As of Saturday afternoon, **at least three people had died** and **more than 150,000 customers had lost power** across the affected states. Indiana Governor **Mike Braun** declared a statewide disaster emergency, activated the **Indiana National Guard**, and formally requested a presidential emergency declaration through FEMA to bring in federal funding and resources. The National Weather Service said additional storms were expected to move through the Ohio Valley, the Midwest, and the central Appalachians through at least Sunday, threatening fresh flooding in areas that hadn't yet had a chance to drain.
key_points: At least **3 people have died** and over **150,000 lost power** as flooding hit Indiana and Ohio.
Some areas got more than **11 inches of rain in a week**, on top of tornadoes and a derecho.
Indiana Gov. **Mike Braun** declared a **statewide disaster emergency** and called out the **National Guard**.
Braun has asked **FEMA** for a presidential emergency declaration to unlock federal money and resources.
Forecasters warn **more heavy rain is coming through Sunday**, on ground that's already soaked.

depth.background: Indiana and the wider Ohio Valley have been stuck under a **relentless stretch of thunderstorms** this week, layered on top of tornadoes and a **derecho** — a fast-moving band of destructive straight-line winds — that had already battered the region. Ground that was still soaked from earlier storms had barely started to dry out before this new round of rain arrived. It's part of a broader pattern of unusually intense, slow-moving rain events hitting the US interior in recent years, the kind that overwhelm drainage systems built for an earlier, gentler climate.

stories.title: Bangladesh closes in on a stunning Test win as Australia slump to 161 for 4 following on in Darwin
stories.what_happened: Bangladesh posted a commanding first-innings total of **426**, built through the middle order, while paceman **Josh Hazlewood** was Australia's standout bowler with figures of **6 for 89**. In reply, Australia collapsed to just **198 all out**, handing Bangladesh a **228-run lead** and forcing Australia to follow on and bat again immediately. Batting a second time, Australia lost **Steven Smith**, one of the world's best Test batters, caught off spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz**, and closed the third day's play on **161 for 4**, with **Cameron Green (43 not out)** and **Alex Carey (19 not out)** still at the crease — still trailing Bangladesh's first-innings total by **67 runs**.
key_points: Bangladesh posted **426** in their first innings, a **228-run lead**, powered by **Josh Hazlewood's 6-89**
Australia were bowled out for just **198** in reply, forcing them to bat again
Australia closed Day 3 at **161 for 4**, still trailing by **67 runs**
Star batter **Steven Smith** was dismissed, caught off spinner **Mehidy Hasan Miraz**

depth.background: Bangladesh have never won a Test match in Australia, and Australia are one of the most dominant home Test sides in the sport — so any contest that puts Australia under real pressure on their own soil is unusual. This is the first Test of a two-match series in Darwin, played on a pitch that has clearly favored batting more than expected, with Bangladesh's middle order cashing in heavily in the first innings.

stories.title: Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out of the Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games with a hamstring tear — Pratika Rawal steps in
stories.what_happened: Rodrigues **tore her right hamstring** — described as a 'high-grade' tear, the more serious end of the injury scale — while playing for Southern Brave in The Hundred on **August 3**. After medical assessment, India's Women's Selection Committee ruled her out of both the upcoming **Women's Asia Cup**, which runs from **August 28 to September 13** in Dubai, and the **Asian Games** later this year. **Pratika Rawal**, who has previously played Test cricket for India, has been named as her replacement, earning a recall to the white-ball squad. The rest of the squad remains largely settled around captain **Harmanpreet Kaur** and vice-captain **Smriti Mandhana**.
key_points: Rodrigues suffered a **high-grade right hamstring tear** playing for Southern Brave in **The Hundred** on August 3.
She is ruled out of both the **Women's Asia Cup (Aug 28–Sep 13)** and the **Asian Games**.
**Pratika Rawal** has been named her replacement, earning a recall to the squad.
**Harmanpreet Kaur** continues as captain with **Smriti Mandhana** as vice-captain.
It's the second major batting reshuffle in the squad, after 18-year-old **G. Kamalini** was added as second wicketkeeper.

depth.background: Jemimah Rodrigues is one of India's most important middle-order batters in white-ball cricket and had been named in India's squad for the **Women's Asia Cup 2026** in the UAE, a tournament India has dominated with seven titles historically. She'd been playing in **The Hundred**, England's short-format franchise league, for Southern Brave — a common pre-tournament tune-up for international players — when she picked up the injury.

stories.title: Babar Azam hit on the hand in Pakistan's last England warm-up, fitness doubt before Leeds Test
stories.what_happened: Babar Azam was struck on the right hand by a delivery from pace bowler **Manny Lumsden** on the final ball of the 39th over on day two of Pakistan's warm-up match against a Professional County Club Select XI at Kent County Cricket Ground in Beckenham. He had scored just 5 runs at the time. Pakistan's team doctor examined him and advised he take no further part in the match as a precaution, rather than because of a confirmed serious injury. The Pakistan Cricket Board said Babar is scheduled to join the full squad's training session at Headingley on **August 17**, the Monday before the first Test against England begins on **August 19**.
key_points: **Babar Azam** was struck on the right hand by a delivery from pacer **Manny Lumsden** on day two in Beckenham.
Pakistan's team doctor pulled him out of the rest of the practice match **as a precaution**.
It's the **second time in a month** Babar has been hit on the hand, after a similar blow vs West Indies.
He's set to train at **Headingley on August 17**, two days before the **first Test against England** begins.

depth.background: Babar Azam is Pakistan's Test captain and their most important batter heading into a three-match series against England, starting August 19 at Headingley in Leeds and continuing at Lord's and The Oval. Pakistan were playing a three-day practice match against a Professional County Club Select XI in Beckenham to sharpen up before the series. Babar had already taken a similar blow to the hand during Pakistan's recent Test series against the West Indies, making this the second such scare in under a month.

stories.title: Devdutt Padikkal smashes a maiden Test century as India dominate day one of their historic 600th Test
stories.what_happened: India chose to bat first on winning the toss and dominated the opening day of the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle. Opener **Devdutt Padikkal** anchored the innings, reaching his maiden Test century off 134 balls and finishing the day unbeaten on **118**. He shared a **150-run partnership** with **KL Rahul**, who brought up his half-century before retiring hurt on **77** in the final session. Sri Lanka's only breakthrough came when spinner **Prabath Jayasuriya** dismissed captain **Shubman Gill** for 16, caught at mid-off attempting a lofted drive. India closed the day strongly placed at **273 for 2**, with **Rishabh Pant** unbeaten on 18 alongside Padikkal.
key_points: **Devdutt Padikkal** scored a maiden Test century, finishing day one unbeaten on **118**.
India closed play at **273/2** after choosing to bat first at Galle.
Padikkal and **KL Rahul** put on a **150-run partnership** before Rahul retired hurt on 77.
Captain **Shubman Gill** was the only big wicket to fall, out for 16 to Prabath Jayasuriya.
**Rishabh Pant** was unbeaten on 18 at the close alongside Padikkal.

depth.background: This is India's 600th Test match — a milestone only one other team (England) had reached before, and the first for any Asian side. India opted to bowl first when they won the toss (as covered earlier), leaving uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi out of the XI, with Jasprit Bumrah already ruled out of the series through injury. Devdutt Padikkal, a 24-year-old left-hander with a strong domestic first-class record, had played Tests before without converting a start into a century — making today's knock his first three-figure score at this level.

stories.title: Afghanistan complete a dominant series sweep over Ireland as Rahmat Shah blazes an unbeaten 143
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan had already wrapped up the 5-match ODI series 3-0 after the fourth game, then extended their dominance further by winning the fifth and final match at Stormont too, with Rahmat Shah's unbeaten 143 the standout innings. The result capped a lopsided series in which Ireland struggled to compete with Afghanistan's batting and bowling depth throughout.
key_points: Afghanistan won the **5th and final ODI** at Stormont, Belfast, having already sealed the **5-match series 3-0** after the 4th game.
**Rahmat Shah** finished unbeaten on **143 off 133 balls**, anchoring Afghanistan's innings in the decider.
The series was played under the shadow of protest calls from **Amnesty International**, which objected to Ireland hosting Afghanistan's men's team given Taliban restrictions on women's cricket there.
Afghanistan extended their dominance on Irish soil, continuing a strong run of form in the **One-Day International (ODI)** format.

depth.background: Afghanistan's men's cricket team continues to compete internationally even though the Taliban government at home bans women from playing the sport — a contradiction that has repeatedly drawn criticism from human-rights groups and reignited debate over whether the International Cricket Council (ICC) should restrict Afghanistan's participation. Ireland had already faced calls to reconsider hosting this series before a ball was bowled.

thread.changed: The series has now concluded — Afghanistan completed a 3-0 series sweep and then won the fifth and final ODI too, with Rahmat Shah's unbeaten century the headline performance.

stories.title: Alpine boss Flavio Briatore rules out chasing a 'monster' star hire, says the team needs technical consolidation instead
stories.what_happened: Speaking about Alpine's ongoing rebuild, Briatore said the team will not chase a 'monster high-profile' figure to lead its technical department, arguing Enstone's own history shows it can develop such talent internally rather than buy it in. 'For us, it's a question of consolidating the technical side because now we have the engine, and now we need to improve our technology quality in the team,' he said. Alpine has already brought in former Ferrari and McLaren technical chief David Sanchez as executive technical director, ex-FIA figure Jason Sommerville as his deputy, and Kimi Raikkonen's former Ferrari race engineer Dave Greenwood as racing director. Briatore said that when he arrived, the situation was difficult, with frequent staff departures and management changes, and that building a stable, strong technical team matters more now than one big-name hire.
key_points: Briatore said Alpine will **not** sign a 'monster high-profile' technical figure, betting instead on **consolidating** the team it already has.
Alpine has already added ex-Ferrari/McLaren technical chief **David Sanchez**, former FIA figure **Jason Sommerville**, and ex-Ferrari race engineer **Dave Greenwood**.
Briatore, Alpine's **de facto team boss** since Oliver Oakes' shock resignation, says the priority now is **quality and consistency**, not another big name.
Alpine has climbed from **10th to 5th** in the constructors' standings in 2026 after switching to a customer Mercedes engine.

depth.background: Alpine's Enstone-based team has churned through management in recent years, including the shock resignation of team principal Oliver Oakes in May 2025, after which **Flavio Briatore** — in his third stint with the team — stepped in as de facto boss. For 2026, Alpine switched from works Renault engines to a customer Mercedes power unit, which has coincided with a marked improvement in results.

stories.title: India vice-captain KL Rahul forced off with severe cramps in Galle — a fitness scare that revives India's rotation worries
stories.what_happened: KL Rahul was forced to retire hurt on **77 off 162 balls** during the opening day of India's first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, after suffering severe cramps that spread through his body. He first received treatment from the team physio after a cramp surfaced in his right forearm during the 51st over; things worsened from there as he felt contractions in his left hand and wrist, and muscle spasms in his legs, forcing him off the field before the tea interval. His exit ended a **150-run partnership** for the second wicket with Devdutt Padikkal, his Karnataka teammate; India captain **Shubman Gill** came in to replace him at the crease, with the team well-placed at 197/1 at the time. Early reports describe the issue as severe cramping rather than a diagnosed muscle or structural injury, and India is hopeful it was a case of exhaustion after a marathon innings in humid conditions rather than anything more serious.
key_points: KL Rahul retired hurt on **77** after severe cramps spread from his forearm to his hand, wrist and legs during Day 1 in Galle.
It ended a **150-run partnership** with Devdutt Padikkal, his Karnataka teammate, with **Shubman Gill** coming in to bat instead.
Early reports describe **cramping, not a diagnosed injury** — India hopes it's a case of exhaustion after a long, humid innings.
It adds to a season of fitness scares for India's top order, coming weeks after **Jasprit Bumrah's** own shock Sri Lanka Test withdrawal.
Rahul's fitness for the **2nd Test in Colombo (Aug 23-27)** is now the immediate question for team management.

depth.background: KL Rahul is India's vice-captain and one of its most experienced batters, currently opening in the ongoing Test series against Sri Lanka. India has already been managing fitness concerns this series — frontline fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah pulled out of the tour in a shock, last-minute withdrawal that sparked its own internal blame game inside the BCCI. A cramping issue for the vice-captain, even a minor one, lands in the middle of an already fitness-anxious campaign for the team.

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton says he feels 'released' at Ferrari after 'shouting from the top of the mountain' for changes
stories.what_happened: In comments reported by RacingNews365, Hamilton described how he now feels 'released' to do what he 'does best' after having pushed hard — 'shouting from the top of the mountain' — for changes he felt Ferrari needed to make. He said team principal Fred Vasseur has been instrumental in working with him to implement those changes, which has 'released' him to focus on driving rather than fighting for structural fixes. At the summer break, Hamilton sits second in the drivers' championship, 59 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, with one win and four further podiums from the season's first 11 rounds — a marked contrast to his difficult first year at Maranello in 2025.
key_points: Hamilton says he now feels **'released'** to perform after pushing Ferrari to make internal changes he wanted.
He credits team principal **Fred Vasseur** for working with him to make those changes happen.
At the summer break, Hamilton sits **2nd in the drivers' championship**, 59 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, with his **first Ferrari win** at the Spanish Grand Prix.
It's a sharp turnaround from his **difficult debut season** at Ferrari in 2025.

depth.background: Hamilton joined Ferrari for 2025 after over a decade at Mercedes, but his first season in red was widely seen as a struggle as he adapted to a new team and car. Heading into 2026, he has pushed publicly and internally for changes to how Ferrari operates around him, and 2026 has looked like a genuine turnaround — highlighted by his maiden win for the team at the **Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix**.

stories.title: Government opens one-time window for small taxpayers to declare hidden foreign assets
stories.what_happened: The CBDT notified the **Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers – Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026 (FAST-DS)**, which takes effect today, August 16, and stays open until **December 31, 2026**. It gives people who were Indian residents in the relevant year a one-time chance to voluntarily disclose foreign assets or income they failed to report. Under Category 1, undisclosed foreign assets/income up to **₹1 crore** in aggregate can be declared by paying 30% tax plus an equal penalty amount — an effective **60%** levy. Under Category 2, foreign assets bought with already-taxed money but never disclosed, valued up to **₹5 crore**, can be declared for a flat fee of **₹1 lakh**. Declarations must be filed electronically in Form 1, with March 31, 2026 fixed as the valuation date for computing asset values, and successful declarants get immunity from Black Money Act prosecution and penalty on the disclosed items.
key_points: New disclosure scheme **FAST-DS 2026** opens today, closes **December 31**
Covers undisclosed foreign assets/income up to **₹1 crore** in one track
Second track allows assets up to **₹5 crore** for a flat **₹1 lakh** fee
Effective tax on declared money can reach **60%** under the main track
Aimed at students, tech employees and NRIs who missed reporting foreign holdings

depth.background: Indian tax law requires residents to list every foreign bank account, stock, ESOP or property in a special section of their income-tax return called **Schedule FA**. Missing this — even by accident — can trigger India's strict **Black Money Act, 2015**, which allows heavy penalties and even prosecution regardless of intent. The scheme was first flagged in the **Union Budget 2026-27** as relief specifically for smaller, often unintentional, defaulters rather than large-scale tax evaders. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has now notified the actual rules that bring it into force.

stories.title: Europe declares 'high wildfire alert' as fires force fresh evacuations in France, Spain, Germany and Croatia amid record heat
stories.what_happened: On Saturday, EU Commission President **Ursula von der Leyen** said Europe was on 'high wildfire alert,' with growing pressure now on Eastern European countries too, and confirmed the EU's Copernicus satellite system was actively mapping fires in Spain, Albania, Greece, France, Germany and Serbia. In **France**, roughly 100 more residents and holidaymakers were evacuated near Luglon in the Landes region from a fire burning since Thursday. In **Spain**, about 1,000 people were evacuated in the Aragón region, where a fire has burned over 15,000 hectares. In **Germany**, all 1,800 residents of the village of Gey, near Cologne, were evacuated after a fire in the nearby Hürtgen forest threatened it, with 1,400 firefighters deployed. In **Croatia**, more than 1,000 people were evacuated near the coastal town of Omiš, with a separate fire also burning on the island of Dugi Otok. Seasonally, this adds to a toll that had already reached at least 17 civilian deaths, 8 firefighter/crew deaths, and around 330,000 people displaced across Spain and France by early August.
key_points: EU chief **Ursula von der Leyen** put Europe on 'high wildfire alert', with mounting pressure now spreading to **Eastern Europe** too.
Germany evacuated an **entire village of 1,800 people** near Cologne as a forest fire threatened it; **1,400 firefighters** were deployed.
Spain evacuated **1,000 people** in Aragón, where a single fire has burned more than **15,000 hectares**.
This summer's fires have already killed at least **17 civilians and 8 firefighters/crew**, and displaced **~330,000 people** across Spain and France alone.
The EU's largest-ever firefighting deployment — **22 aircraft, 5 helicopters, 777 firefighters** — is now active across 12 countries.

depth.background: Southern and central Europe has been in an active, worsening wildfire season since early July 2026, driven by an extended heatwave and drought that the EU's own Joint Research Centre flagged on August 12 as fueling 'extraordinary wildfires.' The EU built up a shared firefighting system, **rescEU**, plus a new **300-strong rapid-reaction firefighting force** launched in February 2026, specifically because individual countries kept getting overwhelmed in recent fire seasons. This mid-August flare-up is a fresh escalation on top of an already record-bad summer.

stories.title: Death toll in Uttarakhand's Pipalkoti tunnel collapse climbs to 8, two workers still trapped
stories.what_happened: The accident occurred on Thursday when debris and water suddenly surged into the under-construction THDC tunnel, trapping 22 workers inside. By Saturday, rescue teams had recovered another body, taking the confirmed death toll to **eight**, while **two workers remained missing**. Uttarakhand's Disaster Management Minister **Madan Kaushik** said the rescue operation would 'continue till the end,' while local officials said crews were battling **high water levels** and had so far only been able to reach a few hundred metres from the site of the collapse. NDRF, SDRF and local police teams remain on site searching for the two still unaccounted for.
key_points: Rescuers recovered **another body** on Saturday, taking the confirmed death toll to **eight**.
**Two workers** remain missing and trapped inside the under-construction tunnel.
The accident happened when **debris and water burst into** a hydroelectric tunnel being built by state-run **THDC**, initially trapping **22 workers**.
Rescue teams (NDRF, SDRF, police) say **high water levels** inside the tunnel are slowing the search, with crews able to reach only a few hundred metres in.

depth.background: The collapse happened at the **Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project**, an under-construction tunnel being built by the state-run **Tehri Hydro Development Corporation (THDC)** in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand — a Himalayan state that regularly sees flash floods and landslides during the monsoon. It is one of several deadly monsoon disasters to hit the wider region this season, alongside flooding and landslides reported elsewhere in Uttarakhand and neighboring states.

thread.previously: We reported that one of three workers missing after a tunnel collapse at a hydroelectric project in Chamoli, Uttarakhand, had been found dead as the rescue operation entered its third day.
thread.changed: Rescue teams recovered **another body** on Saturday, taking the confirmed death toll to **eight**, while **two workers remain trapped** and the search is being slowed by **high water levels** inside the tunnel.

stories.title: Josh Hazlewood becomes just the ninth Australian to reach 300 Test wickets
stories.what_happened: During Australia's first Test against Bangladesh in Darwin, **Josh Hazlewood took a six-wicket haul**, dismissing Mominul Haque, Najmul Shanto, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Hasan Mahmud, Taijul Islam and Ebadot Hossain, which carried him past **300 Test wickets** for his career. He becomes the **ninth Australian** to reach the milestone, and joins **Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc** as the fourth member of Australia's current attack to do so — the first time in Test history that four bowlers from the same attack have all individually passed 300 wickets while playing together. His career bowling average of **24.02** ranks behind only Glenn McGrath, Pat Cummins and Dennis Lillee among Australians with 300-plus Test wickets.
key_points: Hazlewood took **six wickets** in an innings against Bangladesh in Darwin to pass the milestone.
He's only the **ninth Australian bowler ever** to reach 300 Test wickets.
He joins **Nathan Lyon, Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc** as teammates who've all crossed 300 — a first in Test history.
His bowling average of **24.02** is bettered by only **Glenn McGrath, Pat Cummins and Dennis Lillee** among Australians with 300+ wickets.

depth.background: Reaching 300 Test wickets is one of cricket's most respected milestones, achieved by only a small group of the format's greatest bowlers. Josh Hazlewood has been a mainstay of Australia's pace attack since debuting in 2014, prized for his metronomic accuracy alongside more express bowlers like Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins. Australia's four-man pace-and-spin attack of Hazlewood, Starc, Cummins and off-spinner Nathan Lyon has been settled for years, making this milestone a landmark for the whole unit, not just Hazlewood individually.

stories.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal run out in bizarre mid-pitch collision with Sri Lanka's bowler on Galle Test's opening day
stories.what_happened: Facing a delivery from Sri Lankan left-arm spinner **Keshara Nuwantha**, KL Rahul pushed the ball towards mid-on and immediately called for a single. As Jaiswal set off from the non-striker's end, Nuwantha — who had followed through and dived sharply to his right trying to stop the ball — collided with him, knocking him off balance. The contact left Jaiswal briefly stranded and disoriented, and by the time he recovered his footing, the fielding side had already gathered the ball and broken the stumps at the bowler's end with both batters caught out of their ground. Television replays showed the incident was accidental rather than deliberate obstruction by either side, and the third umpire confirmed the run-out. Jaiswal walked off for **32**, ending a promising start, while Rahul and the incoming Devdutt Padikkal steadied India to 101 for 1 at the lunch break.
key_points: Jaiswal was run out for **32** after colliding mid-pitch with Sri Lankan spinner **Keshara Nuwantha**, who had dived to stop the ball.
The mix-up started when **KL Rahul** tapped the ball to mid-on and set off for what looked like a routine single.
It is at least the **third time in his Test career** Jaiswal has lost his wicket to a running mix-up with a partner.
India recovered to **101/1 at lunch** on day one, with Rahul (32*) and **Devdutt Padikkal** (35*) rebuilding steadily.
The dismissal came on the opening day of India's historic **600th Test**, the first of a two-match series in Galle.

depth.background: India began their tour of Sri Lanka today by playing their **600th Test match** — only the third team in history, after England and Australia, to reach that mark. Yashasvi Jaiswal has been India's first-choice Test opener for the past two years and walked out with KL Rahul to start the innings after India won the toss and chose to bat. In cricket, the **non-striker** (the batter waiting at the bowler's end) must judge, in a split second, whether to run when their partner hits the ball — a call that occasionally goes wrong, sometimes with unusual consequences. Jaiswal himself has been part of more than one such mix-up earlier in his career.

stories.title: The US pulls its last aircraft carrier out of the Pacific, as the Iran war strains the Navy and leaves China's backyard uncovered
stories.what_happened: The Navy is sending the Japan-based carrier **USS George Washington** from the Pacific to the Middle East to relieve the **USS Abraham Lincoln**, whose deployment has stretched past **240 uninterrupted days at sea** — a record-setting stint that has reportedly left the crew dealing with mold, plumbing failures, critical supply shortages, and multiple incidents of sailors attempting to jump overboard amid the strain. The George Washington left port in Da Nang, Vietnam, and has since been tracked crossing the **Singapore Strait and the Strait of Malacca**, putting it on course for the Indian Ocean and, from there, the Arabian Sea within roughly a week. Because the George Washington was one of the only carriers regularly patrolling the western Pacific, its departure leaves that entire region — including waters near Taiwan — without a US carrier presence for the first time in years. Greg Poling of the Center for Strategic and International Studies said the move is the 'exact opposite' of the administration's own stated goal of treating the Pacific as more important than the Middle East. The redeployment comes as the US continues an open-ended air campaign against Iran that began in February 2026, alongside a separate, unrelated military buildup in the Western Hemisphere.
key_points: The **USS George Washington** is leaving the Pacific to relieve the crisis-hit **USS Abraham Lincoln** in the Middle East.
The Lincoln has been deployed for more than **240 straight days**, with reports of mold, plumbing failures, supply shortages and sailors attempting to jump overboard.
The move leaves the **western Pacific without a single US aircraft carrier** for the first time in years, just as China increases pressure near Taiwan.
Analysts call it the '**exact opposite**' of the administration's stated strategy of prioritizing the Pacific over the Middle East.
The George Washington is transiting the **Strait of Malacca** and should reach the Arabian Sea within about a week.

depth.background: Aircraft carriers are the most visible symbol of US military power projection — a single carrier strike group carries dozens of fighter jets and thousands of sailors, and its mere presence near an ally is meant to reassure them and deter adversaries. The US has fought an escalating, open-ended air campaign against Iran since **February 2026**, on top of a separate military buildup focused on Venezuela and the Western Hemisphere. Both campaigns draw on the same limited pool of carriers and strike groups, so committing more ships to the Middle East and the Americas necessarily means fewer available for the Indo-Pacific, where China has been the US Navy's stated long-term priority for over a decade.

stories.title: Formula 1's teenage title leader goes undercover at a German karting event — and wins
stories.what_happened: Antonelli entered a karting event in Germany under the alias 'Franz Antonelli' — a play on Verstappen's own pseudonym — reportedly outpacing other competitors at the session despite trying to stay under the radar. The appearance came in the closing days of F1's summer break, just before the grid reconvenes for the Dutch Grand Prix weekend at Zandvoort on August 21–23, where Antonelli will defend a 50-point lead over second-placed Lewis Hamilton and a 59-point lead over his own teammate George Russell.
key_points: Mercedes' **Kimi Antonelli**, F1's **19-year-old championship leader**, raced go-karts in Germany under the alias 'Franz Antonelli.'
The fake name is a **direct nod to Max Verstappen**, who used 'Franz Hermann' to race incognito in 2025.
Antonelli reportedly **smashed rival competitors' lap times** despite the disguise.
He heads into next week's **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort** holding a **50-point championship lead** over Lewis Hamilton.
The stunt keeps alive an unofficial F1 tradition of stars **racing incognito** between race weekends.

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli was promoted to Mercedes' race seat and has become the sport's breakout story in 2026, becoming the youngest points leader in F1 history at just 19. The 'racing incognito' tradition traces back to Max Verstappen, who first used the pseudonym 'Franz Hermann' in May 2025 to enter karting events without drawing a crowd. Formula 1 is on its summer break before resuming at Zandvoort for the Dutch Grand Prix — confirmed as the venue's final scheduled appearance on the calendar after five years back on the F1 schedule, and the first time the race will run as a Sprint weekend.

stories.title: Mercedes says grid penalties are now 'almost inevitable' for both Antonelli and Russell — and Monza looks like the place to take the hit
stories.what_happened: Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord told media it is **'almost inevitable'** that both Kimi Antonelli, who leads the drivers' championship, and George Russell, currently P3, will take grid penalties before the season ends. His exact words: 'Looking at how many components we've used in the first half of the season, it's almost inevitable that at some point there will be penalties to take... it's realistically going to be hard to get to the end of the season on the existing hardware.' Team principal Toto Wolff has gone further, openly discussing where — not if — Mercedes takes the hit: 'Monza can be very special for Kimi, but on paper it looks like it's a good place to take an engine penalty, so I need to speak to Marco [Antonelli's father] on whether we want to take it there,' he said, half-joking that 'we'll take the pressure off in Monza by starting him from the back!' Monza's long straights make overtaking easier than at tracks like Zandvoort or Baku, making it the team's preferred venue to absorb a penalty.
key_points: Mercedes deputy team boss Bradley Lord says penalties for **both title contenders** are **'almost inevitable'** before season's end.
Kimi Antonelli is already on his **4th engine and exhaust**; George Russell on his **3rd set** — one more change triggers an automatic grid drop.
Team boss Toto Wolff is weighing taking the hit at **Monza** (Sept 4-6), where long straights make overtaking easiest.
Mercedes leads the **constructors' championship by 72 points**; Antonelli leads the drivers' standings by **50 points**.
The timing decision could hand track position — and a title-fight opening — to **Ferrari's Hamilton** or Red Bull's Verstappen.

depth.background: Formula 1's power-unit rules cap how many engine components (the ICE, exhaust, energy store, control electronics, among others) each driver can use per season — typically four — before further changes trigger an automatic grid-position penalty. Antonelli has already needed a 4th ICE and exhaust after reliability failures this year (a battery issue in Spain, an engine swap at Belgium), and Russell is on his 3rd set after a water leak forced an engine change in Hungary qualifying and a battery failure in Canada earlier in the season.

stories.title: ITBP Deputy Inspector General killed in head-on highway collision in Saharanpur
stories.what_happened: Around 11 am, ITBP DIG Parminder Singh was travelling in a Scorpio vehicle on the Dehradun–Panchkula National Highway near Sarsawa police station in Saharanpur district, Uttar Pradesh, when the vehicle struck a road divider and then collided head-on with an oncoming Swift car. **Singh and his driver Ramsharan died** at the scene or shortly after. The DIG's gunner sustained serious injuries, and three occupants of the Swift — Gurunanak Singh, Devendra Kaur and Gurnam Singh — were also injured. All the injured were admitted to the medical college in Pilkhani for treatment.
key_points: ITBP **Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Parminder Singh, 52**, and his driver Ramsharan, 35, were killed in the crash.
It happened around **11 am** on the Dehradun–Panchkula national highway near Sarsawa police station, Saharanpur.
Singh's vehicle hit a **road divider** and then collided head-on with an oncoming Swift car.
The DIG's gunner and three occupants of the other car were **injured** and taken to hospital in Pilkhani.
ITBP is the **Indo-Tibetan Border Police**, a paramilitary force that guards India's Himalayan frontier.

depth.background: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) is one of India's central armed police forces, primarily responsible for guarding the mountainous India-China border. A Deputy Inspector General is a senior field-command rank within the force. High-speed convoy or official-vehicle accidents on Indian national highways are unfortunately common, and this crash claimed the life of a serving senior officer in transit.

stories.title: Jharkhand exam-scandal hunger striker enters his 14th day, hospitalized, as protesters say Modi's new exam reforms don't go far enough
stories.what_happened: Devendra Nath Mahto is now on the **14th consecutive day** of his hunger strike and has been admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi, after a march to gherao (surround) the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly turned chaotic when police responded with **lathi charges** (baton charges) against protesting students. When Mahto expressed a wish to leave the hospital and join Ranchi's Independence Day Tiranga Yatra (flag march) on August 15, police mounted a **heavy deployment outside his hospital room** and stopped him from attending. Protesters continue to demand the **cancellation of the JSSC-CGL recruitment exam** they say was compromised, along with a **CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation) probe** into the alleged irregularities — comprehensive reforms to the recruitment process generally. Jharkhand Chief Minister **Hemant Soren** has responded by launching an outreach initiative called 'Chhatron Ki Baat, Chhatron Ke Sath' (translating roughly to 'talking with students, standing with students') to solicit student input, but has not agreed to the specific demands. Students have warned they are prepared to escalate into a broader 'mass movement' if their demands continue to go unmet.
key_points: Student leader **Devendra Nath Mahto** is on the **14th day** of an indefinite hunger strike that began August 2.
He's been **admitted to Sadar Hospital** after a Vidhan Sabha gherao march turned chaotic when police used lathi charges.
Police mounted **heavy deployment outside his hospital room** on August 15 to stop him joining the Independence Day flag-hoisting march.
Protesters are demanding the **JSSC-CGL exam be cancelled** and a **CBI probe** into alleged irregularities — neither has happened yet.
Jharkhand's Chief Minister Hemant Soren has launched a student-outreach program, but **the hunger strike hasn't stopped**.

depth.background: The protests trace back to alleged **irregularities in recruitment exams** run by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) — students allege leaked questions and a rigged, opaque selection process that has cost thousands of young job-seekers a fair shot at coveted government jobs. Devendra Nath Mahto began an indefinite hunger strike on **August 2** as the movement's central, symbolic act of protest. The unrest grew large enough that it became a national story, feeding into **President Murmu's announcement of nationwide exam reforms** during her Independence Day address on August 15 — but that announcement was a general, national-level fix, not the specific local demands (cancelling the JSSC-CGL exam, a CBI investigation) that Jharkhand's protesters are asking for.

thread.previously: We reported that President Murmu announced sweeping national exam reforms in response to nationwide protests over recruitment-exam paper leaks.
thread.changed: The protest that triggered those reforms hasn't ended — its most visible leader, Devendra Nath Mahto, is now on the 14th day of an indefinite hunger strike, has been hospitalized, and was blocked by police from joining Independence Day's flag-hoisting march, showing Jharkhand's protesters see the national reforms as insufficient.

stories.title: Myanmar says it has verified 300,000+ Rohingya refugees for return, as the exodus enters its ninth year
stories.what_happened: Myanmar's ruling military-backed government said on **Saturday** that it has verified more than **300,000 Rohingya refugees** currently living in Bangladesh's camps as former residents of western Rakhine state, making them eligible in principle for repatriation. Officials said Myanmar would accept their return once **security conditions improve** — but offered no date or concrete mechanism for how or when that would actually happen. The announcement comes as the crisis enters its **ninth year**, with hundreds of thousands still confined to camps around Cox's Bazar, one of the world's largest refugee settlements. It follows a 2018 repatriation agreement between Bangladesh and Myanmar that set a two-year timeline — one that expired years ago without a single organized, verified return taking place. Myanmar's security situation has deteriorated rather than improved since then: a 2021 coup ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi, and since 2023 the **Arakan Army** has been fighting the military for control of the very region refugees would return to, driving fresh waves of displacement.
key_points: Myanmar's military-backed government says it has verified **more than 300,000** Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh as former Rakhine residents eligible to return.
Return is conditional — Myanmar says people can come back only **"once security conditions improve,"** with no timeline given.
The crisis is now in its **ninth year**, with hundreds of thousands still in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar camps since fleeing a 2017 military crackdown.
A **2021 military coup** and a **2023 civil war** in Rakhine State between the army and the Arakan Army have made the region less safe, not more.
Bangladesh and Myanmar agreed a **two-year repatriation plan back in 2018** that has still not moved a single verified refugee home.

depth.background: In August 2017, Myanmar's military launched a brutal crackdown in Rakhine State after attacks by a Rohingya insurgent group, driving roughly **740,000 Rohingya** — a Muslim minority Myanmar has long denied citizenship to — across the border into Bangladesh within weeks. The United Nations later called it a **textbook example of ethnic cleansing**. Bangladesh and Myanmar signed a repatriation agreement in 2018, but it has never meaningfully proceeded, largely because Myanmar has refused to guarantee refugees' safety or citizenship rights. Myanmar's 2021 coup, followed by armed resistance and, since 2023, direct fighting between the army and the ethnic **Arakan Army** for control of Rakhine, has left the region even less stable than the one refugees fled.

stories.title: Alonso reportedly agrees terms to stay at Aston Martin through 2028 — with a big raise
stories.what_happened: After a near-winless first half of 2026 that left Aston Martin bottom of the constructors' table with a single point, Alonso reportedly told the team he wants a substantial pay increase — roughly **€10 million more per year** — in exchange for committing to a new deal through 2028. Marca and multiple other outlets now report the two sides have settled on terms in principle and are simply choosing the moment to announce it, with Zandvoort this coming weekend floated as the likely stage. The timing lines up with a genuine on-track improvement: Aston Martin's long-awaited 16-part upgrade package arrived at the Hungarian Grand Prix and immediately made the car far more competitive, which Newey says has been decisive in keeping Alonso interested in staying rather than testing the market.
key_points: Alonso has scored just **one point** all season and sits **19th** in the drivers' standings, as Aston Martin languishes **10th** (last) in the constructors' championship at the summer break
He's reportedly seeking a **33% pay rise**, from around **€30 million to €40 million a year**, to sign a new deal running through **2028**
Spanish outlet Marca reports the two sides have **already agreed terms**, with an announcement possible as soon as this weekend's **Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort**

Aston Martin's technical boss **Adrian Newey** says he's "pretty confident" Alonso will stay, pointing to a **16-upgrade package** introduced at the Hungarian Grand Prix that finally made the car competitive
Alonso turned **45** this year and had said he would decide his F1 future only after the summer break

depth.background: **Fernando Alonso**, a two-time world champion, joined Aston Martin in 2023 and has been racing on a contract due to expire at the end of **2026**. The team paired with a new **Honda power unit** for F1's 2026 rules overhaul, but the combination has been badly unreliable and slow all season — at points so rough that Alonso and teammate Lance Stroll reported physical discomfort from vibrations during races. Alonso has been openly frustrated but has repeatedly said the team, led by design chief Adrian Newey, is building toward something better.

stories.title: Flores earthquake death toll more than doubles to 47, as rescuers remain cut off from the worst-hit district
stories.what_happened: The earthquake's confirmed death toll has jumped from an initial count of about 20 on Saturday to **at least 47** as of the latest figures from Indonesia's National Disaster Management Agency. Search-and-rescue teams have still not been able to reach **Nagekeo Regency**, the area closest to the quake's epicenter, because landslides triggered by the tremor have blocked the roads leading in — one team tried to reach it by car and was turned back, while another is attempting the journey by ferry instead. Roughly **2,000 residents of Nagekeo evacuated** their homes, and officials have reported damage to houses, warehouses and government facilities in the district. The quake's epicenter was located **42 miles north-northwest of Ende**, a city on Flores Island in East Nusa Tenggara province. Communications with the hardest-hit areas remain disrupted, which is part of why officials can't yet give a precise damage assessment. Both Indonesian disaster officials and the US Geological Survey's automated damage-estimate system say the death toll is likely to keep rising once rescuers finally get in.
key_points: Confirmed deaths have climbed to **at least 47**, more than double Saturday's initial count of 20.
Rescue teams still **cannot physically reach Nagekeo**, the district nearest the epicenter — landslides have blocked every road.
About **2,000 residents evacuated** from Nagekeo as homes, warehouses and government buildings took damage.
The **magnitude-7.7 quake** struck 42 miles north-northwest of the city of Ende, and briefly triggered a tsunami warning that has since been lifted.
Indonesia's disaster agency and the **USGS both expect the toll to rise further** once crews finally break through to the cut-off area.

depth.background: Indonesia sits on the **Pacific Ring of Fire**, the horseshoe-shaped chain of fault lines that produces most of the world's earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, so powerful quakes are a recurring national risk. East Nusa Tenggara, the province that includes Flores, is one of Indonesia's poorest and least-connected regions, with narrow mountain roads that wash out easily in bad weather. That geography is now the core problem: it isn't a shortage of rescuers holding back the response, it's that **landslides have physically cut off the area closest to the epicenter**. The initial magnitude-7.7 shock hit early Saturday morning local time and was strong enough to trigger a tsunami warning for nearby coastlines before it was lifted hours later.

thread.previously: We reported the magnitude-7.7 quake that struck off Flores Island on Saturday, killing at least 20 people and triggering a since-lifted tsunami warning.
thread.changed: The confirmed death toll has more than doubled to at least 47, and officials say it will keep climbing because rescue teams still haven't reached Nagekeo, the district closest to the epicenter, where landslides have blocked every road in.

stories.title: Bortoleto shuts down Audi exit talk with a 'no clauses' contract
stories.what_happened: Bortoleto told media this week he has a **long-term, multi-year contract** with Audi that runs well beyond 2026. Asked about its structure, he said **"there are no clauses"** — notable in a sport where driver deals are usually loaded with performance triggers and team options. He confirmed he'll be at Audi **"next year, and not only next year, but for the following years as well,"** with reports suggesting the deal stretches toward Audi's 2030 target. The statement directly addresses swirling rumors that Audi could pursue Sainz or Piastri for 2027. It lands as Audi endures a difficult first season as a full works team, sitting near the back of the constructors' standings.
key_points: Bortoleto says his Audi deal has **no exit clauses**, unusual for F1 contracts
Deal runs **beyond 2026**, toward Audi's stated **2030** project target
He's scored **10 of Audi's 12 points** in 2026, the team's top scorer
Move addresses rumors linking **Carlos Sainz** and **Oscar Piastri** to his seat
Audi is in its **debut season** as a full manufacturer works team

depth.background: Audi entered Formula 1 in 2026 as a full works manufacturer, absorbing the former **Sauber** team, with boss **Mattia Binotto** framing it as a long-term project aimed at real competitiveness by **2030**. **Gabriel Bortoleto**, a 21-year-old Brazilian, joined as a rookie in 2025 (Sauber's final season) and has been the team's most productive scorer through a rocky debut works season. Speculation had linked bigger names — Sainz and even reigning-form McLaren driver Piastri — to a future Audi seat, raising doubts about Bortoleto's own long-term status at the team.

stories.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is live — and the contract offers keep shifting
stories.what_happened: Verstappen went into F1's summer break sitting sixth in the championship, more than **100 points** off leader Kimi Antonelli, which mathematically triggered the exit clause in his contract. That set off weeks of contract theater: Red Bull first proposed a short, one-year extension to 2029 that would strip the exit clause out of his deal in exchange for more money, then reportedly pivoted to offering a much longer **five-year contract taking him to 2033**. Neither offer has been publicly accepted. When a report circulated suggesting Max was already leaning toward re-signing without the clause, his father and manager Jos Verstappen bluntly dismissed it online. Team boss-level sources say Red Bull is trying to lock him down before rival teams can make a serious approach during the clause window, which stays open until October.
key_points: Verstappen sits **P6** in the drivers' championship with **109 points**, well outside the top two he needed to stay above to keep his contract locked in — so his exit clause is now officially active
He has until **October 2026** to decide whether to use that clause and leave Red Bull for 2027
Red Bull first offered a **one-year extension to 2029** that would delete the exit clause entirely, then reportedly switched to a **five-year deal running to 2033**
His father and manager **Jos Verstappen** publicly shot down reports of a done deal, replying "You know absolutely nothing" to a report claiming Max was close to re-signing
Red Bull remains the only front-running team yet to win a race in **2026**, fueling speculation about why Verstappen hasn't jumped at a new deal

depth.background: Max Verstappen, a **four-time world champion**, is contracted to Red Bull through the end of **2028**, but that deal contains a performance-linked exit clause: if he isn't in the top two of the standings by the summer break, he can trigger a route out for 2027. New engine and aerodynamic rules introduced this year have shaken up the competitive order, and Red Bull's 2026 car (the RB22) has been difficult to set up, leaving Verstappen well off the pace he's used to. He has openly criticized the new regulations this season.

stories.title: Government cuts export tax on petrol, diesel and jet fuel as crude prices ease
stories.what_happened: Effective **August 15, 2026**, India's government cut export duties on petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF). The **petrol export duty was scrapped entirely**, dropping from ₹3.5 per litre (set August 3) to **zero**. The **diesel** windfall tax was cut to **₹24/litre** from ₹25.5, and the **ATF** rate was cut to **₹19.5/litre** from ₹22. The finance ministry clarified there is **no change to domestic retail fuel prices** — these levies apply only to fuel Indian refiners sell abroad, not what consumers pay at the pump.
key_points: Export duty on **petrol cut to zero**, from **₹3.5/litre** charged just two weeks earlier.
**Diesel** export tax (SAED) cut to **₹24/litre**, down from **₹25.5**.
**ATF (jet fuel)** export tax cut to **₹19.5/litre**, down from **₹22**.
Domestic pump prices for petrol and diesel are **unchanged** — this only affects fuel sold abroad.

depth.background: India taxes fuel exports through a **'windfall tax'** (formally the Special Additional Excise Duty, SAED), first introduced in 2022 when refiners were earning outsized profits exporting fuel refined from cheap Russian crude while domestic supply tightened. The government reviews and adjusts these rates roughly every two weeks based on international oil and fuel prices — raising them when refiner margins spike, cutting them when crude prices fall. Less than two weeks before this cut, the government had actually **raised** these same export levies, reflecting how quickly crude markets have been swinging amid the broader Iran-linked Middle East tensions.

stories.title: India win the toss and bat first in their historic 600th Test, but leave uncapped Auqib Nabi out of the XI at Galle
stories.what_happened: Play began on schedule at **Galle International Stadium**, with India winning the toss and opting to bat first on what looked, in Gill's own assessment, like a good batting surface. The announced XI answered yesterday's open question: **Auqib Nabi did not get his debut**. Instead, India fielded three specialist spinners — Ravindra Jadeja, **Kuldeep Yadav**, and uncapped spinner Manav Suthar — alongside pacers Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna, betting on spin-friendly Galle conditions over an extra seamer. The top order got off to a rocky start when **Yashasvi Jaiswal was run out** within the first hour, before KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal steadied the innings; India were past 70 runs for one wicket as the morning session progressed. This is officially India's 600th Test and their first match of the new World Test Championship cycle, played under Gill's captaincy on a day that also happens to be India's Independence Day.
key_points: India **won the toss and chose to bat first** in what is officially their **600th Test match**, only the third team ever to reach that number.
Uncapped pacer **Auqib Nabi was left out of the XI** despite his shock call-up, with India instead picking **three spinners** — Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar.
Opener **Yashasvi Jaiswal was run out** inside the first hour, an early setback for the new-look batting order.
The Test is India's **first fixture of the 2025–2027 World Test Championship cycle** and the first under new full-time captain **Shubman Gill**.
August 15 is **India's Independence Day**, adding symbolic weight to a match already billed as a milestone occasion.

depth.background: This is the same landmark Test previewed a day earlier: India entering their 600th match, a mark only England and Australia had reached before, at Galle's 50th-ever Test — a first for any Asian venue. Shubman Gill leads the side for the first time in a bilateral Test series since being installed as India's full-time red-ball captain, working alongside head coach **Gautam Gambhir**. Ahead of the game, India's pace attack had already lost **Jasprit Bumrah** to a knee injury, prompting the surprise squad inclusion of uncapped Jammu and Kashmir seamer Auqib Nabi — whose potential debut was the single biggest open question heading into the match.

thread.previously: Yesterday's story previewed India's 600th Test — a milestone only England and Australia had previously reached — with Shubman Gill captaining and uncapped seamer Auqib Nabi in the squad after Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out injured; the open question was whether Nabi would get a shock debut.
thread.changed: The match has now actually started: India won the toss and chose to bat, and the announced XI leaves Auqib Nabi out — India went in with Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar as spinners alongside Jadeja instead of handing Nabi his debut. Play is underway, with India past 70 for the loss of Yashasvi Jaiswal, who was run out early.

stories.title: Honda says its upgraded Aston Martin engine has hit its targets, arriving at Zandvoort as the second half of the team's revival plan
stories.what_happened: Honda has detailed the technical content of a new-specification engine for Aston Martin — sometimes called 'spec-2' — confirming it will debut at the **Dutch Grand Prix, August 21-23**, the first race back from F1's summer break. Honda's GM of Trackside Engineering, Shintaro Orihara, confirmed the engine has hit Honda's internal performance targets but declined to confirm exact horsepower figures, which media estimates put anywhere from **30 to 50 additional horsepower**. The changes include a redesigned combustion pre-chamber for a faster burn, a reshaped piston head for better combustion, and revised internal lubrication to reduce parasitic friction losses. This lands as the second half of a planned Aston Martin revival: the team already introduced a major aerodynamic 'B-spec' chassis at the Hungarian Grand Prix before the break, which immediately helped Alonso and Stroll compete in the midfield instead of running at the back.
key_points: Honda confirms a new-spec engine for Aston Martin has hit its **internal performance targets**, debuting at the **Dutch GP (Aug 21-23)**.
The upgrade redesigns the **combustion pre-chamber, piston shape, and internal lubrication** to cut friction and burn fuel faster.
Estimates of the power gain range from **30 to 50 horsepower**, though Honda won't confirm the exact figure.
Aston Martin's power unit has reportedly been down **over 100bhp** on rivals at points this season.
It follows a chassis 'B-spec' introduced at the **Hungarian GP** that already helped Alonso and Stroll fight in the midfield.

depth.background: Honda's 2026 return to F1 as Aston Martin's works engine partner has been rocky — the power unit has struggled with both performance and reliability, traced partly to Honda reassigning many of its F1 specialists to other projects ahead of the 2026 rules reset. Aston Martin, with an Adrian Newey-designed car and one of the grid's biggest budgets, has been arguably the season's most disappointing team relative to its ambitions, though a new aerodynamic package introduced at the Hungarian GP before the summer break already helped Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll compete with Williams and Haas rather than running last.

stories.title: Opposition pounces on Modi's Independence Day speech fumble and 'dimaagi Naxal' remark
stories.what_happened: During his address, Modi appeared to **fumble while citing statistics on India's bioeconomy growth** since 2014, a moment Congress and AAP leaders quickly clipped and shared on social media. Congress's **Pawan Khera** described Modi as **"an under-confident, nervous and shaky Prime Minister,"** and AAP chief **Arvind Kejriwal** offered similar criticism of the delivery. Separately, a remark using the phrase **"dimaagi Naxal"** — loosely, someone who is a "Naxal [left-wing extremist] in their thinking" — aimed at critics of the government drew accusations of inflammatory, divisive language on a day meant to unite the country. Congress also renewed substantive criticism, accusing the government of a **"dishonest pitch"** on **women's reservation in Parliament** and of reversing its earlier opposition to a **caste census** before announcing one itself. The **BJP defended** the speech, casting it as a genuine roadmap for **"Viksit Bharat"** by 2047.
key_points: Modi **stumbled while citing bioeconomy growth figures** during his 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort.
Congress's **Pawan Khera** called him **"under-confident, nervous and shaky"**; AAP's **Arvind Kejriwal** echoed the criticism.
A **"dimaagi Naxal"** (roughly, "Naxal in the mind") remark aimed at government critics drew sharp opposition backlash.
Congress accused the government of a **"dishonest pitch"** on women's reservation and flip-flopping on the **caste census**.
The **BJP has defended** the speech as a roadmap for a **"Viksit Bharat" (developed India)**.

depth.background: Every August 15, India's Prime Minister addresses the nation from the ramparts of the **Red Fort** in Delhi — the most-watched political speech of the year, traditionally used to set the government's agenda. This year marked India's **80th year of independence**, and Modi used the speech to announce a slate of new initiatives under the banner **"Shakti Ki Saptadhara."** Opposition parties, led by **Congress** and the **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)**, routinely contest the government's framing and record in the speech's aftermath, and this year's reaction has focused as much on how Modi delivered the speech as on what he said.

stories.title: Bumrah's shock Sri Lanka Test withdrawal sparks an internal BCCI blame game, reports say
stories.what_happened: Fresh reporting says the sudden nature of Bumrah's withdrawal wasn't a simple case of a player failing a late fitness test — it has instead triggered an **internal BCCI storm** over who knew what and when. According to the reports, the **CoE's sports science team had indicated to Agarkar and the selectors that Bumrah would be fit enough to travel** for the series, only for a subsequent, more thorough medical assessment to reveal his knee injury required a **longer recovery period** than first thought, forcing his withdrawal after all. That gap between the CoE's initial read and the final medical picture has reportedly left the chief selector's panel unhappy with how the CoE handled and communicated Bumrah's case. Compounding the issue, the report notes the **CoE has been without a full-time head of sports science** since Nitin Patel departed the role — a structural gap that may have contributed to the mixed signals. The BCCI is now said to be reviewing its **injury-management and communication protocols**. J&K's uncapped **Auqib Nabi**, who took 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, remains in as Bumrah's replacement.
key_points: Reports say India's selectors were told **Jasprit Bumrah would be fit** for the Sri Lanka Tests, only for a **later medical assessment** to rule him out.
The apparent miscommunication is between the **BCCI Centre of Excellence's sports science team** and **chief selector Ajit Agarkar's** panel.
The **Centre of Excellence has had no full-time head of sports science** since Nitin Patel's departure.
The BCCI is now said to be **reviewing its injury-management and communication process**.
Uncapped **Jammu and Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi**, who took **104 wickets** over two Ranji Trophy seasons, was Bumrah's shock replacement.

depth.background: **Jasprit Bumrah** is India's premier fast bowler, and his fitness has been a recurring storyline for over a year because of a history of back trouble carefully managed through a workload-management system centered on the **BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE)** in Bengaluru. It was reported yesterday that Bumrah, who picked up a **knee injury** fielding in a one-day international against England in Cardiff in July, had been **ruled out of the two-Test series against Sri Lanka**, with uncapped pacer **Auqib Nabi** getting a shock call-up in his place. India's chief selector, **Ajit Agarkar**, leads the panel responsible for naming the Test squad, working off fitness assessments the CoE provides.

thread.previously: Bumrah had been ruled out of the Sri Lanka Test series with a knee injury, and India gave uncapped Auqib Nabi a shock call-up as his replacement.
thread.changed: New reporting says the withdrawal has triggered an internal BCCI storm — selectors were reportedly told Bumrah would be fit, only for a later assessment to rule him out, exposing a communication gap with the Centre of Excellence that the BCCI is now said to be reviewing.
