stories.title: Christian Horner's best shot at an F1 return hinges on a September veto deadline at Alpine
stories.what_happened: Otro's 24% stake in Alpine is reportedly for sale, but Renault, Alpine's parent, currently holds a **right of veto** over who it can be sold to — and has been widely expected to block any sale to a group linked to Horner. That veto is set to **expire in September 2026**, after which Otro would be free to sell to whichever bidder it chooses. Mercedes had been exploring a purchase of the stake but has since **ended those talks**, reportedly unwilling to meet an asking price of around **$720 million** — more than triple what Otro paid for it in 2023. The backdrop is a Formula 1 where team valuations are surging toward the **$10 billion mark**, making a stake like this increasingly valuable regardless of who ends up buying it.
key_points: Spanish investment group **Otro** owns a **24% stake in Alpine** that is reportedly up for sale.
Alpine's parent company **Renault holds a veto** over any sale of that stake — but the veto **expires in September**.
Once the veto lapses, Otro could sell to **any bidder**, including a group linked to Horner, without Renault's approval.
Mercedes had explored buying the stake but **walked away**, reportedly balking at a **$720 million asking price**.

depth.background: **Christian Horner** was Red Bull's team principal for two decades before being fired in **July 2025**, ending a run that included multiple championship wins. Since then he has been out of Formula 1 entirely, and Alpine — the French manufacturer team — has emerged as his most realistic route back in, if a takeover of its Otro-owned stake goes through with backers connected to him.

stories.title: Canada and the US race to strike a trade deal before Trump's 50% tariff deadline hits Wednesday
stories.what_happened: Canadian Trade Minister **Dominic LeBlanc** met US Trade Representative **Jamieson Greer** in Washington twice this week, trying to strike a deal before **50%** tariffs on roughly **$20 billion** worth of Canadian goods — including milk, plywood, hockey sticks and beer — are due to take effect at 12:01 a.m. on **August 19**. Proposals reportedly on the table include Canada dropping its counter-tariffs on US autos and alcohol, and changes to how Canada manages its dairy import quotas, in exchange for the US backing off the 50% threat and reducing other existing tariffs. After meeting with Canada's provincial premiers in Charlottetown, Prime Minister **Mark Carney** said "everything's on the table" if no agreement is reached, while insisting Canada will not retaliate before the deadline passes. Carney has repeatedly said he will only sign a deal that is "in the best interest of Canadians."
key_points: US threatens **50%** tariffs on Canada starting August 19.
Levies would hit about **$20 billion** in Canadian goods.
Targets dairy, alcohol, plywood, furniture and **autos**.
PM Carney says **"everything's on the table"** if talks fail.
Trade officials met **twice this week** racing the clock.

depth.background: Trump has used tariffs — taxes charged on imported goods — as a central tool of US trade policy this year, already hitting dozens of countries with new duties. Canada has been a repeated target over its **supply-managed dairy system**, provincial bans on US alcohol, and the counter-tariffs Canada placed on US autos in response to earlier US tariffs. Trump had already raised tariffs on Canadian goods to **35%** earlier this year; this new threat would push them to **50%**. The two economies have deeply integrated supply chains, especially in autos, so a tariff this large would ripple through factories on both sides of the border.

stories.title: A Jeff Bezos-backed group buys a minority stake in Liverpool FC, with an option to take control
stories.what_happened: Fenway Sports Group announced the sale of a minority equity stake in Liverpool to a new consortium backed by Amazon founder **Jeff Bezos**, estimated at between **30% and a third of the club**. The investment group is led by **Amit Bhatia**, who will become Liverpool's vice chairman and join its expanded board, and combines Bezos's K5 Sports fund with the **Mittal family trusts** and **EE Capital**, the family office of Eduardo and Elaine Saverin. FSG says it will retain majority ownership and day-to-day operational control of the club for now. Crucially, the new group has been given the **option to become Liverpool's controlling shareholder within the next year** — meaning this stake could be the first step toward a full change of ownership rather than a one-off investment.
key_points: A consortium including **Amazon founder Jeff Bezos** has bought a minority stake in Liverpool FC, estimated at **30% to a third** of the club.
The investment group, led by **Amit Bhatia**, includes Bezos's **K5 Sports fund**, the **Mittal family trusts**, and Eduardo Saverin's family office.
Fenway Sports Group (FSG), Liverpool's owner since 2010, **keeps majority ownership and operational control** — for now.
The new investors have an **option to become the controlling owner within a year**.
Bhatia joins Liverpool's board as **vice chairman**.

depth.background: Liverpool FC, one of English football's most successful and valuable clubs, has been owned by Fenway Sports Group — the US group that also owns baseball's Boston Red Sox — since 2010. FSG has brought in outside investors before, but a deal of this size, with a path to a change of control, is unusual. It reflects a broader trend of US tech and finance billionaires buying into elite European football as top clubs have become scarce, prestige global assets.

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants blitz SunRisers Leeds to reach the Hundred men's final at Lord's
stories.what_happened: Batting first under lights at the Oval, Manchester Super Giants were given a flying platform by Paul Walter and Heinrich Klaasen, who put on 114 runs together — Walter's innings included eight sixes, a new individual record for the franchise, as the pair took the total to 186 for 4 from their 100 balls. In reply, SunRisers Leeds never quite got the asking rate under control: Josh Tongue struck twice inside his opening spell, top-edging Mitch Marsh and trapping captain Zak Crawley leg-before four balls later, and despite a fighting effort from Harry Brook (49) and an unbeaten 54 from Ryan Rickelton, Leeds fell 20 runs short. The result ends SunRisers Leeds' 2026 campaign — hours after their women's side also lost their own Eliminator on the same night at the Oval — and sends Manchester Super Giants through to face Trent Rockets in Sunday's men's final at Lord's.
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants** beat **SunRisers Leeds** by **20 runs** in Friday night's Eliminator at the Kia Oval to book a spot in Sunday's men's final.

Opener **Paul Walter** smashed **80 off 46 balls** including a club-record **8 sixes** in an innings, sharing a **114-run third-wicket stand** with **Heinrich Klaasen (63 off 26)** — Manchester's biggest-ever third-wicket partnership in T20 cricket.
Manchester posted **186-4** from their 100 balls; SunRisers fell short despite fifties from **Harry Brook (49 off 31)** and **Ryan Rickelton (54 not out off 34)**.
Seamer **Josh Tongue** took **4 wickets for 26 runs**, removing SunRisers openers Mitch Marsh and captain Zak Crawley early to swing the chase back Manchester's way.
Manchester Super Giants now face **Trent Rockets** in the men's final at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16**, with SunRisers Leeds' 2026 campaign over.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's franchise short-form competition, where each innings is a fixed 100 balls rather than the usual 120 of T20 cricket, and the top four men's and women's teams from the group stage progress to knockout play. SunRisers Leeds had topped the group table and looked the form side coming into the knockouts, while Manchester Super Giants scraped into the playoffs on net run rate. Trent Rockets had already secured their place in the final by finishing group-stage leaders and winning their own semi-final-equivalent fixture, leaving the Oval Eliminator to decide their opponent.

stories.title: The Hundred sets its Lord's finals: Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds join Trent Rockets
stories.what_happened: **Manchester Super Giants** defeated **Sunrisers Leeds** by 20 runs in Friday's men's Eliminator at the Kia Oval, setting up a men's final against table-toppers **Trent Rockets** at Lord's. In the women's competition, played the same day, **Sunrisers Leeds** beat **Southern Brave** by five wickets — Lauren Winfield-Hill (37) and Deepti Sharma (28 not out) guiding them home with 11 balls to spare after Southern Brave posted 114/7 — to reach the women's final, also against Trent Rockets. Both finals will be played at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16**, with the women's final at 2:15pm and the men's at 6pm; a reserve day is scheduled for Monday, August 17 in case of a washout. Trent Rockets finished top of both the men's and women's points tables this season, meaning they avoided the Eliminator entirely and go into Sunday's finals with extra rest compared to their opponents.
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants** beat Sunrisers Leeds by **20 runs** in the men's Eliminator at the Kia Oval to book a Lord's final spot against **Trent Rockets**, who topped the table.
In the women's competition, **Sunrisers Leeds** won a tense **five-wicket** Eliminator over Southern Brave to reach their final, also against **Trent Rockets**.
Both finals are at **Lord's on Sunday, August 16** — women's at 2:15pm, men's at 6pm — with a reserve day on Monday if needed.
**Trent Rockets** finished top of both the men's and women's tables this season, earning a rest before the final while their rivals fought through the Eliminator.
The Hundred is now in its **sixth year** as English cricket's short-format franchise competition.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is an English franchise cricket tournament launched in 2021, built around a shortened 100-ball-per-innings format designed to be faster and more accessible than traditional Twenty20. Eight men's and eight women's teams, mostly named after England's historic Test grounds and cities, compete each August. The top team in each table qualifies straight for the final; the second- and third-placed teams play an Eliminator for the second final spot — the format that decided both of Sunday's finalists.

stories.title: BCCI names Pratika Rawal as Jemimah Rodrigues' Asia Cup replacement after hamstring tear
stories.what_happened: Rodrigues was assessed by the BCCI Medical Team at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, which confirmed a high-grade hamstring tear, ruling her out of both the Women's Asia Cup and the Asian Games in Japan. The Women's Selection Committee has now named Pratika Rawal as her replacement for the Asia Cup squad, giving Rawal her maiden T20I call-up. The BCCI has not given a firm timeline for Rodrigues' recovery and return.
key_points: The **BCCI Women's Selection Committee** has named **Pratika Rawal** to replace the injured Jemimah Rodrigues for the T20 **Women's Asia Cup**.
Rodrigues suffered a **high-grade right hamstring tear** on **August 3** while playing for Southern Brave in England's **The Hundred**.
Rawal earns her first **T20I call-up**, after missing selection for this year's Women's T20 World Cup.
**Harmanpreet Kaur** continues as captain and **Smriti Mandhana** as vice-captain for the tournament, which runs in the UAE from **August 28 to September 13**.

depth.background: Jemimah Rodrigues is a key middle-order batter for India's white-ball sides, and her injury is a blow ahead of a tournament India is chasing after losing the Asia Cup title to Sri Lanka in 2024. The injury happened while she was playing in The Hundred, England's franchise T20 competition — a reminder that international boards increasingly have to weigh the release of players for lucrative overseas leagues against injury risk just before their own major tournaments.

thread.previously: We reported Jemimah Rodrigues was ruled out of the Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games with a severe hamstring tear.
thread.changed: The BCCI has now named her replacement — Pratika Rawal earns her first T20I call-up for the Asia Cup squad.

stories.title: The Hundred men's final is set: Trent Rockets face Manchester Super Giants at Lord's after MSG oust Sunrisers Leeds
stories.what_happened: **Manchester Super Giants beat Sunrisers Leeds by 20 runs** in the men's eliminator, posting **186 for 4** before restricting Sunrisers Leeds to **166 for 7** in reply. The result sends Manchester Super Giants through to face **Trent Rockets**, who had already qualified directly, in the men's final at **Lord's**. In a separate match on the same eliminators day, **Sunrisers Leeds' women's team advanced to the women's final**, where they will face Southern Brave — meaning Sunrisers Leeds' men's and women's sides had contrasting fortunes on the same day, with the men eliminated and the women through.
key_points: **Manchester Super Giants beat Sunrisers Leeds by 20 runs** in the men's eliminator, scoring 186/4 to SRL's 166/7.
The win sends **Manchester Super Giants to Lord's** to face **Trent Rockets** in the men's final.
Sunrisers Leeds' women's side, in a separate match, **advanced to the women's final** instead against Southern Brave.
Trent Rockets had already secured their final spot directly, without needing to play the eliminator.
The men's final at **Lord's** is cricket's biggest single stage in England outside a home Test.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England and Wales Cricket Board's short-format franchise competition, played in 100-ball innings, that runs each August and culminates in finals at **Lord's**, the sport's most famous ground. Because both the men's and women's competitions use a similar knockout structure, the team that finishes top of the group stage goes straight to the final, while the second- and third-placed teams play an **eliminator** for the last spot. Trent Rockets had already secured their place in the men's final directly; Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds had to play off for the second spot.

thread.previously: We reported that Manchester Super Giants and Sunrisers Leeds had both reached Lord's finals day alongside Trent Rockets, across the men's and women's competitions.
thread.changed: The men's eliminator has now been played and decided: Manchester Super Giants beat Sunrisers Leeds by 20 runs to claim the final men's spot, setting up a Trent Rockets vs Manchester Super Giants final at Lord's, while Sunrisers Leeds instead advanced to the separate women's final.

stories.title: Assam's flood death toll climbs to 104 as the monsoon disaster drags into its second month
stories.what_happened: The Assam State Disaster Management Authority confirmed on **Friday, August 14** that one more death in Sivasagar district pushed the state's cumulative flood toll for 2026 to **104**, while the number of people still affected ticked up slightly to over **78,000**. Floodwaters continue to affect **313 villages across 20 revenue circles** in seven districts — Nagaon, Golaghat, Sivasagar, Kamrup, Hojai, Jorhat and Lakhimpur — with Golaghat the worst hit at roughly **30,778 affected people**, followed by Nagaon at **26,292**. The state is running dozens of relief camps and distribution centres, and boats have evacuated well over a hundred stranded residents in the worst-hit pockets. CM Himanta Biswa Sarma separately announced **₹11.3 crore** to rebuild flood-damaged Anganwadi (government childcare) centres across four districts, while West Bengal's government pledged **₹10 crore** from its own relief fund and India's TVS Group donated **₹5 crore**. Officials say no major river is currently flowing above the danger mark, suggesting the worst of this wave may be passing even as the human cost keeps climbing.
key_points: Assam's 2026 flood death toll has risen to **104** after a fresh death in **Sivasagar district**.
Over **78,000 people** remain affected across **seven districts**, even as the overall numbers slowly recede.
**313 villages** in **20 revenue circles** are still under floodwater, with Golaghat the worst-hit at over **30,000 people**.
Assam's government is running **31 relief camps** and has committed **₹11.3 crore** just to rebuild flood-hit childcare centres.
Neighbouring **West Bengal** has chipped in **₹10 crore** in inter-state relief aid.

depth.background: Assam floods almost every monsoon because it sits in the floodplain of the **Brahmaputra** and its tributaries, one of the world's most flood-prone river systems, fed by heavy rain both locally and upstream in the Himalayas. This year's flooding began in early August 2026 and the death toll passed the symbolic **100 mark on August 10**, driven by a mix of river overflow, embankment breaches and landslide-triggered flash floods in low-lying districts like **Golaghat, Nagaon and Sivasagar**. Assam's government, led by Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, activates a standard playbook every year — relief camps, boat evacuations and central disaster funds — but chronic under-investment in embankments means the damage repeats with only the scale varying.

stories.title: Sunrisers Leeds grind past Southern Brave to reach the Hundred women's final
stories.what_happened: Defending champions **Sunrisers Leeds** beat **Southern Brave** by **five wickets** in the Hundred women's Eliminator at the Kennington Oval, chasing down Southern Brave's **114 for 7** with **116 for 5** and 11 balls to spare. **Hannah Baker** took **2 wickets for 13 runs** off her 20 balls and was named Player of the Match for a tight bowling spell that kept the target low. In the chase, **Lauren Winfield-Hill** made **37**, and **Deepti Sharma** anchored the finish with an unbeaten **28** to see Sunrisers home. The win sends Sunrisers Leeds into **Sunday's final** at Lord's, where they will defend the title they won last year. It comes after Sunrisers had already needed a separate win over Manchester Super Giants to even reach this Eliminator, in a tense finish to the group stage this week.
key_points: **Sunrisers Leeds** beat Southern Brave by **five wickets**, chasing 114/7 with **116/5** and 11 balls in hand.
**Hannah Baker** (2/13) was Player of the Match for a disciplined bowling display.
**Deepti Sharma's unbeaten 28** anchored the chase, with Winfield-Hill making 37.
Sunrisers advance to **Sunday's final at Lord's** to defend their Hundred women's title.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's franchise cricket competition, with eight men's and eight women's teams playing a 100-ball format each August. Sunrisers Leeds are the reigning women's champions and needed a nervy group-stage win over Manchester Super Giants earlier this week just to qualify for the knockout stage, before facing Southern Brave in Friday's winner-takes-all Eliminator at the Oval.

stories.title: Colombia's new president asks Trump to bring his deadly anti-cartel military campaign to Colombian soil
stories.what_happened: US Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth** said Colombia's newly inaugurated president had **"requested that the Department of War join Colombia in its fight against narco-terrorism,"** authorizing **joint military operations** against cartels and their networks. Colombia has joined the **Americas Counter-Cartel Coalition** as its 19th member, with the government naming Medellín as a hub for the initiative, which Trump has branded the **"Shield of the Americas."** De la Espriella campaigned on using the air force, army and police to intercept every plane and boat leaving Colombia loaded with drugs. The move marks a sharp reversal from Petro's presidency, when Colombia repeatedly condemned Washington's campaign of **lethal strikes on suspected drug boats** — a campaign human rights groups have criticized for killing suspects without trial.
key_points: New president **Abelardo de la Espriella** has asked Washington to extend its lethal anti-drug campaign into Colombia
Colombia becomes the **19th member** of the US-led Americas Counter-Cartel Coalition
Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth** says Colombia authorized **joint military operations** against cartels
It's the world's **largest cocaine producer**, and the shift ends years of friction under predecessor Gustavo Petro

depth.background: Colombia is the world's largest producer of cocaine, and for decades the US has poured billions of dollars into fighting the drug trade there through aid, training and intelligence-sharing. Under outgoing president **Gustavo Petro**, ties with Washington soured badly: Petro criticized Trump's expanding military strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and Pacific, which have killed dozens of people without judicial process, and Trump at one point warned Petro he would **"be next."** De la Espriella, an outsider who won the presidency campaigning on a **"wrath of God"** crackdown on traffickers, took office pledging full alignment with the US instead.

stories.title: CPL debutants Jamaica Kingsmen slump to a third straight defeat
stories.what_happened: Jamaica Kingsmen lost their third straight CPL 2026 match, falling to the **Barbados Tridents by 5 runs** after being bowled out for **201 for 9** while chasing a target of **207**. It followed a tight **2-wicket opening loss to the Antigua and Barbuda Falcons** (167/7 versus 168/8) and a heavier defeat to the **Guyana Amazon Warriors** at Sabina Park, where the Amazon Warriors won by 6 wickets. With three matches gone, the Kingsmen are now **bottom of the seven-team CPL table** without a single win in their debut season.
key_points: The **Jamaica Kingsmen**, playing their **debut CPL season**, have now lost **all three of their matches**.
They fell to **Barbados Tridents by 5 runs** after being bowled out chasing, managing **201 for 9** against a target of 207.
Their campaign began with a **2-wicket loss to Antigua and Barbuda Falcons** and continued with a loss to **Guyana Amazon Warriors** at Sabina Park.
After three rounds, the Kingsmen sit **last of seven teams** in the CPL 2026 table without a win.
It's a rough start for the Caribbean Premier League's newest franchise, playing in front of home fans at Sabina Park.

depth.background: The **Caribbean Premier League (CPL)** is the Caribbean's top T20 franchise cricket tournament, featuring teams representing different islands and cities. The **Jamaica Kingsmen** are a brand-new franchise entering the competition this season, meaning they're still assembling squad chemistry and experience compared to the six established teams they're competing against. Losing narrowly, as the Kingsmen have in two of their three defeats, often reflects a team that's competitive but not yet closing out tight games — a common growing pain for expansion sides in any franchise league.

stories.title: France's tax authority confirms hackers stole taxpayer data from nearly 700,000 people
stories.what_happened: France's Finance Ministry confirmed late on **Thursday, August 14** that taxpayer data was stolen in a cyberattack. A hacker operating under the name **"ZeroBytes"** claimed on August 12 that they had broken into the DGFiP's systems using **stolen login credentials and a technique to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA)**, and that they'd been inside since **late June**. The ministry says roughly **678,000** taxpayers' data was accessed, though the hacker claims the real number tops **2 million** records. Investigators say the unauthorized access was actually spotted and shut down in late June during routine security checks — but by then, the data had already been taken.
key_points: Hackers stole personal data belonging to around **678,000** French taxpayers, individuals and businesses
A hacker using the alias **'ZeroBytes'** claims the true haul is over **2 million** records
The intruder reportedly used **stolen credentials and an MFA bypass** to get in
The breach was quietly detected and cut off in **late June**, but only confirmed publicly this week

depth.background: France's tax authority, the **General Direction of Public Finances (DGFiP)**, holds sensitive financial data on virtually every taxpayer in the country — incomes, addresses, and bank details tied to tax filings. Government tax agencies are prime targets for cybercriminals precisely because a single breach can expose so much personal financial data at once, useful for identity theft and fraud. Attacks like this have become increasingly common against public-sector databases worldwide.

stories.title: Trump asks the Supreme Court to let construction resume on his $400 million White House ballroom
stories.what_happened: On Friday, August 14, the Trump administration filed an emergency request asking the **Supreme Court** to lift a federal appeals court's injunction and let construction on the White House ballroom continue while the underlying lawsuit plays out. The appeals court's stop-work order is due to take effect on **August 21**, and the administration told the justices the $400 million project is now **'beyond the point of no return,'** arguing that pausing it would cause irreversible harm. Trump has increasingly framed the ballroom as a national-security asset, saying it will include a rooftop **'drone port.'** The case originated with a lawsuit from the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which argues the demolition of the East Wing and the ballroom build violated federal preservation law and bypassed required oversight. The Supreme Court will now decide whether to let building resume immediately or leave the pause in place while the broader legal fight continues.
key_points: The Trump administration asked the **Supreme Court** on Friday to block a lower-court order halting construction of the president's **$400 million White House ballroom**.
A federal appeals court had ordered the project **stopped** just a week earlier, with the injunction set to bite on **August 21**.
The ballroom sits on the site of the old **East Wing**, which Trump had demolished last year **without notifying Congress**.
The administration argues the project is now **'beyond the point of no return'** and calls it a matter of national security because of a planned rooftop **'drone port.'**
The lawsuit was brought by the **National Trust for Historic Preservation**, which says the demolition and build broke federal preservation law.

depth.background: The White House's East Wing — the low-rise building that historically housed the First Lady's offices and the visitor entrance — was torn down in 2025 to make way for a huge new ballroom Trump has wanted since his first term. Because the White House complex is protected under federal historic-preservation rules, major changes normally require review by an independent commission and notice to Congress; preservation groups say none of that happened here. The **National Trust for Historic Preservation**, America's leading heritage-protection nonprofit, sued to stop the project, and a federal appeals court sided with it last week, ordering work paused while the case continues.

stories.title: St Lucia Kings survive a rain-hit chase to edge Antigua & Barbuda Falcons in a low-scoring CPL thriller
stories.what_happened: Put in to bat, the Falcons never got going against tight St Lucia bowling, managing only **98 for 9** in their 19 overs, with Rahkeem Cornwall (26) and Amir Jangoo (23) the only batters to pass 20. Rain then reduced the Kings' chase, leaving them a **DLS target of 52** from a shortened innings — a total that looked routine on paper. Instead, the Kings' batting collapsed under pressure, losing wickets steadily to slip to **54 for 7** in just 7.4 overs before finally reaching the target with two balls to spare. Matthew Forde was the standout performer on both counts, taking **4 wickets for 29 runs** with the ball before returning to hit the winning runs himself, and was named player of the match. Despite the small numbers involved, commentators and fans described it as one of the most tense finishes of the tournament so far.
key_points: Antigua & Barbuda Falcons were bowled out for just **98/9 in 19 overs** at a rain-affected Gros Islet.
Rain cut the Kings' chase target to a revised **DLS target of 52**, but they still slipped to **54/7** before getting over the line.
Player of the match **Matthew Forde** took **4/29** with the ball and then struck the winning runs himself.
The Kings won by **3 wickets with 2 balls to spare**, their **second win over the Falcons in less than a week**.
It is St Lucia's second win in as many completed CPL 2026 matches against these opponents this season.

depth.background: The **Caribbean Premier League (CPL)** is the Caribbean's flagship T20 franchise tournament, running through August and drawing some of the biggest names in white-ball cricket to island grounds across the region. St Lucia Kings and Antigua & Barbuda Falcons had already met once this season, on August 9, when the Kings won a nail-biter by just four runs. This rematch at the Daren Sammy stadium in Gros Islet was interrupted by rain, forcing officials to use the **DLS method** — a mathematical formula used to reset targets fairly when overs are lost to weather.

stories.title: Trump says he will soon 'declare' the Strait of Hormuz a US territory
stories.what_happened: Speaking to a crowd of law enforcement officers at the **Nassau County Police Academy** in New York on **Friday, August 14**, Trump said: 'After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated — pretty soon, I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States.' He added, 'Essentially, that's what it is. We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to.' The remark came as commercial shipping through the Strait remains near a standstill, oil stockpiles are being drawn down internationally, and Iran and Oman are separately negotiating a framework to manage — and eventually reopen — the waterway without US or Israeli vessels. The US has not taken any formal legal or diplomatic step to annex or claim the strait; this was a spoken threat, not policy.
key_points: Trump told police officers at a Nassau County, New York event he'll 'pretty soon' be **declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States**.
He argued the US already runs it in practice: **'We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to.'**
The US has **no legal or historical claim** to the waterway — sovereignty over it is shared by **Iran and Oman**, not Washington.
It escalates a rhetorical fight that began days earlier when Trump claimed the US had **'total control'** of the Strait after tanker attacks and an oil spill.
Iran's government has repeatedly said the Strait remains under its **'complete management and control'**, rejecting any US claim.

depth.background: The **Strait of Hormuz** is the narrow shipping lane between Iran and Oman that roughly **a fifth of the world's oil** passes through on tankers headed from Gulf producers to global markets. Since a US-Iran conflict escalated this summer, Iran has restricted ship traffic and the US Navy has moved to enforce what it calls an **'indefinite' blockade**, while a sanctioned Russian tanker sank nearby and spilled oil. Trump has been building toward this claim for days, first saying the US had 'total control' of the waterway and now going further by threatening to formally call it American territory — something with **no basis in international law**, since the strait runs through Iranian and Omani territorial waters.

thread.previously: We reported that after tanker attacks and a Russian 'shadow fleet' tanker sank and spilled oil, Trump claimed the US had 'total control' of the Strait of Hormuz and might 'keep it', while Iran insisted the waterway remained under its own 'complete management and control'.
thread.changed: Trump went a step further, saying he will soon formally 'declare' the Strait a 'territory of the United States' — an unprecedented claim with no legal basis, since the US has no sovereignty there and Oman and Iran jointly control the waterway.

stories.title: President Murmu unveils sweeping exam reforms after nationwide protests over paper leaks
stories.what_happened: On the eve of India's 80th Independence Day, President **Droupadi Murmu** used her nationally televised address to lay out the government's response to the protests: the **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026**, which took effect on **July 31**. The law sets prison terms of up to **10 years** and fines up to **₹50 lakh** for individuals caught cheating or leaking papers, and penalties up to **₹10 crore** for organized cheating syndicates. Murmu also announced a high-powered task force chaired by **Nandan Nilekani** — the Infosys co-founder known for building India's Aadhaar digital-identity system — to design technology-driven methods that make future exams harder to leak.
key_points: New law imposes up to **10 years in prison** and a **₹50 lakh fine** for individual exam cheats
Organized cheating syndicates face penalties up to **₹10 crore**
A task force chaired by **Nandan Nilekani** will design **leak-proof** exam technology
Reforms followed **Gen Z-led protests** at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak

depth.background: India runs some of the world's largest and highest-stakes competitive exams — **NEET-UG** for medical college admission among them — taken by millions of students each year, often deciding their entire career path. Repeated leaks of exam papers before test day have triggered public fury, since a leak can mean re-tests, delayed results, or an unfair edge for students who paid for stolen questions. A leak in the NEET-UG exam set off nationwide protests, concentrated at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, pressure serious enough that it contributed to the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan** as Union Education Minister.

stories.title: RBI abruptly cuts short its dollar-deposit scheme after banks poured in over $52 billion
stories.what_happened: RBI announced it is closing the deposit-collection window for its FCNR(B) dollar-swap scheme a full month early — moving the deadline from **September 30 to August 31, 2026** — while giving banks until **September 11** to complete the actual swap trades. The central bank cited overwhelming demand: by **August 13**, the broader scheme (which also covers corporate foreign borrowing) had already pulled in a reported **$56.85 billion** in total forex inflows, of which more than **$52 billion** came from the FCNR(B) deposit leg alone. Only the deposit window is being cut short — the separate window for foreign corporate borrowing (ECBs and OFCBs) stays open until **December 31**. The reversal is notable because RBI Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** had said on August 5 there were no plans to close the scheme early, making this a sharper pivot than usual just over a week later.
key_points: RBI moved the deadline for its **FCNR(B) dollar-swap scheme** from **September 30 to August 31**
Banks had already brought in **over $52 billion** through the scheme by August 13
The total swap facility, including corporate borrowing, pulled in nearly **$57 billion**
It echoes a **2013 scheme** RBI used to defend the rupee during that year's market shock
The Governor had said just over a week earlier there were **'no plans'** to end it early

depth.background: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) — the country's central bank — announced this swap scheme on **June 5, 2026**, after the rupee had fallen more than **6%** in the first half of the year amid foreign capital leaving India. Under the scheme, Indian banks could take in fresh dollar deposits from Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) — called FCNR(B), or Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank deposits — and swap those dollars with the RBI at a fixed, favorable exchange rate, making it cheaper for banks to attract and hold foreign currency. It deliberately mirrors a similar scheme RBI ran in **2013** under then-Governor Raghuram Rajan, which helped stabilize the rupee during that year's 'taper tantrum' — a period when global investors pulled money out of emerging markets like India.

stories.title: Maharashtra regulator suspends 14 quick-commerce dark-store licences over food safety violations
stories.what_happened: The Maharashtra FDA carried out a state-wide inspection drive covering **86 quick-commerce facilities** on August 13 and, on **August 14**, suspended the operating licences of **14 of them** — 5 linked to Blinkit, 5 to Zepto, 2 to Instamart, and one each to two smaller operators — citing serious food-safety and hygiene violations. Inspectors found specific breaches including a Blinkit chiller in Malad West running at **6°C**, above safe cold-chain limits; a Zepto facility in Pune's Lohegaon storing products beyond their declared "Use By" dates; and an Instamart site in Andheri keeping food packets directly on the floor with inadequate storage space. Beyond the 14 suspensions, the FDA issued **60 improvement notices** to other facilities and ordered one to stop operations immediately, though it stopped short of permanently cancelling any licence. The inspection checked practices including temperature control, pest control, staff hygiene, and whether facilities followed **FIFO/FEFO** stock rotation.
key_points: Maharashtra's **Food and Drug Administration (FDA)** suspended the licences of **14 dark stores** run by Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a snap inspection drive.
Inspectors covered **86 facilities** across the state; violations ranged from food stored on the floor to products kept **past their "Use By" dates**.
Of the 14 suspended, **5 were Blinkit**, **5 were Zepto**, and **2 were Instamart** outlets, plus two smaller operators.
A Blinkit facility in Mumbai's Malad West had its chiller running at **6°C** — above the safe limit for the perishables it stored.
The FDA also issued **60 improvement notices** and ordered one facility to halt operations immediately, though no licences were permanently cancelled.

depth.background: "Dark stores" are the small, customer-inaccessible warehouses that power India's **10-minute grocery delivery boom** — Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart have built thousands of them in cities to promise near-instant delivery. That speed depends on tight, high-turnover storage of fresh and perishable food, which is exactly where food-safety risk concentrates: a warehouse racing to restock and dispatch orders in minutes has less margin for error on temperature control, expiry tracking and hygiene than a traditional, slower-moving retail store.

stories.title: Chief Justice Surya Kant says his 'cockroach' remark was misquoted and used with 'malicious intent' to mislead youth
stories.what_happened: In a DD News interview aired Thursday, August 14, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed the ongoing controversy over his May 'cockroach' remark directly, saying it was 'misquoted' and that 'what was not said is presented as though it was said' in what he called a 'major malicious attempt to mislead the youth of the country.' He clarified the original comment was aimed specifically at people holding fraudulent educational degrees who use activism as cover, not at India's youth in general. The remark had already triggered significant public backlash, including the emergence of the satirical 'Cockroach Janta Party' movement, which grew to roughly three million followers within days. The CJI also used the interview to call for a formal protocol around how courts' informal oral observations are reported by the media, arguing the current lack of context in reporting can distort what judges actually mean.
key_points: **CJI Surya Kant** told DD News his May courtroom remark comparing certain people to 'cockroaches' was **misquoted** and taken out of context.
The original remark, made **May 15**, targeted holders of **fraudulent degrees** who allegedly pose as activists — not youth broadly, he said.
He called the spread of the clip a **'major malicious attempt'** to mislead the country's young people.
The remark had already sparked a satirical online movement, the **'Cockroach Janta Party,'** which gained **3 million followers within 78 hours**.
The CJI also called for a **protocol on reporting oral court observations**, which are often informal and not part of a final ruling.

depth.background: In India, judges frequently make informal spoken remarks during court hearings — called **'oral observations'** — that are distinct from a court's final written judgment but are often reported by media and go viral on social media, sometimes stripped of context. On May 15, Chief Justice of India **Surya Kant**, the country's top judge, made a courtroom comment comparing people who hold fraudulent degrees and pose as social-media or RTI (Right to Information) activists to 'cockroaches.' Clips of the remark spread rapidly online, and a satirical protest movement calling itself the 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP) emerged, reportedly gaining three million Instagram followers within 78 hours, widely read as a youth-led backlash against the remark.

stories.title: Ben Stokes publicly questions England's snub of his own vice-captain
stories.what_happened: Speaking publicly for the first time since retiring, Stokes joined former teammates **Stuart Broad and Jos Buttler** on their podcast and directly challenged the ECB's decision to bypass Brook. He pointed out Brook had already been made **vice-captain** and led the side when Stokes himself was dropped for one Test after a nightclub curfew breach, yet still wasn't given the job: "He's vice-captain, and the captain is not playing, but he's not captain... what message is that sending to him?" Stokes drew a direct comparison to his own start as captain, noting he **"had no leadership or captaincy experience"** when England gave him the role in 2022. Rob Key defended the call, saying the Test captaincy is **"a huge amount to put on his plate"** given Brook already juggles all three formats, and that Brook's disciplinary record was **"not the main reason"** but was a factor. Stokes did also back Root, saying **"I wish him nothing but success"** and that his real worry was the toll the job would take on Root personally. Brook himself has stayed diplomatic, telling ESPNcricinfo just days ago that captaincy is **"blood hard"** while sidestepping questions about being overlooked.
key_points: Stokes retired from international cricket in **June 2026** after **4 years** as England Test captain
England handed the Test captaincy to **35-year-old Joe Root**, not Stokes' own vice-captain **Harry Brook**
Director of cricket **Rob Key** called it **'too soon'** for Brook to take over
Stokes, on the **For The Love of Cricket podcast**, said: 'If you think someone is going to be a good captain... just give it to them'
England open a **3-Test series vs Pakistan on August 19** at Headingley under Root, with Fleming as incoming coach

depth.background: **Ben Stokes** captained England's Test side for four years, reshaping the team around aggressive '**Bazball**' cricket alongside coach Brendon McCullum. He shocked the sport by announcing his retirement from all international cricket **mid-Test at Trent Bridge in June 2026**, citing accumulated **physical and mental exhaustion**. His vice-captain, **Harry Brook**, already captains England's white-ball (limited-overs) sides and was widely seen as the natural Test successor. Instead the ECB (England's cricket board) recalled **Joe Root**, who had previously captained England from 2017-2022, for a second stint, while **Stephen Fleming** was named the new permanent Test head coach on a **four-year deal to 2030**, starting officially on the tour of South Africa in December.

stories.title: Big Tech's AI spending commitments near $1.5 trillion — and the debt behind them is getting harder to track
stories.what_happened: A Financial Times analysis published this week found that Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, Oracle and Meta have amassed close to **$1.5 trillion** in purchase commitments tied to computing infrastructure, chips, data-center capacity and energy. Separately, Goldman Sachs estimates hyperscalers' combined lease commitments for data centers, offices and equipment have hit **$1.5 trillion**, up from roughly $200 billion five years ago. The four biggest spenders — Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta — plan to spend about **$745 billion** in 2026 alone, with Alphabet's capex reaching up to $205 billion and Meta's up to $145 billion. CNBC reported this week that a growing share of this build-out is financed through debt and off-balance-sheet structures, which makes it harder for outside investors to see exactly how leveraged the AI boom has become.
key_points: Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, Oracle and Meta have combined **~$1.5 trillion** in AI-related purchase commitments, a Financial Times analysis found.
Hyperscaler **lease commitments** for data centers have rocketed to **$1.5 trillion**, up from about **$200 billion** just five years ago.
The biggest spenders plan roughly **$745 billion** in AI capital spending in 2026 alone, including Amazon's **$220 billion**.
More of this spending is now funded through **debt and off-balance-sheet vehicles**, making the real risk harder for investors to see.
Citigroup has raised its 2029 AI infrastructure forecast to **$2.8 trillion**, up from $2.3 trillion.

depth.background: Since ChatGPT's 2023 breakthrough, the biggest technology companies have been racing to build the computing power — chips, data centers, electricity — needed to train and run AI models, on the belief that whoever has the most compute wins the AI race. That spending has already topped **$1.1 trillion since 2023**. Increasingly, though, companies are not paying for all of this out of their own cash reserves; they are leasing capacity, signing multi-year purchase contracts, and using **special-purpose financing vehicles** that don't always show up cleanly on a company's main balance sheet.

stories.title: Poland says it thwarted a Russian plot to assassinate a Ukrainian-American in Warsaw
stories.what_happened: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced Thursday that the Internal Security Agency (ABW) and police arrested a Russian man on August 7 who had been recruited by Russian services to kill a Ukrainian-American — someone Tusk described as "inconvenient to the Putin regime." Tusk said authorities intervened "at the last minute" to stop what he called a planned "execution." He stressed this was carried out in cooperation with U.S. intelligence services and represents the first documented instance of Russia ordering an attack on a U.S. citizen inside another NATO member state. The suspect has been remanded into three months of pretrial detention while the investigation continues. Polish officials tied the plot to the broader pattern of Kremlin-directed sabotage and killings across Europe, including DHL parcel-bomb test runs and the November 2025 railway bombing.
key_points: Polish security services arrested a **Russian national** in Warsaw on **August 7** who had allegedly been recruited by Russian intelligence to kill a man holding both **Ukrainian and US citizenship**.
Prime Minister **Donald Tusk** called it the **first known case** of Russia ordering the killing of an American citizen on the soil of another **NATO** country.
The operation to stop the plot was run jointly with **U.S. services**, and the suspect will be held in pretrial custody for **three months**.

It follows a **June 2026** assassination of Putin critic Semyon Skrepetsky (real name Robert Kuzovkov) in eastern Poland, and a **November 2025** railway bombing Warsaw blamed on Russian intelligence.
Western officials say Moscow has run dozens of parcel-bomb, arson and sabotage plots across Europe since the **2022 invasion of Ukraine** — this is the first to target a US passport-holder directly.

depth.background: Since Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, European security agencies have accused Russian military intelligence (the GRU) and the FSB of running a low-level campaign of sabotage across NATO countries — railway bombings, warehouse arson, and parcel bombs sent through courier networks like DHL. Poland, as Ukraine's key logistics and military-aid corridor and a NATO/EU border state, has been hit hardest, including a **November 2025** rail bombing and the assassination of a Russian dissident cartoonist in Poland this past **June**. Until now, these plots have targeted Ukrainian exiles, dissidents, and infrastructure — not American citizens directly.

stories.title: Pakistan slip to 261 behind on day two of their final Test warm-up before the England series
stories.what_happened: On day two of their three-day warm-up match at Beckenham, Pakistan's top order struggled to make inroads, with the side closing the day trailing by **261 runs** after the PCC Select XI's first-innings total of **305**. Openers **Imam-ul-Haq (26 not out)** and **Azan Awais (15 not out)** were still at the crease at the close of play, having avoided losing a wicket so far in Pakistan's reply. On day one, Pakistan's bowlers — sharing six wickets between them — had restricted the PCC Select XI to 305 all out. With the match reduced to three days because of player availability, day three (August 15) is Pakistan's last chance to build some batting form and rhythm before the series opener.
key_points: Pakistan closed day two trailing by **261 runs** in their three-day warm-up match at Beckenham.
Openers **Imam-ul-Haq (26*) and Azan Awais (15*)** were unbeaten at the close.
The match is Pakistan's **last hit-out** before the first Test at **Headingley on August 19**.
The fixture was **shortened from four days to three** due to player availability.
Pakistan had bowled the **PCC Select XI** out for **305** on day one.

depth.background: Before a Test series, touring teams typically play one or more 'warm-up' matches against a mix of county and invitational players to get used to English conditions — the pitch, the weather, and the swinging ball — before the real series begins. Pakistan are preparing for a three-match Test series against England that starts **August 19 at Headingley in Leeds**, their first assignment under a series that also marks a fresh start for England, who are being led by a returning captain, Joe Root, this series. This particular warm-up fixture, against a **Professional County Club (PCC) Select XI** at Beckenham, was trimmed from four days to three because of player availability.

stories.title: Lightning McQueen is joining the F1 grid — Disney and Formula 1 extend their partnership through 2028
stories.what_happened: F1 confirmed that **Lightning McQueen** will appear at the **Italian Grand Prix weekend at Monza** with a special commemorative livery marking **20 years** since *Cars* first released. The appearance is part of an extended **Disney-F1 partnership through 2028**, expanding the existing "Fuel the Magic" collaboration to include Pixar's Cars characters for the first time. The first wave of merchandise — a hat, fleece, and Mattel die-cast model cars — was unveiled at Disney's **D23 fan expo** and went on sale online on **August 14**, with the full collection launching globally on **August 27** and also available at F1's Monza flagship store during the Italian Grand Prix.
key_points: **Lightning McQueen**, Pixar's animated race car from *Cars*, will make its **F1 debut** at the **Italian Grand Prix at Monza**
The appearance marks **20 years** since the original *Cars* movie was released
Formula 1 and Disney are extending their **"Fuel the Magic"** partnership through **2028**
It's the first time the collaboration expands beyond classic Disney characters like Mickey Mouse into Pixar's **Cars** franchise
The first six products — including a hat, fleece and **Mattel die-cast models** — launch online **August 14**, with a wider release **August 27**

depth.background: F1 and Disney have run a licensed merchandise and promotional tie-up called **"Fuel the Magic"** for a while, mostly built around classic Disney characters. This is the first time it's expanding into Pixar's **Cars** franchise, whose main character, Lightning McQueen, is himself a fictional racecar — making the crossover a natural fit. The tie-up lands as F1 continues to lean into entertainment and lifestyle branding to grow its audience beyond traditional racing fans, particularly in markets like the US where Disney's reach is enormous.

stories.title: A bipartisan US House delegation secretly visited the Vatican to discuss AI with Pope Leo XIV
stories.what_happened: According to reporting first published by Politico, a bipartisan delegation of nine US House members traveled to the Vatican for a previously unreported meeting focused on artificial intelligence, organized by the House committee that handles strategic rivalry with China. Pope Leo XIV joined the conversation for part of the visit. Discussions covered religious freedom, the geopolitical risks AI poses as major powers race to develop it, and its ethical implications for humanity — themes the Pope has already raised publicly since taking office. The trip had not been disclosed publicly before the report, an unusual level of discretion for a congressional delegation.
key_points: **Nine members of Congress** from both parties made a previously unreported trip to the **Vatican** to discuss artificial intelligence.
The trip was organized by a House committee focused on **strategic competition with China**.
**Pope Leo XIV** joined the discussion briefly, after publishing his first encyclical on AI and human dignity in May.
Talks covered **religious freedom**, the **geopolitical risks of AI**, and its **ethical implications** for humanity.
The visit shows the Vatican positioning itself as a moral voice in the global AI debate, alongside governments and tech firms.

depth.background: Pope Leo XIV, elected in 2025, has made artificial intelligence a defining early theme of his papacy — setting up a Vatican commission on AI and publishing an encyclical, **'Magnifica Humanitas,'** in May 2026 that warned about AI's risks to human dignity. Separately, the US Congress has increasingly framed AI development as a front in **strategic competition with China**, with export controls on advanced chips and growing concern about who sets the global rules for the technology. Congressional delegations to foreign capitals and international bodies are a normal, if usually publicized, part of US diplomacy.

stories.title: Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out of Asia Cup and Asian Games with severe hamstring tear
stories.what_happened: Rodrigues felt her hamstring go while batting for Southern Brave in The Hundred on August 3 and was withdrawn from the rest of that tournament immediately, with Australian all-rounder Charlie Knott brought in as her club replacement. She flew back to India for assessment at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, where scans confirmed a high-grade tear — serious enough that the medical team ruled out any chance of recovery in time for either the Asia Cup or the Asian Games. The BCCI announced her withdrawal from both tournaments on August 14. Selectors moved quickly, naming Pratika Rawal — herself recently recovered from a prior injury setback at the 2025 World Cup — as the direct replacement in the 15-player Asia Cup squad announced alongside her. The rest of India's squad remains largely settled around Harmanpreet Kaur (captain), Smriti Mandhana (vice-captain), Deepti Sharma, and Richa Ghosh.
key_points: India batter **Jemimah Rodrigues** has been ruled out of the **Women's Asia Cup** (starts August 28, Dubai) and the **Asian Games** (Aichi-Nagoya, Sept 17–Oct 3) after a **high-grade hamstring tear**.
She got hurt on **August 3** while playing for **Southern Brave** in England's Hundred tournament, and was scanned by the **BCCI medical team** at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
Before the injury she had scored **143 runs in six Hundred innings** at an average of 35.75.
**Pratika Rawal** has been named her replacement in India's Asia Cup squad, batting alongside captain **Harmanpreet Kaur**.
India will defend the women's cricket gold they won at the **2023 Asian Games** without one of their most explosive middle-order batters.

depth.background: Jemimah Rodrigues is one of India's most important middle-order batters in white-ball cricket, known for her fielding as much as her stroke play, and has been a fixture in India's T20 and ODI sides for several years. India women are defending champions in Asian Games cricket and are among the favourites for the T20 Asia Cup, which doubles as a key form guide before the 2027 T20 World Cup cycle. Hamstring tears are graded by severity (low to high), and a 'high-grade' tear typically means weeks, not days, of recovery — closer to a season-ending than a match-missing injury. She picked up the injury playing in **The Hundred**, England's short-form franchise league that many international players use for extra match practice and pay outside their national board's control.

stories.title: Bangladesh claws back to 175 for 2 on day two in Darwin, trailing Australia by just 23 runs
stories.what_happened: On day one, Bangladesh's bowlers bundled Australia out for just 198, with fast bowler Hasan Mahmud claiming a career-best 6 for 55, and the tourists closed the day at 96 for 1 in reply. On day two, Bangladesh continued building on that platform, reaching 175 for 2 after 50 overs with Mominul Haque unbeaten on 35 and Tanzid Hasan unbeaten on 32, cutting the deficit to Australia's total to just 23 runs. During Australia's innings, veteran fast bowler Mitchell Starc passed Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath to become the most successful left-arm bowler in Test cricket history.
key_points: Bangladesh reached **175/2** after 50 overs on day two, having bowled Australia out for **198** in their first innings
**Mominul Haque (35 not out)** and **Tanzid Hasan (32 not out)** are steering a fightback that has trimmed the deficit to just **23 runs**
The platform follows **Hasan Mahmud's career-best 6 for 55**, which skittled Australia's first innings on day one
This is Bangladesh's **first-ever Test tour of Australia**, ending a 23-year wait for a red-ball series Down Under
Australia's **Mitchell Starc** became Test cricket's most successful left-arm bowler during the innings, passing Rangana Herath

depth.background: Bangladesh's tour of Australia is historic in itself — this is the first time the team has played a Test series in Australia, 23 years after first joining the small group of nations with Test status. The match is being played in Darwin, a venue known for hot, humid conditions that can behave differently to Australia's more familiar southern grounds. Bangladesh went into day one as heavy underdogs against an Australian side that includes veteran fast bowler Mitchell Starc, one of the most successful bowlers in the format's history.

thread.previously: At stumps on day one, Bangladesh had reached 96 for 1 in reply after bowling Australia out for 198, trailing by 102 runs.
thread.changed: Bangladesh have extended their reply to 175 for 2 after 50 overs on day two, cutting the deficit to just 23 runs behind Australia's total.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty claw back most of the day's losses to close only slightly lower
stories.what_happened: India's benchmark indices opened weak and slid further at midday on **Friday, August 14**, as fears about a potential **US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz** pushed crude oil prices higher. By the close, the **BSE Sensex** had recovered most of its losses to end down just **71 points (0.09%) at 78,009.25**, while the **Nifty 50** settled **0.12% lower at 24,366**, helped by **softer-than-expected US inflation data** and broadly positive global cues. The **Bank Nifty** fell a sharper **144 points (0.25%)** to close at **57,491**. Selling was concentrated in **auto, energy, FMCG, metal, pharma and realty** stocks, while **consumer durables and media** shares bucked the trend and gained. Broader markets underperformed the benchmarks, with the **Nifty Midcap 100 down 0.53%** and the **Nifty Smallcap 100 down 0.69%**.
key_points: The **Sensex fell just 71 points (-0.09%)** to close at **78,009**, recovering from a much steeper drop earlier in the day.
The **Nifty 50 dropped 0.12%** to settle at **24,366**.
Markets had sunk further at midday on fears of a **US naval blockade at the Strait of Hormuz**, a key oil chokepoint.
**Softer US inflation data** and positive global cues helped indices recover off their intraday lows.
**Auto, energy, FMCG, metal, pharma and realty** stocks dragged, while **consumer durables and media** shares gained.

depth.background: Indian markets had a rough start on Friday, sliding further at midday as fears grew that the **US might blockade the Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through — amid elevated US-Iran tension. A blockade there would squeeze global oil supply and push up prices, which matters enormously for **India**, one of the world's largest oil importers, because costlier crude widens India's trade deficit and adds to inflation. By the close, though, markets had pared back most of that morning loss.

thread.previously: Sensex and Nifty had slipped at midday on Friday as oil prices firmed on fears of a US naval blockade at the Strait of Hormuz.
thread.changed: By the close, markets had recovered most of that loss — the Sensex ended down just 71 points and the Nifty 0.12% lower — helped by softer US inflation data, even as auto, metal, and energy stocks stayed under pressure.

stories.title: The rupee edges up as oil prices ease, while RBI proposes tying more loan rates directly to its repo rate
stories.what_happened: On Friday, the rupee held around **₹95.67 to the US dollar**, edging higher as Brent crude fell more than 2% on Thursday to roughly **$86.50 a barrel** — a relief for India's oil-import bill even as the US threatened to maintain an **indefinite naval blockade** of Iranian ports. The rupee has still lost **9.32% of its value over the past 12 months**, though it has recovered about 0.67% over the past month. Traders said persistent dollar demand from importers, plus maturing forward contracts, kept weighing on the currency, while the RBI's **near-daily intervention** helped prevent a sharper fall. Separately, the RBI floated a new draft framework that would require **floating-rate personal and MSME (small business) loans** to be linked to external benchmarks such as its repo rate, a change intended to make rate changes pass through to borrowers faster and more transparently — though it would only take effect from **April 2027** if finalized.
key_points: The **rupee** traded around **₹95.67/$1** on Friday, helped by a pullback in crude oil prices.
**Brent crude** fell over **2%** to around **$86.50 a barrel**, easing import-cost pressure on India.
The **RBI has been intervening near-daily** in currency markets to cushion the rupee's slide.
The rupee is still down **9.3% over the past 12 months**, despite a modest 0.7% bounce this month.
RBI's new draft rule would link **floating-rate personal and MSME loans** directly to its repo rate from **April 2027**.

depth.background: The Indian rupee has weakened steadily over the past year, squeezed by a strong US dollar, persistent demand for dollars from Indian importers, and — this year in particular — elevated global oil prices driven by the **Iran war and Strait of Hormuz crisis** (India imports over 80% of its crude). The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) doesn't let the rupee float completely freely; it periodically sells dollars from its reserves to slow sharp declines, a practice called intervention. Separately, RBI has long pushed lenders to price loans more transparently by linking them to a clear external benchmark (like its own repo rate) instead of banks' own internal, harder-to-track formulas.

stories.title: Audi opens the door to Carlos Sainz for 2027 as his Williams future comes into doubt
stories.what_happened: In an exclusive interview during the F1 summer break, Audi team principal Mattia Binotto said it was **'flattering'** that Sainz has been linked with Audi for 2027, adding that outside interest shows people **'perceive that our project has a clear ambition and is going in the right direction.'** Separately, reports emerged that Audi's camp had discussed with Nico Hulkenberg's side whether he would step aside — reportedly even discussing a **financial arrangement** — to free up a seat for Sainz, but those talks did not progress. Hulkenberg addressed the rumours directly at Spa-Francorchamps, joking that **'the reserve driver's seat is available'** and calling it **'typical summer F1 noise.'** Audi has indicated its 2027 line-up is still expected to be Hulkenberg and Bortoleto, leaving Sainz's path forward unclear as the summer break winds down.
key_points: Audi F1 boss Mattia Binotto said Sainz's interest proves the team's project is **'going in the right direction'**
Sainz's Williams contract runs out at the **end of 2026**, and a tough season has fuelled exit speculation
Reports say Audi explored **paying Nico Hulkenberg** to give up his seat for Sainz, but the talks reportedly stalled
Hulkenberg brushed off the rumours, joking only the **'reserve driver's seat'** is available
Audi is still expected to **keep Hulkenberg and rookie Gabriel Bortoleto** for 2027, leaving Sainz's next move open

depth.background: Carlos Sainz once turned down a seat at Sauber (Audi's F1 project before it became a full manufacturer team) to join Williams for 2025 instead. That switch has not gone to plan — Williams has struggled through the 2026 season, and Sainz's contract with the team expires at the end of the year. Audi, meanwhile, has stepped up from being just an engine supplier to owning a full **'works' team** (one directly run by the car manufacturer, not just a customer), with Nico Hulkenberg and rookie Gabriel Bortoleto as its 2026 line-up. Both of those drivers are believed to already be on longer-term deals, which complicates any Sainz move.

stories.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal charges in UnitedHealthcare CEO's killing
stories.what_happened: On Friday, August 14, Mangione entered an **"open plea"** in a Manhattan federal courtroom, pleading guilty to two counts — **interstate stalking resulting in death** and **stalking through use of interstate facilities resulting in death** — each carrying a possible life sentence. He pleaded guilty without any plea agreement or sentencing concessions, meaning prosecutors remain free to seek the toughest possible punishment. In court, Mangione admitted he trailed Thompson to an investor conference in December 2024 and shot him on a New York City street, and said he had contacted UnitedHealthcare in advance under the guise of being an investor to learn Thompson's schedule. He told the judge: "I knew what I was doing was illegal." Judge Garnett scheduled **sentencing for December 18**; federal guidelines point to a **24-to-30-year range**, but prosecutors remain free to push for life. Immediately after, Mangione's defense team filed a motion to **dismiss his upcoming state trial** in New York, arguing double-jeopardy protections should block a second prosecution over the same conduct.
key_points: Mangione pleaded guilty to **two federal counts of stalking resulting in death**, each carrying up to life in prison.
It was an **"open plea"** — no deal, no promises from prosecutors, who remain free to seek the **maximum sentence**.
He told the judge: **"I knew what I was doing was illegal."**
**Sentencing is set for December 18**; guidelines suggest **24 to 30 years**, but prosecutors can ask for life.
His lawyers immediately moved to **dismiss his separate New York state murder trial**, citing double jeopardy.

depth.background: Mangione, 27, was arrested in December 2024 after **UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson was shot and killed** on a New York City street, an attack that turned him into a folk-hero figure for many Americans angry at the health insurance industry. He faced two parallel prosecutions — a federal case in Manhattan over stalking and firearms charges, and a separate New York state case charging him with **murder and terrorism**. Friday's guilty plea resolves only the federal side. Prosecutors say Mangione tracked Thompson for months, including by posing as an investor to learn his schedule, before the shooting outside a Manhattan hotel.

stories.title: Delhi Capitals wicketkeeper Abishek Porel denied bail, sent to 14-day judicial custody in a rape case
stories.what_happened: A court in Chinsurah, West Bengal denied bail to cricketer Abishek Porel on August 14 and ordered him held in 14 days of judicial custody. Porel was arrested on August 11 by police in Mogra, West Bengal, acting on a specific directive from the Calcutta High Court, over allegations brought by a third-year medical student studying in Karnataka. The complainant's original complaint, filed June 23 at Mogra Police Station, alleges she was in a relationship with Porel for over three years based on his assurances of marriage, which she says he later retracted; the case involves accusations of rape, physical assault, and criminal intimidation. The Calcutta High Court has set its next hearing in the matter for September 14, 2026. Porel has not been convicted of any offense, and the legal process is ongoing.
key_points: A court in **Chinsurah, West Bengal** denied bail to IPL wicketkeeper **Abishek Porel** and remanded him to **14 days of judicial custody**.
Porel, who plays for the **Delhi Capitals** and Bengal in domestic cricket, was arrested on **August 11** by Mogra police.
The case stems from a complaint filed **June 23** by a **medical student**, alleging a three-year relationship based on a **false promise of marriage**.
The arrest followed a specific directive from the **Calcutta High Court**, which has scheduled its next hearing for **September 14**.
The allegations include rape, physical assault, and criminal intimidation; Porel has not been convicted and the case is ongoing.

depth.background: Under Indian law, a criminal case alleging rape 'on the false promise of marriage' arises when a complainant says sexual relations occurred because a partner promised marriage and later reneged — a distinct and often legally contested category of case in Indian courts. Porel, a left-handed wicketkeeper-batter, plays for the **Delhi Capitals** in the IPL and represents **Bengal** in India's domestic first-class cricket, making him a recognizable name among Indian cricket followers rather than an international star.

stories.title: Verstappen expected to confirm he's staying at Red Bull through 2028 at the Dutch GP
stories.what_happened: Speaking on the Pit Talk podcast from the Zandvoort race weekend, Doornbos said he expects Verstappen to publicly settle his future at his home race, arguing that neither McLaren nor Mercedes have room or interest in signing him, leaving Red Bull as effectively his only real option. Verstappen has yet to make any official statement himself.
key_points: Former F1 driver **Robert Doornbos** expects Verstappen to confirm his **Red Bull future** at his home race, the **Dutch Grand Prix** (Aug 21-23).
Verstappen is contracted to Red Bull through **2028** but holds an **exit clause** he could activate to leave early.
Doornbos says a McLaren or Mercedes switch is **"off the table"** — in his view, Verstappen "has to stay with Red Bull."
Verstappen sits **sixth** in the standings at the season's halfway point, without a win, trailing leader Kimi Antonelli by **110 points**.

depth.background: Red Bull's underwhelming form through 2026 fuelled months of speculation about whether Verstappen — a four-time champion — might use his contract's exit clause to leave for a faster car elsewhere. Reports had suggested Red Bull was even willing to remove the exit clause entirely to secure his commitment. This year's Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, Verstappen's home race, is also the last one on the calendar after organisers chose not to renew beyond 2026.

thread.previously: We reported Verstappen's exit clause had become active and that Red Bull's contract offers to him kept changing.
thread.changed: A well-connected Dutch pundit now expects Verstappen to publicly confirm he's staying at Red Bull through 2028 during his home race at Zandvoort.

stories.title: Bangladesh push Australia to the brink in Darwin as Starc and Miraz clash on a tense day two
stories.what_happened: On day two of the first Test in Darwin, Bangladesh took firm control, with opener **Tanzid Hasan Tamim** producing a history-making innings that made batting look straightforward against the Australian attack for most of the day. By stumps, **Australia trailed by 153 runs**, having lost three wickets in the final session — and it would have been four had **Cameron Green** not put down a catch on the last ball of the day. Tensions boiled over during the day when **Mitchell Starc** accused Bangladesh's **Mehidy Miraz** of deliberately blocking his follow-through path, with the two exchanging words on the field after a long, hard session for the home bowlers.
key_points: Australia trail Bangladesh by **153 runs** at stumps on day two in Darwin.
**Tanzid Hasan Tamim's** history-making innings anchored Bangladesh's dominant day.
**Mitchell Starc** and **Mehidy Miraz** exchanged words after Starc accused Miraz of blocking his follow-through.
Australia lost **three wickets** in the final session — a fourth chance went down when Cameron Green dropped a catch.
It is a rare position of real control for Bangladesh in a Test match on Australian soil.

depth.background: Bangladesh have historically struggled badly on tours of Australia, where fast, bouncy pitches have traditionally favoured the host attack. Darwin, hosting this Test, is a newer and less familiar venue on the international circuit, adding an extra layer of unpredictability. Openers like Tanzid Hasan Tamim have been central to a slow but real improvement in Bangladesh's Test batting depth in recent years, even as results away from home remained difficult.

stories.title: Fighting flares again in Yemen's Taiz as Houthi forces clash with government troops
stories.what_happened: Yemen's government-aligned National Resistance Forces, led by Tareq Saleh (a member of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council), said their strikes killed **more than 27 Houthi fighters** and injured **19 others** over three days of fighting on the Al-Barh front in southwestern Taiz province, reported August 14. Several Houthi military vehicles were destroyed or disabled, according to the government side's account. This escalation follows an early-August wave of Houthi missile and drone attacks that Yemeni officials said killed roughly **30 soldiers** and wounded **15** in the Hadramout and Marib provinces. Fighting has since resumed in several fronts, including **Marib, Al-Jawf, Al-Dhalea** and **Taiz**, marking the most significant ground escalation in years.
key_points: **Over 27 Houthi fighters killed** and **19 injured** in three days of clashes on Taiz's Al-Barh front.
Government-aligned **National Resistance Forces**, led by Tareq Saleh, say they repelled the attacks.
The flare-up follows Houthi missile and drone strikes early this month that killed **~30 soldiers** elsewhere in Yemen.
Fighting has now spread to **Marib, Al-Jawf, Al-Dhalea and Taiz** after years of relative calm.

depth.background: Yemen's civil war has run since 2014, pitting the Iran-aligned **Houthi movement**, which controls the capital Sanaa and much of the north, against Yemen's internationally recognized government and allied forces in the south, backed at times by Saudi Arabia and the UAE. A fragile, years-long lull in major ground fighting had mostly held even as the Houthis separately fired at Israel and Red Sea shipping during the Gaza war. That lull is now cracking: fresh Houthi missile and drone attacks in early August killed dozens of government soldiers, and fighting has since spread across multiple provinces.

stories.title: Cadillac's owner shuts down Perez-to-Williams talk, says he'll be racing for them in 2027
stories.what_happened: Amid swirling rumors that **Sergio Perez** could leave Cadillac for **Williams**, team owner and CEO **Dan Towriss** issued a firm on-record denial: **"I'm confident that Checo is going to remain with Cadillac, and we're not distracted by the Williams rumours for a second. We're very confident in the relationship here, and that you're going to see him piloting the Cadillac F1 car [in 2027]."** The statement came just days after Cadillac abruptly fired team principal Graeme Lowdon and installed **Marcin Budkowski**, formerly of Alpine, in his place — a leadership shake-up that had fueled speculation about wider instability at the rookie team, Perez's future included. Despite Cadillac not yet scoring a point this season due to a lack of competitive machinery, Perez has out-qualified teammate **Valtteri Bottas 9 times to 5**, a data point Towriss and the team point to as evidence he remains worth keeping.
key_points: Cadillac co-owner and CEO **Dan Towriss** said he's **"confident"** Sergio Perez stays with the team, dismissing Williams rumors.
Towriss said fans will see **Perez piloting the Cadillac car in 2027**.
The comments follow days of speculation Perez could jump to **Williams**, where **Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz's** seats are both uncertain.
Perez currently **leads teammate Valtteri Bottas 9-5** in their qualifying head-to-head this season.
New team principal **Marcin Budkowski**, installed after Cadillac fired **Graeme Lowdon**, has also backed Perez's future.

depth.background: **Cadillac** is Formula 1's newest team, debuting in 2026 with **Sergio "Checo" Perez** and **Valtteri Bottas** as its two drivers — both experienced former race-winners brought in to anchor a brand-new outfit. The team has struggled in its rookie season and has yet to score a championship point, and this week it fired team principal **Graeme Lowdon**, replacing him with **Marcin Budkowski**, a former Alpine executive. Against that turbulent backdrop, rumors began circulating that Perez could switch to **Williams** instead, a team whose own driver lineup is unsettled heading into 2027.

thread.previously: Cadillac had already begun moving to shut down rumors that Sergio Perez could leave for Williams, in a story that centered mainly on a separate Verstappen comment about Fernando Alonso.
thread.changed: Cadillac's own team owner, Dan Towriss, went further today with an explicit, on-record commitment that Perez will still be racing for Cadillac in 2027.
